## BOOK TWO

...on the other side beyond the equator. **Northerners** <note>original: *Aquilonares*; those living toward the North Wind</note> prevail in physical strength and ferocity, because the cold does not allow their internal heat to escape sufficiently. **Southerners** <note>original: *Australes*; those living toward the South Wind</note>, who possess much internal heat but a thin and <term>smoky spirit</term> <note>original: *spiritus fuliginosus*; in old medicine, this refers to the "sooty" vapors produced by the body's internal heat that needed to be exhaled</note>, prevail in cunning; they are weak in body and suited for slavery and lust. Those in the **middle regions** excel in both talent and body; they are suited for the governance of a republic and are tenacious of their liberty, just as Northerners are prone to license and Southerners to servitude.

3 We say, moreover, that those **Northerners** who live beyond the Arctic Circle, and those **Southerners** who live a little before or a little beyond the tropics, are **Saturnine** <note>influenced by the planet Saturn, traditionally associated with cold, slowness, and melancholy</note> in their customs and strength. For just as those who inhabit the <term>equinoctial region</term> <note>the area around the equator</note> have the extreme tropical signs dedicated to **Saturn**—because those signs represent the furthest reaches for them—so too those who hold the middle climates will assign the extremes to Saturn, the most remote of the planets. However, this occurs for different reasons: the former due to excessive cold, the latter due to excessive dryness. Consequently, those placed outside of a temperate climate are monstrous, as if falling away from human nature. **Pygmies** in the North are crude in talent and miserable in food and clothing; they are "blackish" because their heat is extinguished by excessive cold—this is why, in winter, even our own hands turn black. For once you pass the fair-skinned **Germans** and **Poles**, you come to the reddish **Norwegians**, then to "greenish" men, and finally to those who are blackish and small. Similarly, those who live under the tropics are black for a different reason, namely because their white color is "drawn out" by the Sun. They are dull in talent, not because of unpurged "excremental filth" <note>referring to a buildup of bodily fluids or "humors" caused by cold</note> like the Arctic peoples, but because of foul "smokes" and thin spirits. They are wild <unclear>men</unclear>, so much so that some are said to be **satyrs** there, according to the testimony of **St. Jerome**, and <unclear>dog-headed</unclear> <note>original: *Cynocephali*; a mythical race of men with dog heads</note> if you believe **Pliny**. There are others who are scarcely believed to be humans of our own race. Astrologers attribute these deformities to the "intemperance" <note>lack of balance</note> of Saturn.

4 In the center of the equator, **Jupiter** dominates. Although **St. Thomas Aquinas**, believing **Aristotle**, thought that zone was uninhabitable, we know otherwise. Along with **Avicenna**, **Albert the Great**, and **Pliny**—and as the experience of recent voyages testifies—we know the region is full of people of the best temperament and customs, living to a great age because of the equality of cold and heat. Therefore, we assign the middle region to Jupiter. In the same way, we divide the middle area between the tropic and the Arctic Circle (which contains roughly 43 degrees) as follows: the southern part, from the tropic up to 15 degrees, is given to **Venus**; the middle part for the next 15 degrees is given to **Jupiter**; and the final thirteen remaining degrees are given to **Mars**. Therefore, from 23 degrees from the equator to 38 degrees, **Venus** reigns; from 38 to 53...

->OF ASTROLOGICAL MATTERS<-

**Jupiter**: from 53 up to 68 degrees. **Mars**: from 68 up to 90 degrees. **Saturn**: The **Sun** and **Moon**, however, are general causes <note>meaning they influence the entire world generally rather than being tied to specific local climates</note>. **Mercury** truly has no region of its own, but is mixed into all of them, adopting their languages and customs. He is also reasonably placed by **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century Alexandrian astronomer whose work 'Tetrabiblos' founded Western astrology</note> in the middle of the regions. The customs of these regions testify that this partition is true. For the **Arabs**, the **Moors**, the **Egyptians**, and the **Chinese** are **Venus-like** <note>original: *venerei*; influenced by Venus, associated with pleasure, art, and luxury</note> in their customs. **Italians**, **Spaniards**, and **Greeks** reflect **Jupiter** <note>associated with law, religion, and governance</note>. **Germans**, the **English**, and the **French** reflect **Mars** <note>associated with war and physical labor</note>; those at the extreme edges are **Saturnine**. The Arabs measured the <term>climates</term> <note>latitudinal zones of the Earth</note>—especially **Haly Abenragel** <note>a famous 11th-century Arab astrologer</note>—and assigned the seven planets to them, but they did so erroneously. For they looked only at the numerical order of the planets rather than the actual customs and the agreement of the regions with the stars. For **Saturn** is not found under the equator; nor **Jupiter** in the tropics; nor **Mars** in the third climate; nor the **Sun** in the fourth; nor **Venus** in the fifth; nor **Mercury** in the sixth; nor the **Moon** in the seventh. This is clear because the Northern peoples are devoid of the arts <note>which Mercury would provide</note>, and the Moors are far removed from the refined governance of Jupiter. Nor are the peoples of the third climate warlike, but rather the Northerners are; and so it is evident for the rest. For we grant dominion to **Jupiter** where his temperament and customs are actually observed. The Sun heats that climate in such a way that it becomes suitable for the influences of Jupiter, just as the Sun affects the extremes so poorly that they suit the Saturnine nature. We said the same regarding the **houses** <note>astrological divisions of the sky</note>.

5 **Ptolemy**, however, skillfully constructed the dominions of the Planets based on the nature of the <term>triangles</term> <note>also called 'triplicities,' these are groups of three zodiac signs associated with the four elements: Fire, Earth, Air, and Water</note>, but not sufficiently. For he did not concern himself with those living under the equator, nor those in the other hemisphere, nor those beyond the equator. Nor did he follow the reasoning that we use; we, by distributing the planets through parts and climates, have also provided for the **Americans**, distributing the planetary dominions according to the order of the degrees of latitude. In this system, it is manifest that the **Mexicans** are under **Jupiter**, the **Cuzcans** <note>original: *Cuccani*; referring to the people of Cuzco/Inca Empire</note> are under **Venus**, and the **Chichimecs** <note>original: *Cicimeci*; nomadic peoples of north-central Mexico</note> are under **Mars**. Those furthest North, beyond **Florida**, **Spain** <note>likely referring to Spanish territories in North America</note>, and **New France** <note>early colonial Canada</note> toward the Arctic, are **Saturnine**. You will reason conversely for the regions beyond the equator: where those inhabiting the land of **Lucac** <note>a legendary southern land, often appearing on Renaissance maps near Australia</note> are **Saturnine** under the Antarctic, just as those are who live under the tropic of **Saturn**. The intermediate regions are divided just as they are in our hemisphere. But let us explain Ptolemy's reasoning.

6 From the entire earth known to him—which contained **Europe**, **Asia**, and **Africa**—he forms four quadrangles, as if the earth were a square. He gives the East to **Saturn**, the West to **Mars**, the South to **Venus**, and the North to **Jupiter**. He omits the **Sun**, the **Moon**, and **Mercury** as being "common" Planets. Then, in each square, he places the individual triangles. The first, which belongs to **Jupiter** and **Mars**...

### BOOK TWO

...-ties <note>The text continues from the previous page: "triplicities," referring to the four groups of three zodiac signs categorized by the elements</note>, containing three signs of the Zodiac, namely Aries ♈, Leo ♌, and Sagittarius ♐, he assigns to **Europe**. The second, which belongs to **Venus** and **Saturn** (for the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Mercury** are not counted in this way) and contains Taurus ♉, Virgo ♍, and Capricorn ♑, he assigns to **Southern Asia** in its quadrant. The third, which belongs to **Saturn** and **Jupiter**, containing Gemini ♊, Libra ♎, and Aquarius ♒, he assigns to **Northern Asia**, where **Scythia**, **Arsaret** <note>a legendary land beyond the river Euphrates, mentioned in the apocryphal book of 2 Esdras</note>, and **Cathay** <note>the medieval name for China</note> are located. The fourth, which belongs to **Mars** and **Venus**, he assigns to **Africa**, and it contains Cancer ♋, Scorpio ♏, and Pisces ♓. He also assigns the proper winds to these regions, as we wrote above.

Soon he divides the individual quadrants and doubles the triangles into Eastern and Western: so that the triangle of Europe is found in Southern Asia—the eastern part with the eastern **Jupiter** and **Mars**, and in Europe the western ones. Similarly, he divides the triangle of Southern Asia into an Eastern part, which prevails there, and a Western part, which is in Europe. He does the same by interchanging the third and fourth triangles. And he places **Mercury** in the center of the earth, where languages flourish and all the lawgivers are found. For indeed in **Palestine**, **Arabia**, and **Syria**, the laws of **Moses**, **Christ**, the **Apostles**, and **Muhammad** <note>original: "Macometi"</note> began, along with many sciences, as is shown in the following diagram.

...are hot and humid; the western ones are purer, cold, and partly dry. Likewise, how does the North Wind <note>original: *Boreas*</note>, which is cold and dry, suit **Jupiter** ♃? Or how does the South Wind <note>original: *Auster*</note> alone suit **Venus** ♀? Yet it can be explained that eastern **Mercury** ☿, **Mars** ♂, and **Jupiter** ♃ stir up eastern winds; similarly eastern **Mars** ♂ and **Venus** ♀; hence in this diagram every wind can be attributed to every planet.

But the North Wind <note>original: *Septentrio*</note> does not suit **Jupiter** ♃ insofar as it is cold and dry, but insofar as it is pure and healthy. Nor is this description valid beyond 70 degrees of latitude, because from that point on the people are wild <note>original: *sylvestres*</note>, sharing nothing with the civility of **Jupiter** ♃. It is clear that **Ptolemy** was short-sighted <note>original: *curtum*</note> in assigning these judgments. Nor does **Venus** ♀ have any influence in the tropics, where the character of **Saturn** ♄ prevails, and the winds are thin or nonexistent. For those winds that are brought to us thick and wet receive their qualities from the Mediterranean Sea. But in the tropics, everything is parched without any breeze, and people live in caves; they have shorter lives due to the imbalance <note>original: *intemperie*</note> of **Saturn** ♄, and they eat locusts and abominable foods.

Therefore, we have philosophized more correctly and sufficiently than **Ptolemy**. That **Mars** ♂ flourishes in the region of the **Goths** and **Scythians** is an ancient fame celebrated by poets: so that **Jupiter** ♃ has little influence, except for the healthiness of the winds found in the middle region, as has been declared.

8. He <note>Ptolemy</note> learnedly connects the exchange of the triangles <note>the groupings of zodiac signs by element</note>—would that he did so truly. We transfer this system to **America**: and we place it between 27 and 70 degrees of latitude, so that the first quadrant is in **Quivira** <note>a semi-mythical kingdom in North America, often sought by Spanish explorers in the modern-day Great Plains</note>; the second in the island of **Hispaniola** <note>the island containing modern Haiti and the Dominican Republic</note>; the third in **Spanish Florida**; the fourth in the **Peruvian** region and the adjacent islands. But since different winds exist there due to a different placement of the sea, I do not determine them, but only outline them. The same can be done in the other semicircle beyond the equator in both hemispheres. But since there is more sea there than land, and the nature of the winds is different, I leave the Ptolemaic task to its inhabitants; for my own system satisfies both easily.

## On the customs of nations according to the nature of the ruling signs.

### ARTICLE III.

**Aries** ♈ makes men fierce, stubborn, grim, bold, wicked, and treacherous, like the **English**.

**Taurus** ♉ makes them devoted to pleasures, to cleanliness of food and clothing, and to luxuries, like the **Neapolitans**.

**Gemini** ♊ makes them fickle, somewhat wicked, thoughtful, prudent, and possessing understanding of all things related to divine wisdom; they are magicians, founders of secret rites, and mathematicians, like the **Egyptians** of old.

**Cancer** ♋ makes them merchants and good companions who rejoice in an abundance of things; they are fond of women, like the **Carthaginians** of old; but the women are imperious, contentious, and industrious.

**Leo** ♌ makes them constant, kind, eager for friendship, simple, humane, and worshippers of the stars.

**Virgo** ♍ makes them the best mathematicians, astronomers, fit for various disciplines, ingenious, learned, and cultivators of the mind.

**Libra** ♎ makes them devoted to the delights of music, accumulators of wealth, lustful <note>original: *calidos ad coitum*, literally "hot for intercourse"</note>, and fickle in their counsel.

**Scorpio** ♏ makes them savage, warlike, meat-eaters <note>original: *carnivoros*</note>, wicked, despisers of life, devoted to dangers, deceitful, and furious.

**Sagittarius** ♐ makes them simple, lovers of cleanliness and liberty, generous, skillful, and fit for business and contracts.

**Capricorn** ♑ makes them deformed, foul, savage, harsh, alienated from social conversation, but industrious in acquiring property.

**Aquarius** ♒ makes them meat-eaters, fish-eaters <note>original: *ichthyophagos*</note>, shepherds, savage, gloomy, and leading a rustic life.

**Pisces** ♓ makes them generous, merchants, attentive, easy-going, simple in their customs, clean, friends of a popular state <note>likely referring to a preference for republican or democratic governance</note>, strong in counsel, and artisans of beautiful works.

### *Examination of the aforementioned dominions.*

### ARTICLE V.

¹ We have these decrees from Ptolemy concerning the dominions of the planets and signs over nations, organized according to the outer and inner <term>triangles</term> <note>These are "triplicities," groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water) used to categorize the world into quadrants</note>. However, since these assignments do not agree with our times at all—indeed, they differ greatly—it must be that Ptolemy was either in error or failed to realize that his teaching was not eternal.

² To be sure, in his time Greece was the most learned and eloquent of nations, just as he himself teaches regarding the inner triangle of the second triplicity, because Virgo ♍ and Mercury ☿ ruled over it. But now, it has been gradually so overwhelmed by barbarism that, having finally been buried under the rule of the Turks, it seems lost in the darkness of ignorance, sluggishness, cowardice, and triviality; nothing could be worse. # ASTROLOGY

## *Although God changes lower things, it is not without secondary causes. And that which the Ptolemaics said concerning the changes of empires and sects based on the trigons is insufficient.*

### CHAPTER III. ARTICLE I.

<margin>1</margin>Since God rules the lower realms by a natural course—which is the law of the Word of God—and has reserved for Himself a few miracles above the natural course to be shown in His own time, God acts according to nature together with secondary causes <note>In theology, secondary causes are the natural forces or agents through which God, the Primary Cause, operates in the world</note>. For this reason, **Saint Thomas** <note>Thomas Aquinas</note> rejects the opinion of the **followers of Muhammad** <note>original: *Macometistarum*; a reference to Islamic "occasionalist" philosophers who argued that natural objects have no power of their own, but that God performs every action directly</note> who assert that it is not the Sun that shines, but God in the Sun. For in that way, the action of forms <note>The inherent power of a thing to act according to its nature</note> would be taken away. Therefore, the changes in human affairs, even if they are from God, should not be thought to occur without natural causes; although **Cyril** and other theologians ascribe all things principally to God—both more truly and more greatly. Consequently, our affairs do not change without the actions of the stars, nor would they change if the stars remained unchanged.

<margin>2</margin>For this reason, **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century father of Western astrology</note> is deficient in his doctrine when he attributes the changes and beginnings of things to eclipses alone. Since these are of short duration, they only have the power to indicate matters of short duration. The same is true of comets. How can the transfers and durations of kingdoms, or the laws and sects that endure for so many years, be caused by these? Furthermore, how are customs and laws transferred if the **trigons** <note>original: *trigoni*; also called triplicities, these are groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element. Astrologers used their cycles to predict major historical shifts</note> remain the same? If they do not remain the same, why was Ptolemy silent about it, and why did he say nothing of the future based on past changes? Certainly, he knew that the kingdom and law of the Jews were once most flourishing but were scattered in his own time, and that the monarchy had been transferred from **Persia** to the **Macedonians**. This could not be attributed to eclipses, which hardly have a decree lasting beyond 30 months—especially since others continually follow, bringing new and contrary decrees, just as day follows day. It is necessary, therefore, to accept more powerful causes, which **Albumasar** <note>The Latinized name of Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer known for his theory of Great Conjunctions</note> recognized but did not perfect. Just as the decree of a single lunar cycle does not indicate the course of an entire year—but rather the solar quarters and eclipses, which are rarer, do so—likewise an eclipse does not indicate the transfer and duration of monarchies, but only their particular and partial changes. And as for the trigons, we see...

<margin>3</margin>**Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer whose work was a standard textbook in Medieval Europe</note> and **Cardano** <note>Girolamo Cardano (1501–1576), a famous Italian Renaissance physician and astrologer</note> have recourse to the changes of the **triplicities** <term>triplicities: groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element—Fire, Earth, Air, or Water</term>. They do not explain exactly how the change on earth results from the movement of the stars, but rather how the successive **great conjunctions** <term>great conjunctions: the rare meeting of the planets Jupiter and Saturn in the sky, occurring roughly every 20 years and believed to signal major historical shifts</term> of Jupiter and Saturn across the four triplicities introduce various sects, arts, empires, and customs. <margin>4</margin>They say, therefore, that while the great conjunctions occur in the **first trigon** <note>The "Fiery Trigon," consisting of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</note>—which last for 199 years, occurring every 20 years—there are born in the lower world empires, the peace and tranquility of monarchies, through the dominion of the Sun and Jupiter. For 200 years, while the conjunctions occurred in the first trigon, the monarchy and the holy law prevailed, for which countless people died—a fact signified by Mars, the ruler of Aries. Indeed, six years before the birth of Christ, a great conjunction occurred in Aries. After 800 years, a new monarchy of **Charlemagne** arose in the West, similar to the first one. From this, Cardano thinks that after the year 1583—when the conjunctions began to return to the first trigon—there will be a new and most powerful monarchy of the whole world, so that all things may be ruled by the will of one man. The Sun, as King of all the Planets, brings this to pass.

But in the **second earthly trigon** <note>The "Earthly Trigon," consisting of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn</note>, they say earthquakes, floods, and comets occur, and the monarchy of the fiery trigon begins to falter. Those things established under the **watery trigon** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note> are dissolved. Thus, in the time of **Constantine**, idolatry was destroyed. The Moon brought about the travels of Bishops for new Church Councils and the rise of various religious sects. The Empire began to be divided among Counts, and the **Goths, Heruli, Vandals, and Huns** changed their homelands. In these times, luxury, variety, and all matters of Venus flourish, such as once existed in ancient Babylon under this same trigon. Similarly, 200 years after Charlemagne, the strength of the **Franks** [French] began to diminish, the **Saracen** sect was broken, and other previously mentioned innovations began to occur. Under the **third trigon**, which belongs to **Saturn** and **Mercury** <note>The "Airy Trigon," consisting of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius</note>, the monarchies first established are dissolved and transferred to other regions; Republics are founded, wise men are multiplied, and the arts grow strong...

For Mars <note>original: "♂"</note> and the Moon precipitate rash counsel, so that it seems as if there is no freedom within us. At this same time, the Gospel travels to the New World. ### ARTICLE II.

From this, it follows that the obliquity <term>obliquity: the angle between the celestial equator and the ecliptic (the Sun's path), which was observed to be decreasing over centuries</term> toward the tropics decreases. Therefore, because of the descent of the Sun, the narrowing of the obliquity, the anticipation of the solstices, and the change of the signs, we must philosophize about great matters in the lower world <note>The "lower world" refers to the terrestrial realm beneath the heavens</note>. # BOOK SECOND

Parts cut off from the mainland are not suitable to be the seat of empires. From here, religion, the cultivation of the mind, and the tilling of the soil finally migrate from the Spaniards into the other hemisphere; nature itself manifests this same truth. For in the time of Pliny <note>Gaius Plinius Secundus (23–79 AD), author of *Natural History*</note>, dates <note>original: "dactyli"</note> did not grow in Italy, but now they do; they did not used to ripen in Cyprus, but now they do. The earth was not cultivated in Germany, nor was there grain; they lived a life of plunder in the forests without cities. Now, however, Germany is most civilized in its manners, arts, and the cultivation of both the soil and its cities. From here, virtue, religion, and the arts have reached the once most-barbarous Cimbrians and Swedes, so much so that Tycho <note>Tycho Brahe (1546–1601), the famous Danish astronomer</note> has, in Denmark, surpassed even the Egyptian mathematicians. Likewise, Copernicus has revived the Pythagorean sects of Philolaus in Germany, as if not only empire, but also the sciences were transferred from Italy to that place—the Sun now operating more effectively there for the cultivation of the soil and of spirits. Let no one doubt that this happens, since St. Thomas <note>Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274), the influential theologian who sought to reconcile Aristotelian science with Christianity</note> attributes the balance of the humors to the heavens, and teaches that even the foolish and stupid can be made fit for learning by a better constellation; reason itself bears witness to this. Therefore, although the same trigons <term>trigon: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water)</term> persist, the strength of these trigons must nevertheless be changed by the descent of the Sun and the planets—especially when the Sun descends more rapidly, as in the time of Muhammad.

<margin>5</margin> The second general cause of the change in lower things is the "translation" <note>the movement or shifting</note> of the constellations from one angle of the sky to another, and from the position of one sign into the position of another. This occurs by one degree every 100 years according to Ptolemy <note>the 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian astronomer</note>; therefore, the entire circle is completed in 36,000 years. According to Alfonso <note>Alfonso X of Castile (1221–1284), sponsor of the Alfonsine astronomical tables</note>, it is completed in 49,000 years; according to Copernicus, in 25,816 years—from which Tycho does not differ much. Albategnius <note>Al-Battani (c. 858–929), a major Arab astronomer and mathematician</note>, however, reduced this; for in his view, the fixed stars travel one degree backward in 70 years and 7 months; but in another view, it is 66 years. Copernicus, however, places the anomaly <term>anomaly: a technical term for the irregularity in planetary or stellar motion</term> between 70 seconds and Tycho at 30, and between 50, 12, 5 seconds annually because of the observations of the ancients. We have written elsewhere regarding these matters and how they are all mistaken. When, therefore, the fixed stars are transferred from the North to the South and vice-versa, it is necessary that kingdoms and human affairs also change, like a heliotrope <note>a plant that turns to follow the sun</note> turning toward the Sun. This becomes most apparent when stars of the first magnitude pass into other signs. For this reason, when the stars of Leo passed into Virgo—specifically the Tail of the Lion <note>the star Denebola</note>—the empire of Italy was then transferred by Constantine to Greece. For Italy is subject to Leo, and Greece to Virgo, according to Ptolemy. Leo is the strongest sign, in which the Basiliscus <term>Basiliscus: the "Little King," better known as the star Regulus, the brightest star in the constellation Leo</term> has remained; therefore, Italy has not been too greatly depressed.

# ON ASTROLOGY

The **Vandals**, **Goths**, and **Heruli** crossed into **Italy**, however, when the stars of Cancer moved into Leo. When **Regulus** <note>original: "Basiliscus," the brightest star in the constellation Leo</note> passes into Virgo—which will happen in nearly six hundred years—Italian virtue and dominion will collapse, and the Republic will fall, unless perhaps it is preserved by the entry of **Sirius** <note>original: "Canicula," the Dog Star</note>. I do not entirely hope for this, as Sirius has a wide latitude; however, Regulus falls within the Zodiac: I fear a barbaric dominion. For foreign stars bring in foreign rulers. This is why the Italian and Turkish empires rose in **Greece**, but not the Greek empire, which collapsed. When the stars of Taurus entered Gemini, the rule of outsiders entered **Egypt**, and in **Cathay** <note>China</note> and among the less northern **Tartars**, many kingdoms took their rise from **Aldebaran** <note>a giant red star in the constellation Taurus</note>. Since **Antares** <note>a red star in the constellation Scorpio</note> also passed into Sagittarius, the power of the Moors (who are subject to Scorpio) decreased, and the **Spaniards** recovered their dominion, expelled the Moors from Spain, and expanded their rule into foreign regions.

But note that if an empire extends into regions of the same **trigon** <note>one of the four groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note>, the rule will be political <note>referring to a civil or constitutional government among equals</note>; if it extends into a different trigon, the rule will be despotic. In **Italy**, the Spaniards rule civilly, but in Africa and America, they rule cruelly. Nor could they be established in **England** and **Germany**, because these are of the same trigon, and Aries is marked by noble stars. Morals also vary because of the passage of such stars. The regions subject to **Libra** received many benefits from **Spica** <note>original: "Azimech," the brightest star in Virgo/Libra region</note>, such as the **Troglodytes** <note>ancient term for cave-dwelling peoples of Africa or the Red Sea</note> gaining a kingdom, as well as the Cathayans and the **Venetians**, who founded their Republic under a **Great Conjunction** <note>original: "synodus magna"; a rare alignment of Jupiter and Saturn</note> in Libra.

When a new law is promulgated, if it is issued in a region subject to the trigon under whose Great Conjunctions it occurred, it will last a long time and be easily planted. If it is issued under a contrary sign, it will hardly take root there, but will instead pass to the regions of its own trigon. Hence, the Muhammadan law flourishes more in Africa—where the Water Trigon <note>$\triangle$ ♋</note> resides, under which it began—than in Arabia, where <term>+⸬</term> <note>a symbol likely indicating a conflicting astrological aspect or specific location</note>. Likewise, the law of Christ is stronger in Spain (where Sagittarius is, under which it began) than in Syria, where it actually started. It is strengthened in Italy under the fixed sign of Leo, because the outer triangle is more powerful and more durable.

**6** The third general cause is the movement of the **apsides** <note>the points in an orbit farthest from the center, such as the Sun's apogee</note> of the planets from sign to sign, especially if it is a movable sign. This occurs every 1,500 years for the Sun, but at various times for the other planets, as noted by **Copernicus** and **Tycho Brahe**. It is clear that while the Sun's apogee entered Cancer, the sect of Muhammad (belonging to that same trigon) flourished, and the power of the Turks, the **Sharifs** <note>original: "Seriforum"; rulers of Morocco or Mecca</note>, the **Safavids** <note>original: "Sofiorum"; the dynasty ruling Persia</note>, and others was magnified. Similarly, when the apogee of Jupiter reached Libra, the empire of the Tartars...

...then rose their lawgiver **Genghis** <note>original: "Cingus," referring to Genghis Khan</note>, who is said to have emulated the miracles of **Moses** by crossing the **Caspian** Sea with his companions on dry feet. Similarly, **Alexander the Great**, expanding his empire under the same trigon <note>one of the four groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note>, is said to have bridged a river erupting from the Caspian mountains and proclaimed himself the son of the god **Ammon**. For **Saturn** and **Mercury** incline men toward miracles, which they employ whether truly or falsely. Therefore, they are not to be equated with Moses, just as **Theudas** or **Apollonius** <note>Apollonius of Tyana, a first-century philosopher and miracle-worker often compared to Christ in antiquity</note> are not to be equated with **Christ**, nor **Arius** <note>the 4th-century priest whose teachings led to the Arian heresy</note> with **Athanasius** <note>the bishop who defended the orthodox view of the Trinity</note>, even though they attempted similar things under the same trigons.

7. Furthermore, at this time the apogee <term>absis|the point in a planet's orbit farthest from the center of attraction; here used to describe the peak of a planet's astrological influence</term> of **Mercury** passed out of the sign of **Scorpio**—the pestilent sign of **Muhammad** <note>original: "Macometico"</note> and the **Moors**—and into **Sagittarius**, the sign of the **Christians** and **Spain**. Because of this, eloquence, commerce, the proclamation of laws, literature, and the invention of arts have passed from them to our people. Everywhere on the **African** shores, the **Spanish** mostly stand in their way, removing their colonies and planting their own, especially on the southern and eastern coasts. Among the **Arabs**, the **Islanders**, and the borders of the **Persians**, preachers from Spain are spreading out, and letters have begun to be cultivated there most intensely. Also, in **Tuscany** <note>original: "Hetruria"</note>, a new science of the stars begins with **Galileo**. For Tuscany is also subject to Sagittarius, from which we hope for wonders. However, when the apogee of Saturn enters Capricorn—which will happen fifteen years from now—one should expect the preaching of the **Antichrist** (for that is the sign of the Sun in the birth of Christ) or other novelties spoken of in the prophecies. There will arise in **India**, **Illyricum** <note>the Roman province covering much of the Balkan Peninsula</note>, and **Macedonia** most wonderful dominions and sects, if they truly fall under this sign as **Ptolemy** said.

8. The fourth cause of great changes is the variation in obliquity <term>obliquitatum|the tilt of the Earth's axis relative to the sun, which changes over long cycles and affects the seasons</term> both in the course of the **Sun** and the **Planets**. It is evident that just as the poplar, the elm, and the linden tree turn their leaves when the Sun is in the tropics, so too are the celestial motions of souls affected. For this reason, since the obliquity began to narrow—it was 23 degrees and 51 minutes under **Ptolemy**, but now it is nearly 23 degrees and 28 minutes—the northern peoples have almost always raided the southern regions: such as the **Lombards**, **Goths**, **Heruli**, **Huns**, **Vandals**, **Turks**, **Tartars**, and **Mughals** <note>original: "Mogori"</note>. But if the tilt were expanding, as **Copernicus** believes (which I do not), the **Romans**, **Macedonians**, and **Persians** would have expanded their empire and colonies into the North for that reason. However, this is uncertain. Nor was the migration of the Romans into the North, or at least its duration, as great as that of the Goths alone into the South...

# ASTROLOGICAL MATTERS

...our own outpouring. The same occurred in the East Indies. Never have the **Africans** in **Italy** prevailed in the same way the **Italians** have prevailed in **Africa**. This, however, is by the design of **God**, so that the seeds of the fertile northern nations <note>original: "borealium"</note> may be introduced to the sterile nations of the south. The movement of our people, however, is more often along the lines of longitude during the expansion of empires. When it has moved toward the North, it was due to another cause involving trigons <note>groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> and comets, which was opposed by the ratio of the Earth's obliquity <note>the tilt of the Earth's axis</note>. The obliquity of the **Planets** and the **Moon** can also increase; but concerning these, see my work on *Astronomy*. Therefore, the ruling planet will drive events as the logic of its obliquity demands—either toward the North or the South—just as the latitude of its position drives the winds. For the animal spirit <term>spiritus animalis|in medieval physiology, a fine substance that carries sensation and movement through the body</term> is like the wind, whose impulse the human mind can follow or restrain; however, the mind usually follows it, as **Saint Thomas Aquinas** testifies. These seven days of creation correspond to the seven millennia of the world's age, as **David**, **Saint Peter**, and the **Rabbis** seem to suggest. We must always consider under which millennium and under which **Planet** we reside. We seem now to be in the sixth millennium and under **Mercury** [☿]; under **Christ**, we were under the Sun <note>the original uses a star symbol ✱, which Campanella frequently uses for the Sun or a Great Star associated with Christ</note>. ### *On the other causes and beginnings of changes, and their modes and truths.*

### ARTICLE III.

<margin>1</margin> Just as a month contains many days, so a year contains many months, and an age <note>original: "saeculum"</note> contains many years. The causes and beginnings of new ages run in cycles, just like those of days and years.

<margin>2</margin> The first cause, according to **Cardano** <note>Girolamo Cardano, a famous 16th-century Italian polymath and astrologer</note>, is thought to be the conjunction of the "heads" of **Aries** in the eighth and ninth spheres, which occurs every 36,000 years—or more, or fewer, as we previously discussed. He believes this was celebrated at the time of **Christ’s** birth, but he is mistaken, as is clear from the calculations of **Copernicus**. For at that time, the first star of **Aries** was nearly four degrees distant from the equinoctial hinge <note>the point where the celestial equator and ecliptic intersect</note>. And I strongly doubt whether it has always receded, since **Moses**, the **Chaldeans**, and all ancient ages began the equinox from the first star of the constellation **Aries**, not from **Taurus**, as would have been expected; thus **Aries** was the beginning of the twelve-fold division of the signs. It would have had to be distant from the hinge by nearly 30 degrees during the time of Christ, counting from when **Prometheus** first promulgated Astrology in **Chaldea** under **Belus Jupiter** <note>a syncretic reference to the Babylonian god Bel/Marduk, often associated by Renaissance scholars with Nimrod</note>. But if it has always receded, we must admit our ignorance,

What star was the head of the equinox <note>original: "caput æquinoctij"; the point where the celestial equator and ecliptic intersect</note> from the beginning of the world is unknown, since the age of the world is most uncertain. If, however, this recession <note>The precession of the equinoxes, where the positions of the stars slowly change over centuries.</note> began under **Hipparchus** <note>A Greek astronomer (c. 190–120 BC) who is credited with discovering the precession of the equinoxes.</note>, or a little before, as it seems—due to the leadership of **Aries** from that age—it is a wonder from where this novelty arose, were it not for the greatest novelty in human affairs described by Him who said: *I will shake the heaven and the earth, and the desired of all nations shall come.* <note>A reference to the biblical prophecy in Haggai 2:6-7, interpreted here as the coming of Christ.</note> and truly it was so at the advent of **Christ**, which a new star also announced under **Hipparchus**. 4. Of these causes, the slower and more infrequent ones are the most powerful and produce longer-lasting effects. **Cardanus** <note>Girolamo Cardano (1501–1576), an influential Italian physician, mathematician, and astrologer.</note> suggests that when two or more causes coincide, one should multiply the rarity of the effect of one cause by the other. For example, a "great conjunction" <note>The meeting of Jupiter and Saturn, which happens roughly every 20 years.</note> occurs every 20 years; if this happens alongside a conjunction of the Sun and Moon (which occurs every 27 days and 8 hours), they are multiplied together if they occur at the same moment. If they are apart, they are calculated according to the ratio of their distance. However, these effects are further varied by the following configurations. If they are separated by a semi-diameter, you multiply half the Moon’s motion by 20; if by a degree, by a fourth part of 38. Secondly, the magnitude of the effect is multiplied based on its rarity according to precise alignment. For instance, **Saturn** (♄) possesses four units of power, **Jupiter** (♃) five, and **Mars** (♂) three. Therefore, if they are joined at the same point, you multiply three, four, and five together, and that effect will have a strength of 60. But if **Mars** (♂) is distant by one degree, the strength is diminished.

## ARTICLE IV.

1 Furthermore, **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century foundational authority on astronomy and astrology.</note> identifies eclipses and comets as the causes of all changes. We, however, include all the aforementioned conjunctions, and add eclipses and comets as well. Likewise, he cites the duration of an eclipse or comet as the cause for how long its effects last. We, on the other hand, do not disregard the rules of **Cardanus**, nor the timing of the triplicities <note>Groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element: fire, earth, air, or water.</note> and other configurations. Finally, we add the "anomalies" <note>Irregularities or deviations from perfectly circular celestial motion.</note> of the tilt <note>original: "obliquitatis"; the tilt of the Earth's axis.</note>, eccentricity <note>The deviation of an orbit from a perfect circle.</note>, the orbital points <note>original: "abſidum"</note>, the cardinal points, and the movement of the stars from one zodiac sign to another <note>original: "de dodecatemoria in dodecatemoriam"; refers to the twelve divisions of the zodiac.</note>. According to **Copernicus**, this transition happens across all signs every 1,717 years. He believes the return of the tilt of the axis occurs in 3,434 years, for he thinks the poles balance one another <note>original: "librari"</note> and are shaken by an alternating oscillation <note>original: "libratione"</note>, so that they double their motion in the manner of a twisted wreath. ...and the obliquity <note>The angle between the Earth's equator and its path around the sun, which determines the seasons.</note> is always decreasing, and the fixed stars are always being moved further back <note>A phenomenon known as the precession of the equinoxes.</note>; certainly, that idea of a reversal of the Sun upward, and toward the poles of the tropics, and the movement of the stars into a different path, must be considered false.

However, an anomaly <term>anomaly: here referring to the "trepidation" or irregular variation in the speed of the stars' movement</term> must be conceded, even though it was denied by **Tycho Brahe** <note>original: "Thycone"; the famous Danish astronomer known for his accurate celestial observations.</note>. But this does not always occur every 1,717 years, since **Copernicus** observed only one such instance from the time of **Hipparchus** <note>An ancient Greek astronomer (c. 190–120 BCE) who discovered the precession of the equinoxes.</note> until our own day. A universal rule should not be established from a single observation. Nor should we think the poles circle in such a way, nor should reversals of the axial tilts be invented. For the planets are always descending, and the obliquity is tightening, until the very form of this world collapses.

Meanwhile, I say that the law and empire which begins during a period of slowness in these anomalies lasts for a very long time, such as the Roman and Babylonian empires. Those, however, that begin during a period of velocity grow quickly and change quickly. For it is clear that in the time of **Ptolemy**, the fixed stars moved by one degree every 100 years, which is when the monarchy of the Caesars began; and **CHRIST** was born then, choosing for himself the time of the first trigon <note>A "trigon" or triplicity refers to a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element; a "great conjunction" in the fire signs was considered the most auspicious.</note>, the best of all, and a period of constancy in the anomalies.

In the time of **Al-Battani** <note>original: "Albategnij"; a 9th-century Arab astronomer.</note>, however, the stars completed one degree in 60 years, and at that time the anomaly was at its fastest. The law of **Muhammad** began in the fourth trigon, which quickly traversed the world along with the arms of the Saracens, but it soon languished. Now, however, it has been strengthened by the transit of the apsides <term>apsides: the points in an orbit where a planet is closest to or furthest from the sun</term> of the Sun (<term>☉</term>) and Venus (<term>♀</term>) into Cancer (<term>♋</term>). This is because, due to the influence of the Moon (<term>☽</term>) and Mars (<term>♂</term>), the nature of the trigon agreed with the timing of the anomaly.

But the monarchy of **Charlemagne** <note>original: "Caroli Magni"</note> began during a period of velocity in the anomaly, which does not suit the first slow trigon of Jupiter. For that reason, it did not last as long, nor did it expand itself further, even though it rose up quickly. However, the empire which begins at this time—if it be the Spanish one—will break the strength of the Turks and will last for a very long time, because it begins under a period of slowness and a slow trigon, if **Copernicus** is not mistaken and as it seems also to **Tycho**, about which I write elsewhere.

Consider also in all planetary changes whether they are slow or fast, or in an "angle" <note>The most powerful houses in an astrological chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th.</note>, or in "succedent" houses, or "cadent" houses, or whether they rise in the morning or set in the evening. In this way, you will be able to judge the speed and duration of events with expertise.

### *On recognizing the domains of planets and signs over provinces and cities according to our teachings, even though the celestial causes have shifted.*

->ARTICLE V.<-

1 The causes and the origins of the influence of the stars are clear from these principles, but not specifically which things they rule over: nor can you know which regions they govern, unless you know which sign and planet they fall under. This was not sufficiently established by the doctrine of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 CE), the influential Greco-Egyptian astronomer whose "Tetrabiblos" mapped signs of the zodiac to known regions of the world.</note>, since the customs and the strengths of nations have changed; and perhaps it is not perfectly established by our own teaching either, but nevertheless we have something more certain to offer. I say, therefore, that under the equator, **Jupiter** [♃] always rules in the middle, **Saturn** [♄] in the extremes, and **Mars** [♂] and **Venus** in the intermediate areas. Outside the tropics up to 70 degrees, **Venus** holds the first parts, **Jupiter** the second, and **Mars** the third. But just as the customs and powers of regions varied in Ptolemy’s work as the fixed stars moved from sign to sign, so in our own teaching, as the Sun "descends" <note>Referring to the decreasing obliquity of the ecliptic mentioned on the previous page.</note>, the power of **Saturn** gradually expands outside the tropics: and consequently, **Venus** carries her rule, or the limits of her domain, a little further out. Thus the domain of **Jupiter** migrates further with its limits, so that it now moves from **Italy** and **Greece** into **France** <note>original: "Galliam"</note> and **Germany**, and **Venus** succeeds to us. **Mars**, however, reaches to the 70th degree and beyond. For in this way the temperaments of places are varied, and they come to correspond to different planets. The migration of the fixed stars <note>The precession of the equinoxes, which causes the stars to shift their positions relative to the seasons over centuries.</note> also changes much. Therefore, we philosophize generally from these principles in this way.

2 Specifically, however, we know a province is subject to a certain sign from the fact that while an eclipse or a great <term>synodus: a conjunction or meeting of planets</term> occurs in that sign, the province is affected. For this reason, **Brunswick** <note>original: "Bransuicum"</note> is placed under **Capricorn** by **Reinhold** <note>Erasmus Reinhold (1511–1553), a leading astronomer who calculated the "Prutenic Tables" based on Copernicus's work.</note>.

3 When any planet is affected—whether for good or ill—whichever city or region is similarly affected is considered to be under that planet's rule.

4 We can also tell from the customs of a region, their clothing, and their colors: for the most just **Venetians**, who wear religious black garments, are subject to **Jupiter** and **Saturn**.

5 Finally, we can tell from the site of the city: for because it is situated in the waters, **Venice** is assigned to the aquatic signs, such as **Pisces** [♓] or **Cancer** [♋]. The same is true for **Holland**, and formerly for **Mexico** <note>Likely referring to the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, which was built on a lake and famous for its canals.</note>.

# BOOK TWO

6 From the fact that a great conjunction <note>original: *synodus magna*; a significant alignment of planets, usually Jupiter and Saturn, believed to signal major historical shifts</note> presided over the foundation [of a city or movement] in a specific sign: for example, before the founding of Venice, the conjunction was in Libra [♎]. At the founding of Lutheranism, and of the Republics of the Swiss, the Grisons, and Holland, it was in Cancer [♋] and the watery signs. These watery locations and deserts are also significant to **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century authority on geography and astrology.</note>.

7 From the horoscope and the *aphetas* <note>original: *apheta*; the "giver of life" or the planet used to determine the lifespan and vitality in a birth chart</note> of the figure erected for the city, as is done in a nativity <note>original: *genesi*; a birth chart for an individual</note>.

8 When these [the foundation dates] are missing, judgment is made from the day on which the market is celebrated in that city. For this reason, I believe Naples is subject to **Taurus**, because the market is held in Naples on the days of the **Moon** and **Venus**; and truly, the people there are as changeable as the Moon and as delirious as Venus. This rule is a thin one from **Abenragel** <note>Albohazen Haly Abenragel (950–1035), a famous Arab astrologer whose work was central to Medieval European astrology</note>, but it is valid when the customs of the people are considered as well. Nor do I think Naples should be assigned to the fierce Aries, as some authors write. In Cosenza, the market is held on the day of **Saturn**, and truly the people of Cosenza are "Saturnine" <note>Traditionally meaning gloomy, slow, or grave.</note>.

Whether a planet truly rules over the days—specifically the first civil hour of the day, as the tradition and usage of three thousand years has held from the Chaldeans to the Egyptians and Romans—is doubted by **Saint Thomas** [Aquinas] in his *Opuscula*. He says this matters nothing to the theologian: for it neither contradicts the faith nor favors it. But if the week is a constant of nature, one might accept that it corresponds to the planets, just as the ages of man in Ptolemy's work also have a symbolic connection with the year, the day, and the month, as we shall discuss in the proper place.

9 A city sometimes falls under the triplicity <note>original: *trigono*; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element—Fire, Earth, Air, or Water</note> of its province, and sometimes under the specific sign under which it was founded. Therefore, to know if a city will be affected by an event, you must know its triplicity and its nativity. If those are missing, take the *Medium Coeli* <note>The "Midheaven," the highest point in a chart, representing the government, the ruler, or public status</note> of the city's prince and judge according to that; for the suffering and the actions of the prince and his vassals are the same.

10 Erect the figures <note>astrological charts</note> for the great conjunctions and for the beginning of sects and kingdoms, and judge them just as we shall describe regarding eclipses.

[...][planets that] aspect the eclipse, or occupy an angle <note>The four critical points in an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Lower Heaven</note>, or are rising, setting, reaching the highest point in the sky, or reaching the bottom of the heavens, have power over all things. This is especially true if they are stationary <note>original: *stationarij*; when a planet appears to stop moving in the sky before changing direction, believed to concentrate its influence</note>, because they are then closer to us and more firm in promoting their effect. Furthermore, if they are "lords" [ruling planets], benefic [fortunate] planets have power for good, while malefic [unfortunate] planets have power for evil. This is particularly true where they "fall" <note>original: *casu*; a state of planetary weakness</note>, such as **Mars** [♂] and **Saturn** [♄] in **Cancer** [♋]. In their fall—where the former [Mars] affects the place of **Jupiter** and the latter [Saturn] the place of the **Moon**—they corrupt the effects of the planets ruling there.

3. It is necessary to consider the following: the active causes mentioned, the beginnings of the actions, the type of subject being affected, the time, the place, the quality of the effect, and its magnitude.

## *On the place to be affected by stellar causes during an eclipse.*

### ARTICLE II.

Regarding the location, we say that a province is affected if it lies beneath the place of the eclipse. A city is affected if it lies beneath the zodiac sign of the eclipse, or if its *apheta* <note>original: *apheta*; the planet or point in a chart that "gives life" or represents the city's vitality</note> or horoscope <note>original: *horoscopus*; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the city's founding</note> is aligned with it. Likewise, the Midheaven <note>original: *medium coeli*; the highest point of the sky in a chart, representing authority and public standing</note> of the governor or the prince of the city or province is considered. This is especially true in solar eclipses, and only in those places where the eclipse is visible above the earth.

## *On the beginning and duration of the effect.*

### ARTICLE III.

1. To know the timing, one must erect a figure [a chart], as is done in a nativity. In an eclipse <note>original: *defectu*; literally a 'failing' or 'defect' of light</note> of the **Sun** and **Moon**, consider how many equinoctial hours <note>Standard 60-minute hours, as opposed to seasonal hours which varied in length</note> it lasts. The effect of a solar eclipse will last for as many years as there were hours, and the effect of a lunar eclipse will last for as many months. Fractional parts of hours correspond to fractional parts of years or months.

2. If the eclipse occurs on the eastern horizon, the effect begins in the first four months and will be strongest at the start. It gradually weakens over as many months (or parts) as the hours (or parts) it was visible above the earth. If it occurs in the Midheaven [the noon position], the effect will begin in the second four months; it will be weak at the start, strong in the middle, and decrease at the end. If it occurs in the western quarter, it will begin in the third four-month period—that is, after the eighth month through the twelfth, in proportion to its distance from the western angle. It will be strongest in its final portion, as both reason and experience dictate.

3. Some think that one should begin calculating the start of an eclipse's effect from sunrise, according to the number of civil hours <note>Ordinary clock hours used in daily life, as opposed to solar or planetary hours</note>, with the number of months corresponding to that same number. However, it is better to calculate the time from the midpoint of the eclipse and through the "quarters" already mentioned, following the method of Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century scholar whose work was the foundation of medieval and Renaissance astrology</note>.

4. Therefore, all eclipses reveal their effects within the first year from their hour; no effect can progress beyond 30 months in a solar eclipse, nor beyond 16 months in a lunar one.

5. Full moons, new moons <note>original: *interlunia*; the period of the dark moon when it is between the earth and sun</note>, and squares <note>An astrological aspect of 90 degrees, usually indicating tension or challenge</note> in the locations of eclipses increase their effects. The same is true in locations configured by a trine aspect <note>A harmonious 120-degree angle between celestial bodies</note>. Conversely, they diminish the effects if they are not in agreement. Similarly, the planets and fixed stars that agree by dignity <note>A planet's "dignity" is its strength or influence based on its specific position in the zodiac</note>, or by aspect, or by rising, or by being at a cardinal point <note>One of the four "pivots" of the sky: the horizon or the meridian</note> at that time, increase the effect—especially if they emerge from the sun's rays <note>When a planet becomes visible to the eye after being obscured by the sun's brightness</note>, or are stationary <note>When a planet appears to stop in the sky before changing direction</note>, or are rising. On the other hand, they diminish the effects.

## On the types of things to be affected.

### ARTICLE IV.

The type of things to be affected is known from the nature of the sign in the place of the eclipse <note>original: *deliquij*; literally a "failing" or "waning" of light</note>, or in the cardinal place preceding and following the eclipse, or in the place of the eclipse itself. Likewise, it is known from the nature of the fixed stars and the wandering stars <note>The planets</note> dominant during the eclipse or at a cardinal point.

## On the signs that cause effects.

### ARTICLE V.

1. The nature of a sign is determined, first, by whether it is masculine, feminine, diurnal <note>active by day</note>, nocturnal <note>active by night</note>, equinoctial, tropical, fixed, common, commanding, obeying, beholding, or of whatever triplicity <note>The grouping of signs by the four elements: Fire, Earth, Air, and Water</note> it may be.

Second, consider the form of the sign in which the eclipse occurs, and in which the stars ruling the eclipsed location are found. For if it is of human form <note>such as Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius</note>, the effect will be upon humans; if of a wild beast <note>original: *feralis*; such as Leo</note>, upon wild animals; if winged, upon birds; if a reptile, upon snakes and crawling things. **Cancer** [♋] indeed acts upon northern sea creatures, **Capricorn** [♑] upon southern ones, **Delphinus** <note>The constellation of the Dolphin</note> upon the waters and fleets; **Aquarius** [♒] and **Pisces** [♓] upon rivers and springs. **Argo** <note>The constellation of the Ship</note> acts upon both.

Third, if the eclipse and its rulers are in the vernal equinox—that is, in **Aries** [♈]—they indicate effects upon fruits, figs, birds, flowers, crops, and buds. If in the solstice of **Cancer** [♋], upon the perception and gathering—

## *Concerning the Ruling Planets and Fixed Stars regarding the nature of the effect.*

### ARTICLE VI.

1 Which wandering star <term>wandering star|A planet, as opposed to the 'fixed stars' which do not move relative to each other</term> is joined in more ways to the location of the eclipse and the cardinal point <note>The most influential points of an astrological chart, such as the horizon or the highest point in the sky</note> is the ruler of the eclipse’s conjunction. In the first place of importance is an "application" <note>When a faster planet approaches an aspect with a slower one</note>; second is "separation" <note>original: *defluxus*; when a planet moves away from an aspect</note>, whether by physical body or by its light; thirdly, opposition; fourthly, a square <note>A challenging 90-degree angle</note>. I say this regarding contrary aspects, but in similar ones, the trine <note>A harmonious 120-degree angle</note> and sextile <note>A 60-degree angle</note> are used. Fifthly, the antiscia <note>A point mirrored across the solstice axis</note>. Sixthly, equidistance. Seventhly, rulership—specifically in this order: house, triplicity, exaltation, and term <note>These are the "essential dignities" or layers of influence a planet has based on its specific degree in the zodiac</note>.

2 The planet that has more power at the location of the eclipse and at a cardinal point is the most powerful; second is the one that has power only at the location of the eclipse. If indeed two planets dominate equally in these respects, then preference is given to the one that prevails in dignity, or by being at a cardinal point, or by its sect <note>Whether the planet is more naturally suited to day or night</note> and association. A planet in direct motion is not preferred over one in retrograde <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky</note> except when predicting good outcomes.

3 Among the fixed stars, preference is given to the one that sits near the location of the eclipse, or at the preceding or following cardinal point. Usually, the preceding angle is preferred. This is more true for the fixed stars; but for the planets, the following angle is preferred, because they move in the order of the signs. We discussed in the first book how many ways the cardinal points relate to the Luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note>, whether before and after, or together in an angle. Remember, however, to prefer the planet that is in a better angle and aspect, and which is visible—first those that are oriental to the Sun <note>Rising before the Sun</note>, then those that are occidental <note>Setting after the Sun</note>.

The Tropical signs <note>Cancer and Capricorn</note> signify changes in the air and in public affairs...

...of customs and laws. In the tropical signs <note>Cancer and Capricorn, marking the solstices</note>, however, heat and cold are extreme; these have great power over the air and produce actual changes in the state of mind by affecting the senses and the appetite. Because these signs are in "square" <note>at a 90-degree angle</note> to the equinoxes, they tend to change the laws that were established under them.

2 Fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note> preside over the foundation and substructure of buildings, cities, and similar durable things, because they are stable by nature. But bicorporeal <term>bicorporeal|Double-bodied signs, such as Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces, which represent transitions between seasons</term> signs preside over men, kings, and magistrates. This is especially true of Sagittarius <note>original: ♐︎</note> because of its half-beast, half-human form. However, they are not necessarily wicked in this way, even though they are "double" in Virgo <note>original: ♍︎</note> and Gemini <note>original: ♊︎</note>.

3 An eclipse <term>deliquium|A Latin term for an eclipse, literally meaning a 'failing' or 'fainting' of light</term> occurring in the eastern angle <note>The Ascendant or the eastern horizon</note> indicates effects upon youth, the first fruits of the season, and the beginnings of projects and buildings. In the middle of heaven <note>The Medium Coeli, or the highest point in the sky</note>, it affects kings, temples, and those in the prime of life. In the west <note>The Descendant or western horizon</note>, it concerns the elderly, ancestors, the dead, ancient things, and changes to statutes and laws.

## On the magnitude of the effect.
### ARTICLE VIII.

1 The magnitude of the eclipse indicates the magnitude of its effects. For if the Moon is totally eclipsed, the entire class of things is affected; if half, then half; likewise, many, few, or a moderate number will be affected, according to the proportion of the eclipse.

2 The condition of the configured stars shows the same: for "evening" stars <note>Planets that set after the Sun</note> in relation to a solar eclipse, and "morning" stars <note>Planets that rise before the Sun</note> in relation to a lunar one, have little power and affect only a few. On the contrary, they have great power and affect many when the opposite is true. Likewise, the rulers in diameter <note>in direct opposition, 180 degrees apart</note> to the eclipse affect half of the class of things. Those in the exact place of the eclipse affect more than half—increasingly so the more they are "oriental" <note>rising in the east</note> from the Sun and "occidental" <note>setting in the west</note> from the Moon. Conversely, the effect is less for those who are more oriental from the Moon and occidental from the Sun.

...and the planets are the qualifiers <term>qualificatores|Planets or stars that determine the specific nature or "quality" of an astrological effect</term>: to whom they commit the right of governance and the "interregnum" <note>An interim period of rule; here it refers to the period during which the planet's influence is dominant</note>, and who, by their own nature and the nature of those things committed to them, define the outcome. The first lord governs the first rank, and the second lord the second. We call that planet the "first" which rules over the place of the eclipse <term>deliquium|A failing or eclipse of light</term> and the pivot point <term>cardo|One of the four "angles" or most powerful points in an astrological chart: the East, West, Zenith, or Nadir</term>. The "second" is that which both rules a pivot point and casts an aspect toward it. The "third" is that which casts an aspect but does not rule. But if no planet aspects the point, the first lord shall be the one who rules the place of the eclipse; the second, the one who rules the pivot point; and the third, the lord of the places where the aforementioned rulers are located.

3   Furthermore, the fixed stars, being similar to the planets, determine effects just as they do. One must consider not only the planets, but also the fixed stars, and the "missions" <note>The specific influence or "sending" of power from a star</note> of both, choosing those most suited to the locations. They align not only by ray <note>aspect</note> and rulership, but also by conjunction, equal ascension, antiscia <term>antiscia|A point of 'reflection' across the solstice axis; planets in these positions were thought to have a hidden connection</term>, and equidistance: whether in the same "circle of position" by body or aspect; or if they rise together, set together, culminate <note>reach the highest point in the sky</note>, or reach the bottom of the sky <note>original: iment</note>, or are positioned in opposition or any other configuration.

4   Therefore, when **Saturn** alone is the ruler, he generally corrupts through cold. Specifically regarding humans, he causes long-lasting diseases, wasting, withering, ill humors, fluxes, quartan fevers <note>A fever, often malarial, that returns every third day</note>, and afflictions; furthermore, he brings about exile, poverty, distress, terrors, and deaths, especially of the elderly. He kills animals useful to man and similar creatures; he renders herbs and fruits that are useful to us sickly, so that those who eat them fall ill. In the air, he stirs up a horrid, icy, foggy, and pestilential cold, bringing storms, thick clouds, gloom, and harmful rather than healthy snows; he generates serpents. In the sea and rivers, he brings winter storms, shipwrecks, difficult voyages, and the scarcity or death of fish, as well as floods, whirlpools, and the corruption of waters. On land, he brings high prices, scarcity, and devastation of crops—especially those useful to man—and sends forth caterpillars, locusts, floods, the force of rainstorms, and hail; from these come famine and disease, by which men perish.

5   **Jupiter**, when ruling alone, generally provides gentle warmth and moisture, conferring growth upon all things. Specifically holding power over men, he bestows glory, friendships, tranquility, and peace; he increases the family estate, composes both body and mind, and confers gifts and benefits from rulers—whom he also increases, adorns, and makes magnanimous. He is the author of universal happiness. He gives an abundance and high quality of animals useful to us, and brings death or weakness to those that are useless. He makes the seasons healthy with winds and rains that nourish the earth, along with beautiful clear skies; he brings good fortune to the voyages of fleets and an abundance of crops, acting in direct opposition to the decrees of Saturn.

# BOOK TWO

6 **Mars**, when he rules alone during an interim period <note>original: "interregnat." In astrology, this refers to a planet taking temporary command over a specific period of time</note>, corrupts through intense heat. Specifically, he rages against men with wars, seditions, imprisonment, the destruction of populations, plebeian riots, and the wrath of princes; through these, he brings about unexpected deaths. He causes burning fevers, tertian fevers <note>A fever that returns every third day, often associated with malaria in the Renaissance</note>, eruptions of blood, acute diseases, and violent deaths, especially for those in the prime of manhood. Likewise, from his influence come violence, insults, injuries, fires, homicides, robberies, and banditry. In the air, he creates hot, pestilential, and wasting winds, as well as lightning, flames, and parching drought. At sea, he causes sudden sinkings of ships through turbulent winds, lightning, and the like. He swallows up rivers, dries up springs, and fouls the waters. He either kills animals useful to us and the fruits and crops intended for our use while they are in the bud—before they are even gathered—through dreadful heat, or destroys those already harvested through fire and plundering.

7 **Venus** alone generally produces the same effects as **Jupiter**, but with a certain charm. Specifically, she brings fame to men, along with honors, joys, and fruitful years. She grants fortunate marriages, an abundance of children, grace in unions, the increase of goods, a clean way of living, and the pleasing friendships of the powerful and of princes. Likewise, she grants physical beauty, integrity, veneration, and respect. She fills the air with temperate, moist, and most fertile winds, providing pleasant weather, serenity, and the timely arrival of rains; she grants ships happy voyages and profitable outcomes. She fills the channels of rivers. She provides an abundance, growth, convenience, and goodness of useful animals and crops.

8 **Mercury**, generally acting as the sole regent, behaves according to the nature of the star with which he is most closely configured <term>configured|The relative position or "aspect" of one planet to another, which modifies their combined influence</term>. Nevertheless, he is by his own nature entirely impetuous. Specifically regarding men, he is sharp, effective, and adaptable to whatever circumstances present themselves. He is a patron of banditry, theft, and piratical invasion; he is the stirrer of contrary winds. When configured with "malefics" <note>Planets traditionally considered harmful, such as Mars or Saturn</note>, he is the author of diseases, drought, daily fevers, gasping coughs, and wasting sickness. Likewise, he governs priestly accounts, divine worship, and royal revenues; he also brings about changes in laws and customs in his own time—all of which align with those things mentioned and the mixture of the other stars. He stirs up turbulent, vehement, and unstable winds, and causes dryness, mobility, and shifting in the air, especially because he is near the Sun and swift in his course. He sends forth flaming thunders, shakes and scatters the earth, and rouses lightning; for this reason, he is sometimes destructive to animals and useful crops. He dries up the rivers when he is setting <note>original: "occidens"</note> and fills them when he is rising <note>original: "oriens"</note>.

9 Therefore, just as a **beneficent** star <note>original: "benefica," referring to planets like Jupiter and Venus</note> favors us and those things dedicated to our use, but harms hostile things and men who are estranged from a right temperament (namely, the barbarians), so a **malefic** star <note>original: "malefica," referring to planets like Saturn and Mars</note> harms us and things useful to us, while favoring things that are contrary and harmful.

10 For the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note> and the **Star** <note>original: *, likely a shorthand for the Sun or the primary luminary in this context</note> are like magistrates; **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> and **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> are like friends who rule in their absence <note>original: "interregnant"</note>; **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> and **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> are like rebels and tyrants; **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> is in the middle, yet he has the specific duties already mentioned, though they are lesser. The evils from less prevailing malefic stars are smaller, just as the goods from less powerful beneficent stars are smaller, and vice versa.

11 When a star is found in its **peculiar nature** <term>peculiar nature: the inherent characteristics of a planet when it is in its strongest or most natural state</term>, effects of a similar nature follow it, as we have said; where it is mixed with others, the effects are mixed.

12 **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the "Tetrabiblos," the foundational text for Western astrology</note> calls a nature "peculiar" under these conditions: First, if it rules alone. Second, if it is in its own state and condition (such as being a masculine, diurnal planet in a masculine sign and rising in the east from the **Sun**). Third, if it rises with the **Sun**. Fourth, if it is above the earth and setting from the **Sun**. Fifth, if it is below the earth and rising from the **Sun** during the day. Sixth, if it is below the earth and rising in the night. Seventh, if it is below the earth and setting.

13 The status of the **Planets** is considered in five ways: namely, in relation to the **Sun**, to the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, to the fixed stars, to the nature of the signs and their own lordship over them, and by the logic of the world—that is, the quarters, the angles <note>original: "cardinum," the four pivotal points of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli</note>, and by latitude, as was said in the first book.

14 The powers arising from the mixture of Planets and fixed stars, and from their "passions" <note>In this context, "passions" refers to how planets are modified by their celestial environment</note>, along with the ruling Planet and the rules of mixing, are infinite. These are left to the judgment of the **Astrologer**, who will attribute more weight to those factors that are more numerous and more powerful, and will blend them accordingly.

And indeed, peace was made near the time of the eclipse. In the year 1613, an eclipse occurred at 10 degrees **Gemini** <note>original: ♊</note> and harshly troubled two friends who have the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note> as their apheta there, though one was at the opposite point in **Sagittarius** <note>original: ♐</note>. **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> was ruling, found at the end of the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M.C."</note> in the first degree of **Cancer** <note>original: ♋</note>, in **square** <note>an astrological aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</note> to **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> existing at the start of **Aries** <note>original: ♈</note>. There followed the ruin of merchants, scribes, accountants, and officials, as well as prison, exiles, legal briefs, and accusations; the decreed time for these even still lasts. Daily I experience that very many things decreed by eclipses are true.

5 Therefore, in a fruitful place, those who have their aphetas in **opposition** to the eclipses are affected more. Thirdly, those in **squares**. But in a **trine** or **sextile** configuration <note>harmonious astrological aspects of 120 and 60 degrees respectively</note>, things will be well, or at least not bad. If the eclipse is malefic, judge nonetheless according to the apheta's conditions, whether they are in agreement or discord. Truly, men are not affected unless the eclipse appears above their own horizon, or if they are citizens of a city affected by the eclipse, as Haly maintains.

6 It must be known that the privation of light takes something away, from which comes either a balance and happiness, or an imbalance.
