<header>ASTROLOGICAL MATTERS</header>

2 The locations of the inquiries <note>That is, the twelve "Houses" of the zodiac, each representing a different area of life.</note> are as follows. In the **ascendant** <note>original: "horoscopo". The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note> we inquire about temperament, bodily qualities, size, and about those things that happen to the body or are endured by it, such as travels, diseases, and health. In the **second house**, the Arabs place riches, by which the body is preserved. In the **third** are short journeys, siblings, and religion in part. However, **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the most influential astronomer and astrologer of antiquity.</note> considers siblings from the significators of the mother in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M.C." or Medium Coeli, the highest point in the chart.</note>. In the **fourth**, the Arabs treat parents and hidden or underground matters, such as treasure, prison, agriculture, and terrestrial affairs. In the **fifth**, the Arabs seek information regarding embassies, children, and joys. Ptolemy treats children later, in the **eleventh**. In the **sixth** they seek information on diseases, servants, and animals. In the **seventh**, concerning the wife, enemies, absence, and the ends of things. In the **eighth**, concerning death and inheritance. In the **ninth**, concerning religion, long journeys, knowledge, dreams, etc. In the **tenth**, concerning occupation, honor, actions, friends, children, the mother, kings, temples, and illustrious business. In the **eleventh**, concerning friends, children, and benefits. In the **twelfth**, concerning servants, diseases, and enemies: because it does not form an "aspect" <note>A geometric relationship between points in the sky.</note> with the ascendant, and vapors cloud it, just as they do the eighth, continually: for which reason the refraction of the sight of a star at the 30th degree above the horizon decreases greatly according to **Tycho** <note>Tycho Brahe (1546–1601), the Danish astronomer known for his highly accurate observations.</note>, whereas previously it was always thought to increase. The rest are evident from the nature of their positions.

3 But one must also consult the **Planets**. For indeed, the **Sun** signifies glory and dignity. Likewise, the father, the king, and the husband. The **Moon**, however, signifies the wife, the mother, the soul, the senses and their conditions, and travels; and from her we take the beginning of fortune, as she decides concerning riches. From **Saturn** we seek hidden things, stubbornness of mind, perseverance, the father, and slow, long-lasting, and very deep business: as even **Saint Thomas** <note>Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274), the influential theologian who integrated Aristotelian philosophy and some astrological concepts into Christian thought.</note> taught in the first part <note>A reference to the *Summa Theologiae*, Pars Prima.</note> by arguing from the position and motion of Saturn. From **Jupiter**, we seek information on integrity, simplicity, and happiness. From **Mars**, on fortitude, journeys, anger, cruelty, luxury, the manner of intercourse, ambition, and pride. From **Venus**, on love, luxury, and the mother. From **Mercury**, on intelligence, prudence, cunning, trade, and learning. From the **Moon**, promptness, instability, and also honors.

4 Yet these are not the primary significators in all things: for in the more serious doctrines, **Saturn** is considered; in eloquence, **Jupiter**; in beauty, **Venus**; in sharp disputation, **Mars** with **Mercury**; in majesty, the **Sun**. These are considered within the same inquiry. Thus, in other matters, all planets participate.

5 That this doctrine is true is persuaded not only by symbolic reasoning, and by **Saint Thomas** with **Albert** <note>Albertus Magnus (c. 1200–1280), teacher of Aquinas and a proponent of "natural" astrology.</note>, but also by **Jacob the Patriarch**, who

...in the Sun and Moon and eleven stars bowing down to Joseph, he interpreted the father, mother, and brothers. Indeed, there are these many planets in the heavens, if you count the attendants <note>original: "asseclas." A reference to the newly discovered moons (satellites) of the planets.</note> of Jupiter and Saturn. There are also the two Luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note>. For the Moon is a Luminary to us, but not to those on Jupiter <note>original: "iouialibus." The author suggests the Moon's light is specific to Earth's perspective.</note>.

6 Happiness and unhappiness of the outcome in an inquiry is known from the condition and state of the ruling planets: for example, whether it is a **benefic** <note>A "good" planet, like Jupiter or Venus.</note> or a **malefic** <note>A "bad" planet, like Saturn or Mars.</note>; whether it favors the inquiry or opposes it; whether it is **direct**, **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky.</note>, **combust** <note>Weakened by being too close to the Sun.</note>, rising in the morning, or setting in the evening; and whether it is in its "dignity" <note>A place in the zodiac where a planet has more power.</note> of **House** (which prevails in life), **Exaltation** (which prevails in honors), **Trigon** <note>Also called Triplicity.</note> (which prevails in magistracy, fortune, and friends), or **Term** (which prevails in daily business), or if it is outside of its dignity, etc.

7 Timing is known specifically from **direction** <note>A technique of "advancing" a planet's position to predict when an event will happen.</note>: but generally, planets in an **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses—the most powerful positions in a chart.</note> are fast, especially at the beginning; in **succedent** houses <note>The houses following the angles: 2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th.</note>, they are moderate; in **cadent** houses <note>The "falling" houses: 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th.</note>, they are slow. Those that are **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> from the Sun and the world are fast; **occidental** <note>Setting after the Sun.</note> are slow; as are those in the morning and evening. Likewise, timing is judged from the actual speed and slowness of a planet in its own motion.

8 The magnitude and weakness of an effect is learned from the strength of the planets. For instance, if they are in their dignity, oriental, in the angles, or surrounded by a "retinue" <note>original: "satellitio."</note> of friendly planets and fixed stars, and the opposite. Therefore, the **significator** indicates the essence of the inquiry, the **governor** indicates the quality, the **planet in aspect** indicates the fortune and magnitude, the **place** indicates the subject, the **site** indicates the time, and the **power** indicates the magnitude and verification.

# Concerning the parents of the newborn.
## CHAPTER II. ARTICLE I.

1 Astrologers are accustomed to inquire first about the parents, although they are to be known by a weak investigation <note>Meaning it is difficult to determine precise details about parents from a child's birth chart alone.</note>; and this we shall do following **Ptolemy**, their leader.

2 From the **Sun** (☉) and **Saturn** (♄), the status of the father—whether good or bad—is signified; the mother’s status is signified by the **Moon** (☽) and **Venus** (♀). This is either because the Sun signifies by day and Venus by night, while Saturn and the Moon are their [respective] significators; or because one planet alone is not enough to judge regarding those who are firm in age.

3 Indeed, the birth of children signifies future things for parents and siblings: because the generative power is an indicator of itself, and consequently of its origins [the parents] and its co-effects (that is, the siblings) and its effects (that is, the children).

4 The status of the parents follows their own **genesis** <note>The parents' own original birth charts.</note>; then the firstborn...

...born: then the second-born, and so on in order: and the infancy of the children follows the nativity <note>original: "genesim." Once the son is separated from this unity, or if he dies, that indication ceases. On the other hand, a very distinguished status of children draws the parents and brothers toward it: just as Joseph’s status drew Jacob and his sons. And my own tribulations afflicted my father, my brothers, and my sisters along with me. <note>The author likely refers to his own long imprisonment and trials, which brought suffering to his entire family.</note>

5 All things that are made one in some way—such as fathers and sons, wife and husband, or friend with friend—suffer good or evil from the same causes. Those who do not suffer together <note>original: "compatiuntur," meaning to feel or endure together.</note> at the same time are not truly friends according to nature. This is evident in twins born with similar faces, actions, and fortunes, as I myself have witnessed three times. History also bears witness to this with the holy twin brothers Gervasius and Protasius, and likewise Cosmas and Damian, who were equal in life, death, and fortune. This principle fails in part regarding Jacob and Esau, as we shall soon discuss; we will provide the causes for this from the mystery of God and from nature, following Saint Thomas. <note>A reference to Thomas Aquinas, who discussed why twins like Jacob and Esau could have such different lives despite similar births.</note>

6 The Luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> surrounded by a retinue <note>original: "satellitio." However, if they are surrounded by malefic planets <note>Saturn or Mars.</note> or are in a weak position, they decree a poor status.

7 The Luminaries looking upon each other with "hostile" aspects <note>Specifically the square (90°) or opposition (180°) aspects, which were traditionally viewed as tense or conflicting.</note> indicate enmity between the parents; and if they are in a hostile aspect with the horoscope <note>The Ascendant or the 1st House of the birth chart.</note>, they indicate enmity with the newborn.

8 If, in the retinue of the Sun, it happens that Saturn is in the Moon's place and Venus is eastern in her own person or in the angles <note>The most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th.</note>, the status of the parents is most happy. If, however, the attendants are present but are of different "sects" <note>Astrological "sect" divides planets into day and night groups; mixing them was often thought to lessen their effectiveness.</note>—such as when Mars is carried toward the Sun and Saturn toward the Moon—or if they are benefics but not happily situated, the status of the parents is mediocre and inconsistent. Well-disposed malefic planets produce the same mediocre result.

9 If, however, the Sun is surrounded by no stars and is "void of course" <note>A term for a planet that completes its path through a zodiac sign without making contact with any other planets.</note> and outside of the angles, it signifies a lowly status for the father. The same applies to the Moon regarding the mother.

10 The Part of Fortune <note>A calculated mathematical point in a chart representing luck and material success.</note> in a good aspect with the Sun and Moon delivers the paternal inheritance by hand. In a hostile aspect with them, or with the attendants of the Sun and Moon, it denies the inheritance or will make it harmful to the child. Likewise, if the Part of Fortune is "under the rays" of the Sun <note>Combust, or so close to the Sun that its influence is burned away.</note>, the child will not enjoy the inheritance; but if it is under the Moon's influence, he will enjoy it more.

11 If Jupiter or Venus are configured with the Sun or Saturn in any way... <note>original: "configurantur," continued on the next page.</note>

## ->Concerning brothers and sisters.<-

### ->ARTICLE II.<-

1 The Moon by night, Venus by day, and the lord of the Midheaven <note>original: "medii caeli"; the highest point in the chart</note> are the indicators of the mother. If these are configured with many beneficial planets and in bicorporeal signs, they grant more brothers and double their number. If, however, the harmful planets—especially when mixed with the Sun—should damage one of the stated places, they kill the brothers: Saturn rising in the East [kills] the older ones; Mars setting in the West [kills] the younger ones. Being "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun</note> in the world and the Sun indicates males; being "occidental" <note>setting after the Sun</note> indicates females.

2 Benefactors of brothers who are well-situated in relation to the world and the Sun grant illustrious brothers.

3 If a beneficial benefactor agrees with the lord of the mother's place—that is, with the Moon, Venus, and the lord of the Midheaven—the brothers will be in agreement; if not, the opposite.

4 Similarly, if the benefactors and the <term>lot of fortune</term> <note>a calculated mathematical point in a chart representing luck and prosperity</note> agree among themselves, they will live together; if they are in disagreeing signs, <term>antiscia</term> <note>points on the zodiac that are reflections of each other across the solstice axis</note>, and opposites, then the contrary [is true].

5 Place the benefactor of the brother in the ascendant and draw the chart, as you did for the parents, and do so for more [siblings] if there are more.

BOOK FOUR.

## On Sex.

### CHAPTER III. ARTICLE I.

1 A male will be born if the place of the Sun and Moon, and the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: "horoscopi"; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, and their masters, are masculine; if feminine, a female [will be born], or one who is soft and effeminate.

2 Masculinity is known from the nature of the planet, and from its <term>oriental</term> <note>rising before the Sun</note> position relative to the Sun and the world; for there, feminine planets become masculine, just as in an <term>occidental</term> <note>setting after the Sun</note> position, masculine planets become feminine.

3 These decrees are more certain from the chart of conception, and clearer from the chart of birth.

---

->*Concerning the birth of twins.*<-

### ARTICLE II.

1 If the Sun, the Moon, and the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: "horoscopus"</note>, and the masters of those places are in <term>bicorporeal signs</term> <note>double-bodied signs such as Gemini, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, several children will be born, or two. For if other planets are mixed in, there will be more. Likewise, the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "Medium cœli"; the highest point of the chart</note> being bicorporeal signifies the same as the ascendant.

2 Three males are attributed to Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars: like the three Horatii and the three Curiatii in the writings of Livy <note>Livy was a Roman historian who recorded the legendary duel between two sets of triplets, the Horatii of Rome and the Curiatii of Alba Longa</note>. Three females are attributed to the Moon, Venus, and Mercury in an "effeminate" state: like the three Graces. Two males and one female are attributed to Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus: like Castor, Pollux, and Helen <note>In Greek mythology, these siblings were born from eggs after Leda was visited by Zeus</note>. One male and two females are attributed to Mars, Venus, and the Moon: like Dionysus, Ceres, and Isis.

3 Those born in other combinations do not survive, because no other mixture of planets can produce a vital life. According to Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, an influential 2nd-century astronomer and astrologer</note>, no more than three live. Legal experts <note>original: "Iuris-Consulti"</note> even grant life to as many as five; I do not believe this without evidence.

4 Often twins do not survive; or they are subject to notable physical marks or sudden, miraculous accidents. They have a graying back and a retracted <term>sacrum</term> <note>the triangular bone at the base of the spine</note>.

5 Therefore, one can be good and the other wicked; one may live and the other die, because they are influenced by two contrary planets. In this way, the doubt concerning Jacob and Esau <note>Biblical twins who struggled in the womb and had opposite destinies</note> can be resolved, in virtue of the stars carrying out God's ordination. This is what Saint Thomas <note>Thomas Aquinas, the medieval theologian</note> attributed to the different positions of their hearts toward the

### ARTICLE III.

1 If the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and the Moon</note> fall away from the <term>angles</term> <note>the four most powerful points of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, being unconnected to the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: "horoscopo"</note>, and <term>malefic planets</term> <note>Saturn and Mars</note> are in the angles (especially the 1st and 10th), and if neither the ruler nor the location of the preceding New or Full Moon is joined by any relationship to the place of the Moon, the ascendant, or the master of the birth chart, then a "monster" <note>In this period, "monster" referred to any infant born with significant physical deformities or "monstrous" features</note> will be born, contorted or entangled.

2 If, moreover, the Luminaries are in <term>quadruped</term> <note>four-footed signs like Aries, Taurus, Leo, or Sagittarius</note> or wild-beast signs, the child will not have a human form.

3 If also no <term>benefic planets</term> <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> testify to the Luminaries, but only malefics do, the child will be utterly alien to human form, wild, and malicious.

4 If, however, Jupiter or Venus testifies, the child will have the form of animals sacred to the Gods, such as a cat, a monkey, or a dog; in modern terms, you might say animals familiar to humanity.

5 If Mercury testifies, it will have the form of animals devoted to human use, such as pigs, birds, goats, and so on.

6 If the Luminaries are in <term>human signs</term> <note>signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius</note> within the aforementioned arrangement, then the child will have a human form, though modified according to the signs of the Luminaries and the centers occupied by the malefic planets.

7 If no benefic planet testifies, the child will furthermore be mute and monstrous.

### *On those who are not raised.*
### ARTICLE IV.

1. If either of the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>The Sun or the Moon</note> is in an <term>angle</term> <note>the four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note> and is in <term>conjunction</term>, <term>opposition</term>, or a precise <term>square</term> <note>astrological aspects of 0°, 180°, and 90°</note> with a malefic planet, and the ruler of the Luminaries is held in the places of the malefics, and no <term>benefic</term> <note>planets like Jupiter and Venus, thought to have a helpful influence</note> planet gazes upon them, the newborn shall not survive, nor shall they be raised.
2. Similarly, a child is not raised if two malefics are configured toward one or both of the Luminaries—not necessarily precisely, but by <term>application</term> <note>moving toward an exact aspect</note>; or if one malefic affects one Luminary precisely and another affects the other in succession; or if one malefic strikes both through conjunction and opposition at the same time, or two malefics, and so on. Understand this to apply if no benefic planet gazes upon them and the configuration is in the angles.
3. Mars significantly harms the Sun by succession—that is, applying in conjunction—and the Moon in opposition. Conversely, Saturn harms the Sun more in opposition and <term>elevation</term> <note>occupying a more dominant position in the sky</note>, and the Moon in conjunction. This is especially true where these malefics are joined to the rulers of the Luminaries' locations.
4. If the two Luminaries are opposite each other in angles at different <term>latitudes</term> <note>the distance of a planet north or south of the ecliptic</note>, or joined in the same latitude with malefics, the offspring is pulled out half-alive or dead.
5. In the same constellation, if the Luminaries move away from the body or ray of the benefics and apply to the malefics, the child will survive for as many months, days, or hours as there are degrees between the Luminary and the malefic.

### CHAPTER IV. ARTICLE I.

1. We search in vain for the events of a life unless we first know the duration of that life.

2. Life is diagnosed by the <term>aphetic place</term> <note>original: *apheticus locus*; the specific point in a birth chart that "releases" or determines the life force</note>, by its rulers, and by the "killers." <note>original: *interfectoribus*; planets or points that signify the end of life</note>

3. There are five governors of life: the Sun, the Moon, the horoscope, the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>original: *pars fortunae*; a mathematical point in the chart representing the native's physical well-being and luck</note>, and the ruler of these locations.

<margin>hour 5.</margin>

4. The <term>aphetic</term> locations are five: the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: *medium cœli*; the highest point of the sky at birth</note>, the horoscope, and the 11th, 7th, and 9th houses, according to the order given. The remaining houses, because they are not connected to the horoscope and are occupied by vapors, are useless. Similarly, those houses under the earth are useless, because they cannot give life from there—since life is the "day" of the living person—nor can a signifier determine anything regarding life from those places, although the Arabs think otherwise.

5. A house contains five degrees before the <term>cusp</term> <note>the boundary line between two astrological houses</note> and twenty-five degrees after it.

6. There are always several <term>aphetas</term> <note>life-givers</note> in those who grow to maturity; the person who has only one is weak.

## On the selection of the *Apheta*, the primary governor of life.

### ARTICLE II.

1 **By** day, the Sun is chosen first if it is in any of the five <term>aphetic</term> <note>original: *apheticus*; relating to the "Apheta," the planet or point in a birth chart that determines life and its length</note> places. Second, the Moon is chosen if the Sun is not in an aphetic place. Third, a planet is chosen that has three out of the five <term>dignities</term> <note>original: *dignitates*; systems of planetary power based on zodiacal position: house, triplicity, exaltation, term, and aspect</note> in the location of the Sun, the <term>horoscope</term> <note>original: *horoscopus*; here referring specifically to the Ascendant, the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, and the preceding <term>new moon</term> <note>original: *interlunium*; the conjunction of the Sun and Moon</note> (if a new moon preceded the birth). To these dignities, <term>antiscia</term> <note>original: *antiscium*; zodiacal points that mirror each other across the solstice axis</note> and equal distances are also counted. Fourth, if even this planet is not suitable, the horoscope itself shall become the principal <term>apheta</term> <note>original: *apheta*; also known as the "Giver of Life" or *Hyleg*</note>.

2 At night, the Moon is chosen first if it is in an aphetic place. Second, the Sun is chosen if it is within 25 degrees below the horoscope. Third, a planet is chosen which has three out of the five dignities in the places of the Moon, the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>original: *fortuna*; a calculated mathematical point in the chart representing prosperity and physical well-being</note>, and the preceding <term>full moon</term> <note>original: *plenilunium*; the opposition of the Sun and Moon</note>—specifically in the place of the <term>Luminary</term> <note>original: *Luminare*; the Sun or the Moon</note> which is above the earth, provided a full moon preceded the birth.

3 But if a new moon preceded at night, take the horoscope. If a full moon preceded and no planet can be the governor, choose the Part of Fortune if it is in an aphetic place. If not, choose the horoscope.

4 If the Sun, the Moon, and the governor are all in aphetic places, prefer the one that has the most dominion, provided they are all in equally aphetic positions. For indeed, if the Sun is in the 9th house and the Moon is in the 10th, even by day, the Moon is chosen—so long as the Sun is not the lord of the time. If the Sun is in the 11th and the Moon is in the 10th, they are equal due to the prerogative of daytime. Therefore, the one who has greater dignity or <term>testimony</term> <note>original: *testimonium*; a supportive relationship or "aspect" from another planet</note> from the governor is preferred. Thus, at night, the Sun in the 1st house is preferred to the Moon being in the 9th or 7th, because, etc.

5 When the governor is the lord of both times, it is preferred over the Sun and Moon, provided it is in a better aphetic place. To have "dominion over both times" means to have dignity in the places of the Sun, the Moon, the horoscope, and the preceding full moon or new moon.

6 The <term>Lord of the Nativity</term> <note>original: *Dominus genituræ*; the planet with the most overall power in the entire birth chart</note>, who is the most powerful of the planets, strengthens life; however, it does not measure the length of life (as the <term>Arabs</term> <note>original: *Arabes*; referring to the medieval Islamic astrologers whose works were central to European astrology</note> believe) unless it is also the principal apheta.

## *On the measurement of life through the direction of the apheta to the killers.*

### ARTICLE III.

1 There are two types of <term>direction</term> <note>original: *directio*; a symbolic method where degrees of planetary movement are equated to years of life</note>. One is **direct**, through which the <term>interfector</term> <note>original: *interfector*; literally "the killer," the planet or point that signifies the end of life</note> is led to the apheta following the natural order of the zodiac signs, such as the space between the <term>midheaven</term> <note>original: *medium cœli*; the highest point of the chart</note> and the <term>horoscope</term> <note>original: *horoscopus*; the Ascendant or eastern horizon</note>. The other is **converse**, moving against the succession of the signs, because the apheta is led toward the <term>anaereta</term> <note>original: *anæreten*; a Greek term for the "destroyer" or killing planet</note>. There is also another direct movement in the order of the signs, calculated according to the <term>ascensions</term> <note>original: *ascensiones*; the time it takes for a sign to rise over the horizon</note> of the apheta. **Saint Thomas** <note>Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274), a dominant theologian who integrated Aristotelian philosophy and some aspects of astrology into Christian thought</note> in Book 2 of *On Generation and Corruption* measures lifespans by this oblique motion.

2 Since the degree of the sign and its position in the world where the apheta is located is where it bestows and begins life for a human being living as an individual, it is necessary that when another planet arrives at that same physical position in the heavens, it must do something to that life—whether good or evil, depending on its own nature. It does this immediately at the start after one, two, three, or five hours, and so on. But it does not kill at that moment, because it is granted to a man to live as many years as there are degrees between the apheta and the <term>malefic</term> <note>original: *malefica*; a "bad" planet, usually Mars or Saturn</note> planet coming to its position. Nevertheless, the good and bad stars at that position necessarily affect the person born every single day, if one considers the matter well. From this, we can track down the apheta by observing its effects. It seems, therefore, that the apheta and the interfector **signify** life and death rather than **cause** them; otherwise, the planet would kill the person instantly when it reached the apheta’s position. Instead, death occurs only after as many years as there are degrees between them. This is because the interfector is no longer found in its original place, but rather the *degree* in which it once was has become lethal. Therefore, there is more **signification** than **causality** in this business—unless you wish to argue that the cause begins working from the start but does not finish the job until as many years have passed as there were degrees between them. Thus, it is true that we are always tending toward death. It is also a wonder that lower things, being in a motion of deficiency (which is essentially nothingness), can possess life. However, if the Earth is carried around a stationary Sun, as it seems to the <term>Pythagoreans</term> <note>A reference to the heliocentric (Sun-centered) model, which was often historically attributed to Pythagoras or Aristarchus</note>, then the calculation of the apheta toward the interfector will be exactly as we are commonly accustomed to measure it.

3 In the **converse** direction, on the other hand, the killing angle

It proceeds to the <term>apheta</term> <note>original: *aphetam*; the planet or celestial point that "releases" or governs the life force in a birth chart</note> contrary to what Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the foundational authority for Western astrology and astronomy</note> had said. And since while it is above the earth it gives life, when it is submerged [below the horizon], it indicates that life is buried. Moreover, it is submerged by the <term>diurnal motion</term> <note>original: *motu diurno*; the apparent daily rotation of the heavens around the Earth</note>; whence I also think that, even in the diurnal motion, whenever the place of the apheta falls into a malefic <note>original: *maleficum*; harmful or ill-omened</note> place, the person suffers some evil. I also believe that every hostile <term>aspect</term> <note>original: *aspectum hostilem*; specific geometric angles between planets, like 90 or 180 degrees, thought to cause tension</note> is malefic, as is any star found in a position encountering it against the natural order of the zodiac signs. And he who understands this will know every single day when good and bad things will encounter him from his <term>radical</term> <note>original: *locis radicalibus*; the original positions of planets at the moment of birth, the "root" of the person's fate</note> places. This is possible when the apheta reaches good and bad places against the order of the signs, and when bad and good influences encounter it according to that order.

### ARTICLE IV.

1 **In** <term>converse direction</term> <note>original: *directione conuersa*; a method of prediction where the planets are symbolically moved backwards against the order of the zodiac</note>, there is only one interfector: the <term>western angle</term> <note>original: *angulus occidentis*; the Descendant, or the point where the sun sets</note>. Therefore, no malefic planet located between the apheta and the western angle can kill. For the apheta goes toward that planet; it is not invaded by it. Only the angle itself has such power, because there the apheta, as it were, casts itself down from its life-giving position.

2 Therefore, stars placed between the apheta and the setting sun, or their rays [aspects], do not slay; rather, the <term>benefics</term> <note>original: *beneficæ*; helpful planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> add to the time of life, while the <term>malefics</term> <note>original: *maleficæ*; harmful planets like Saturn or Mars</note> take it away.

3 The number of time added or taken away is gathered from the position of each of the parts. For as many as the <term>seasonal hours</term> <note>original: *horaria tempora*; a system where the periods of daylight and night are divided into 12 hours each, meaning hours vary in length depending on the time of year</note> are—diurnal by day, nocturnal by night—so many years are signified. Indeed, when this number is at the rising [the eastern horizon], that is, with the apheta, it must be kept whole, but it must be diminished according to the proportion of its distance from the apheta toward the setting [the west], until at the moment of setting it is reduced to nothing.

4 Seasonal hours are the number of degrees and minutes of the <term>equator</term> <note>original: *æquatoris*</note> that rise in any given temporal hour. Moreover, astronomical hours are equal; but civil hours are unequal, being made from the <term>diurnal and nocturnal arcs</term> <note>original: *arcu diurno & nocturno*; the paths the sun takes above and below the horizon</note>—though they are unequal—each divided equally into six parts. And because some signs rise crookedly <note>original: *tortuosa*; signs of "short ascension" that take less time to rise</note> and others rise straight <note>original: *recta*; signs of "long ascension"</note>, more

### *On the killers and the times of killing in direct direction.*

## ARTICLE V.

1. In direct direction <note>original: *directione recta*; the calculation of planetary movement in the natural order of the zodiac signs</note> there are two killers <note>original: *interfectores*; planets that bring the end of life</note>: Saturn and Mars, and their opposite and square aspects <note>original: *aspectus oppositi, & quadrati*; geometric angles of 180 and 90 degrees, considered very stressful</note>. Therefore, there are six [possible killer points].

2. Meanwhile, the <term>antiscia</term> <note>original: *antiscia*; points of the zodiac that mirror each other across the solstice line</note> of the aforementioned malefics <note>original: *maleficarum*; "bad-doing" planets, usually Saturn and Mars</note> also kill, if they aspected the apheta from the beginning, when the direction reaches those points. Similarly, the equidistance in "obedient" and "commanding" [signs] <note>original: *obedientibus, & imperantibus*; pairs of zodiac signs that share the same distance from the equinoxes and thus have equal power</note>, provided they are not hindered by much latitude <note>original: *latitudinem*; the distance of a planet north or south of the ecliptic path</note>.

3. The "left square" of the apheta also kills according to the series of signs naturally in direction: since it occurs at the contrary sign and degree.

4. However, in signs of <term>short ascension</term> <note>original: *breuium ascensionum*; zodiac signs that take less time to rise over the horizon (Capricorn through Gemini in the Northern Hemisphere)</note> the <term>trine</term> <note>original: *trigonus*; a 120-degree aspect</note> of the malefics kills, and in <term>long ascension</term> <note>original: *longarum ascensionum*; signs that take longer to rise (Cancer through Sagittarius)</note> even the <term>sextile</term> <note>original: *sexagonus*; a 60-degree aspect</note>: since they are equivalent to a square, as was said in the first book: and this in its accidental ascending and descending part of the heaven itself.

5. When the Moon is the apheta, the position of the Sun also kills, if it was in a hostile aspect from the beginning, or imbued with the rays of malefics. If [imbued with the rays] of benefics <note>original: *beneficarum*; helpful planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it does not kill even in a hostile aspect.

## Various ways of escaping and confirming death, and bad events, from the various meetings of the malefics.

### ARTICLE VI.

1 It should be noted that the "hostile" rays <note>original: *radij hoſtiles*; referring to difficult geometric relationships between planets, such as squares or oppositions</note> of the **benefic planets** <note>original: *beneficiarum*; planets traditionally considered helpful or life-sustaining, primarily Jupiter and Venus</note> do not kill, nor do they harm, nor do they help; rather, they usually help only with difficulty. Likewise, the "friendly" aspects of the **malefic planets** <note>original: *maleficarum*; planets traditionally considered harmful, primarily Saturn and Mars</note> do not harm or help. However, they usually cause harm when they have cast a "bad look" <note>original: *malè aſpexerint*; formed a difficult aspect</note> from the start, and where they are equivalent to hostile rays.

2 If the **doctrine of Copernicus** <note>Nicolaus Copernicus (1473–1543), who proposed that the Earth moves around the Sun. The author is weighing how this new model affects astrological math.</note> is true, it is necessary to consider the aspects in the **Zodiac** <note>original: *Zodiaco*; the ecliptic circle, or the Sun's apparent path</note>, because it is a real circle in the heavens, whereas the **equator** is relative to the earth. This is why the Arabs indicate the aspects in the Zodiac and divide the "houses" <note>original: *domicilia*; the twelve segments of the sky used to determine different areas of life</note> there. If, however, **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century authority whose geocentric system was the standard for centuries</note> is more correct, the aspects are to be taken in the equator. Indeed, the followers of Ptolemy concede that they should always be taken in the Zodiac for every constellation and judgment. They say, however, that only in the "direction" <note>a method of moving a planet forward in time to predict events</note> of the **apheta** <note>original: *aphetæ*; the planet or point that carries the "life force" in a birth chart</note>, or in the directions of all points, they should be taken only in the equator. But certainly, if the configuration is valid in the Zodiac, the direction will also be valid. But perhaps while they rise together, their equal aspect changes and becomes unequal because of the "straightness" and "crookedness" <note>original: *rectitudinem, & tortuoſitatem*; the phenomenon where some signs of the zodiac rise more quickly or slowly over the horizon than others</note> of the signs, and thus they truly come to be considered in the equator, which is the rule of daily motion. For it is necessary to understand the signs in the equator; otherwise, there will not always be 90 degrees between one **angle** <note>original: *angulum*; the four pivotal points of a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</note> and another, as we all openly profess.

3 Therefore, consider the aspects in both the equator and the Zodiac: when they agree, consider them very strong; when they disagree, weak. And then consider the properties of each, and judge according to the one that prevails. The one closer to 90 degrees <note>the "square" aspect, often associated with crisis or physical manifestation</note> prevails. But if there is a contradiction between the signs and not the numbers, surely when the direction reaches the fourth sign—even if it is not at exactly 90 degrees—a bad effect should emerge. This, however, is false. Therefore, the nature of the aspect and the sign must be considered together.

4 Sometimes even the <term>anæretes</term> <note>original: *anæretes*; from the Greek for "destroyer," the planet or mathematical point responsible for ending life</note>, that is, the hostile "killing place" to which the direction arrives, does not kill.
Either because it is in the **term** <note>original: *termino*; a specific five-part subdivision of a zodiac sign that changes the influence of a planet</note> of a benefic planet.
Or because a benefic planet is bodily following there.
Or because it projects rays to that place of any kind, whether ho-

11 You will know by what path a planet helps or harms from the **radical figure** <note>original: *radicali figura*; the original birth chart or horoscope</note>. But specifically in diseases, **Jupiter (♃)** helps through medicine; in violent deaths, through the intervention of a magistrate. **Venus (♀)**, however, in violent deaths helps through grace, friendships, and gifts; in diseases, through the chanting of an oracle and other miraculous ways.
12 Finally, I would not deny that the Moon kills when it is soaked in malefic rays, if it held a "bad look" <note>original: *malè asexpit*; formed a difficult geometric aspect</note> from the start. Similarly, **Mercury** kills if it is soaked in malice from the start and looks badly, especially if one or the other is the weak lord of the **apheta**. See Book 5, Chapter 2, on directions.

### On the same subject from the starred signs.

### ARTICLE IV.

1 The signs of human figure in the **Zodiac**, as well as those outside it, produce symmetrical and well-tempered bodies. The other signs deform them, pulling them toward their own specific shape: and in a certain way, the bodies and limbs turn out similar to those signs, whether in greatness or smallness, strength or softness, and symmetry or deformity.

2 **Leo**, **Virgo**, and **Sagittarius** produce large bodies, especially when **Jupiter** is present. **Pisces**, **Cancer**, and **Capricorn** produce small ones.

3 Likewise, **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Capricorn**, and **Leo** grant stronger traits to the upper parts of the body, but make the lower parts weaker.

4 Conversely, **Sagittarius**, **Scorpio**, and **Gemini** pull the front parts of the body toward a weaker temperament, while making the rear parts robust.

5 Similarly, **Virgo**, **Libra**, and **Sagittarius** bring about symmetry and good proportion.

6 But **Scorpio**, **Pisces**, and **Capricorn** bring about an inconsistent and disproportionate form. Thus it is for the rest, whose meanings you must blend.

7 It is necessary to first know the figures of the stars according to **Arginium** <note>Likely a reference to a star catalog or author; possibly a corruption of Hyginus, author of the "Poeticon Astronomicon," or Aratus</note>. Indeed, a high frequency of stars creates strength; a well-measured arrangement creates a becoming form; distance in **longitude** <note>The position along the ecliptic</note> creates a tall stature; and distance in **latitude** <note>The position north or south of the ecliptic</note> creates a thick body. Hence, practicing **physiognomy** <note>The art of judging character or destiny from physical features</note> from the stars is a useful endeavor.

<header>CONCERNING ASTROLOGICAL MATTERS</header>

## *On defects and diseases of the body in general.*

### CHAPTER VI. ARTICLE I.

1 A **defect** <note>original: *vitium*</note> is inflicted once and does not bring lasting pain, such as blindness or lameness. A **disease** <note>original: *morbus*</note>, however, is either continuous, such as a fever, or recurring, such as gout in the feet <note>original: *podagra*</note> or gout in the hands <note>original: *chiragra*</note>, or both, such as a stone <note>original: *calculus*; referring to kidney or bladder stones</note>.

2 Diseases and defects are produced in the first, seventh, and sixth houses (which are not connected to the horoscope <note>The "horoscope" here refers to the Ascendant or the First House; the text notes that the 6th house lacks a "major aspect" to the 1st house</note>).

3 These are caused by malefic planets <note>Usually Mars or Saturn</note> existing there physically, or by their hostile rays <note>astrological aspects like squares or oppositions</note>, or by them affecting the degrees that follow.

4 This is especially the case when the two **Luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> are in the angles <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the strongest points in a chart</note>, whether they are together or opposite each other and thus afflicted.

5 Even a single malefic planet can cause disease if it is in a center <note>an angle</note> and strikes the Luminaries.

6 A malefic planet in the **sixth house** <note>The house traditionally associated with illness</note> does more through its physical presence than through its ray, and even more if it strikes the angle of the Midheaven <note>the highest point in the sky</note> or the Bottom of the Sky <note>the lowest point</note> with a square ray. The twelfth and eighth houses are also associated with diseases.

7 If the lords of the ascendant and the place of the Moon, or the Moon itself in the aforementioned places, are afflicted by malefic planets positioned elsewhere, or if malefic planets positioned in those places afflict those lords located elsewhere.

---

## *On the nature of the defect and disease, and the parts affected by the signs.*

### A R T I C L E  I I.

1 Such diseases and defects follow the nature of the malefic planet, the affected star, and the sign of the Zodiac existing in that same place. That is, in the first, seventh, sixth, or twelfth houses, according to the configuration of the stars and their locations in respect to the pivots <note>the cardinal angles of the chart</note>.

2 The parts of the body to be affected are indicated by the parts of the signs in the location affecting the horizon, and whether it will be a defect, a disease, or both. The nature of the stars, however, declares the causes and types of these ailments.

3 The parts of the "finisher" are the **terms** <note>Specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note> of the affected sign; **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, a 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> says they are of the nature of those terms. For example, if they are the terms of **Mercury**, they indicate an affliction in the tongue, or the spirits <note>the "vital breaths" or nervous energy</note>, etc. **Cardano** <note>Girolamo Cardano (1501–1576)</note>, however, relying on the opinions of the Arabs, understands the parts of the body as indicated by the signs.

# *On the same subject according to the planets as signifiers or qualifiers.*

## ARTICLE III.

1 **Saturn** rules over the right hearing, the bladder, the spleen, the bones, melancholy <note>the humor of "black bile"</note>, unnatural raw phlegm, cartilages, ligaments, the teeth, and the **retentive faculty** <note>the body's ability to hold onto nutrients or waste</note>.

2 **Jupiter** rules the sense of touch, the lungs, the arteries, the blood, the liver, the flesh, and the **digestive faculty**.

3 **Mars** rules the left hearing, the kidneys, the veins, the genitals, the gall, the bile <note>the humor of "yellow bile"</note>, the intestines, the seat <note>original: *fedi*, likely a typo for *sedem*; the anus or rectum</note>, and the **expulsive faculty** <note>the ability to eliminate waste</note>.

4 The **Sun** rules the sight, especially the right eye, the brain, the heart, the nerves, and all the right-sided arteries and arterial blood.

5 **Venus** rules the sense of smell, the liver, the flesh, the sense of taste, the seed <note>reproductive fluids</note>, the seminal vessels, the genitals of both sexes, the stomach, the breasts, the milk, the **radical moisture** <note>the vital fluid thought to sustain life and longevity</note>, and the **appetitive and attractive faculties**.

6 **Mercury** rules speech, the mind, reason, the tongue, the nerves, memory, the fingers, and the **animal spirits** <note>the refined fluids in the nerves responsible for sensation and movement</note>.

7 The **Moon** rules the menstrual blood, the throat, the stomach, the belly, the womb, all left-sided parts, the brain, the left eye, and natural phlegm. When she is full, she signifies much phlegm that is tasteless and sweet; if she is joined with Saturn, it is bitter, because when there is a great deal, it thickens with difficulty and becomes bitter. But when she is empty of light <note>the New Moon</note>, she signifies little phlegm; then, if she is joined with Mars, it easily becomes bitter and salty.

8 The same limb can be ruled by two or three planets: for example, the brain is ruled by the **Moon** by reason of its substance; by the **Sun** by reason of its arteries and its leadership; and by **Mercury** by reason of the animal spirits and faculties.

9 The planets rule over animals and plants that have a symbolic likeness in substance or shape to our limbs. For example, the **Sun** rules the citron <note>a citrus fruit</note> because it is very similar to the heart; **Saturn** rules the cypress, a symbol of melancholy. You shall assign everything that is hard, large, and foul to **Saturn**; to **Jupiter**, things that are temperate, white, charming, and tall. To **Venus**, similar things, but more feminine. To **Mars**, red things, those with a sharp taste, and things hot and dry, such as pepper and nasturtium. To the **Moon**, things soft, changeable, and moist, such as crabs and beets. To the **Sun**, things large, fragrant, and shining, such as palms, laurels, lions, and roosters. To **Mercury**, things common, artificially arranged, varied, and so forth, of which we speak elsewhere.

## *On physical defects specifically.*

### ARTICLE IV.

<margin>1</margin> **Defects** <note>original: *vitia*; physical deformities or impairments</note> mostly occur when the malefics <note>the "harmful" planets, Saturn and Mars</note> are oriental <note>rising before the Sun in the morning</note>; diseases occur when they are occidental <note>setting after the Sun in the evening</note>. You shall also consider their strength.

---

## *On blindness.*

### ARTICLE V.

<margin>1</margin> **Blindness** of one eye occurs when the Moon is found solitary in the aforementioned angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</note>, or is found in conjunction, opposition, or square aspect to the Sun, or in antiscia <note>points on the zodiac that are reflections of each other across the solstice axis</note>.
<margin>2</margin> Likewise, it occurs when the Moon, joined with or opposite to the Sun, applies to nebulous clusters <note>star clusters that appear "cloudy" to the naked eye</note>, such as the stars of the Manger <note>original: *Præsepis*; the Beehive Cluster in Cancer</note>, or the Pleiades, or the tip of the Arrow, or the sting of the Scorpion, or the parts of Leo between Berenice’s Hair, or the urn of Aquarius.
<margin>3</margin> There are four locations that cause blindness and diseases in the eyes: first, the nebulous clusters; second, the Galaxy <note>the Milky Way</note>; third, the hidden stars; fourth, stars of the nature of the Sun and Mars, or the Moon and Mars.
<margin>4</margin> When the Moon is in one of the angles, and likewise Mars or Saturn is in the centers, or if they, being occidental, have ascended toward her while she is oriental. Haly <note>Haly Abenragel, a prominent 11th-century Arabic astrologer</note> understands this as follows: if Mars is at 3 degrees of Aries, and a Luminary <note>the Sun or Moon</note> is in the fifth house ascending at the 1st degree of Aries, it is the same as the manner of the Sun. Or if the Moon is at 10 degrees of Aries in the west, and the degree of the west is 4 degrees of Aries, and Mars is in the east at 12 degrees of Libra, then the Moon is occidental from the malefic, and the malefic ascends by diurnal motion to her opposition. Or if 28 degrees of Virgo are ascending, and Mars is at the 3rd degree of Libra, and the Moon is at the 1st degree, then Mars is nearer to the eastern angle than the Moon. I understand this as "ascending to the position," not to the specific degree.
<margin>5</margin> Also, when the malefics are configured in a hostile aspect to both Luminaries in the same or opposite sign—morning stars to the Sun, evening stars to the Moon—it threatens injury to both eyes.
<margin>6</margin> Also, when the Sun is in the place of the Moon, and Saturn or Mars is positioned before him, blindness is signified.

<margin>7</margin> **Mars** threatens a wound, a burn, injury by iron <note>original: *ferrum*; referring to blades or weapons</note>, or a blow. When joined with **Mercury**, he causes this in wrestling grounds, gymnasiums, or from the attacks of evil men. **Saturn**, however, causes blindness through cataracts <note>original: *suffusionem*; a "pouring over" of fluid in the eye</note>, cold, or glaucoma.

<margin>8</margin> This same thing occurs when only one <term>malefic</term> <note>a planet traditionally viewed as harmful, such as Saturn or Mars</note> strikes only one of the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun or the Moon</note>. This happened in the case of the noble **Fogiano**. He currently has **Saturn** in the 9th house at 29 or 30 degrees, in retrograde. He has the **Moon** in 1 degree of **Aries** and at 7 degrees of **Leo**, flowing away from the nebulous **Manger** <note>original: *Præsepi*; the Beehive star cluster</note> and from four hidden stars; she is also in a <term>sextile</term> <note>a 60-degree harmonious aspect</note> aspect to that same Saturn. His **Sun** is at 21 degrees of **Libra**, equidistant to **Jupiter** located in the 12th house at 9 degrees of **Virgo**. **Mars** is at 4 degrees of **Virgo**, and **Mercury** and **Venus** are at 7 and 8 degrees of **Libra**. Nevertheless, he was blinded in both eyes when the Moon reached 29 degrees of **Leo** by <term>direction</term> <note>a method of timing events by "moving" planets forward in the chart</note>, which is a <term>square</term> <note>a 90-degree challenging aspect</note> aspect to Saturn. He is blinded in such a way, however, that he sees a faint light and things that look like tiny, atom-like particles. I would have hoped for a recovery through religion or medicine due to the aspect of Venus and Mercury, were it not for the fact that the direction was hastening toward Mars.

<margin>9</margin> The **Galaxy** <note>the Milky Way</note> in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the degree rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> with the Luminaries makes the hair of the newborn white, as if they were an old man; it also makes the whole body soft and weak, and the eyes blind. Such is the case with the daughter of the **Jailer**, who has her Sun in the Manger cluster, while **Cancer** rises with the Galaxy and the Moon.

<margin>10</margin> Whenever the Moon is in <term>square</term> or <term>diameter</term> <note>an opposition or 180-degree aspect</note> to the Sun, it weakens the vision, especially when she applies to him <note>moves toward the exact aspect</note> at the time when a direction completes that application.

### On sterility.

#### ARTICLE VI.

<margin>1</margin> If **Venus** is in the first or seventh house (but more so in the seventh) and is configured to **Saturn** by opposition, square, <term>antiscion</term> <note>a point of equal daylight/shadow</note>, or by exchanging dignity with him <note>e.g., Saturn in Cancer and Venus in Capricorn</note>, and if **Mars** is elevated over Venus or opposite her, it denies offspring to males. For women, it decrees miscarriages, "unripe" <note>premature</note> births, and damaged fetuses, especially when in **Cancer**, **Virgo**, or **Capricorn**, or if the Moon applies to Mars at the moment of birth.

<margin>2</margin> It will be worse if **Mercury** is joined or configured to Venus, or if he exchanges dignity with Saturn, and Mars is again elevated over her or opposed. In this way are created eunuchs, hermaphrodites, and those whose genital passages are fused together.

<margin>3</margin> When these are so configured, if the **Sun** is also configured, and the Luminaries and Venus are in masculine signs, and the Moon is <term>occidental</term> <note>setting in the west</note>, and the malefic planets [apply] to her...

### A R T I C L E V I I.

1 **T**hose with **Saturn** ♄ and **Mercury** ☿ in the aforementioned <term>angles</term> <note>the four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> with the **Sun** have hindered speech and a stammer, especially when **Mercury** is "western" <note>setting after the Sun</note> and both are in aspect with the **Moon** ☽.

4 In my own case, I have **Mercury** ☿ and **Saturn** ♄ with the **Sun**, western and "under the rays" <note>original: *sub radiis*; meaning the planet is so close to the Sun it is hidden by its brightness</note> in the first—or rather, the twelfth—house. Yet my tongue is not hindered, nor am I overly talkative. I believe this is because the constellation is in **Virgo** ♍, a sign of beautiful voice, and the harmful planet is hidden by the rays and in a sextile with **Jupiter** ♃; therefore, I was not harmed at all. However, **Brother Julian** has **Pisces** ♓ on the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, with **Saturn** ♄ almost exactly on the opposite angle in 3 degrees of **Virgo** ♍. Following that, he has **Venus** ♀ at 19 degrees, **Mercury** ☿ at 22, and the **Moon** ☽ at 27. Consequently, he stammered heavily until the <term>direction</term> of his horoscope reached **Jupiter** ♃ at 27 degrees of **Pisces** ♓ and the sextile of **Mars** ♂ at 24 degrees of the same sign. Now he fares better. Affliction of the **Moon** in a mute sign or at the point of the horoscope also makes one a stammerer, as with the **Prince of Stigliano**. Those who have **Mars** joined with **Mercury** are sharp-tongued or "biting."

## Concerning the lame, the hunchbacked, and the distorted.

### A R T I C L E V I I I.

1 **I**f the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> are rising in the <term>angles</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</note> toward **malefics** <note>planets traditionally viewed as harmful, specifically Saturn and Mars</note> placed in the centers, or opposite them, and especially if the **Moon** ☽ is in the nodes, or in the "bendings," or in its own tropics, or in harmful or "truncated" signs—**Aries** ♈, **Taurus** ♉, **Cancer** ♋, **Scorpio** ♏, and **Capricorn** ♑—bodily defects occur, such as a hunching of the back, lameness, or the dislocation of joints.
2 If the **Luminaries** are completely joined with the **malefics**, these defects will exist from birth; if not, they will occur later when the <term>direction</term> and <term>progression</term> <note>astrological methods for timing events later in life</note> align.
3 If the **malefics** were then in the **M.C.** <note>the Midheaven, or the highest point in the chart</note> and elevated above the **Luminaries**, or in opposition, or in a square aspect, defects will be inflicted by grave dangers, such as a fall from a height, an attack by bandits, or a blow from a four-legged animal.
4 **Mars** ♂ causes harm through fire and wounds inflicted during a riot, or by robberies—and especially so when he is with **Mercury** ☿. **Saturn** ♄ harms through a fall, a shipwreck, or the "contraction of the limbs" <note>possibly referring to paralysis or muscle wasting</note>.
5 In this configuration, the southern node is worse than the northern one; this applies not only to the **Moon's** nodes, but also the nodes and tropics of other planets. Hence the **Dragon's Tail** <note>the South Node, ☊</note> with the **Moon**, and often with other planets, causes the same effect when in the angles, as **Cardano** <note>Gerolamo Cardano, a famous 16th-century Italian polymath and astrologer</note> testifies. In the case of **Haly** <note>likely the Arab astrologer Ali ibn Ridwan</note>, the **Moon** was with **Mars** ♂ and the **South Node** ☊ in the 12th house, in square aspect to the **Sun** and a <term>combust</term> **Jupiter** <note>a planet so close to the Sun that its influence is "burned up" or hidden</note> in the third house; he became hunchbacked in his twelfth year, according to the astrological period.

### Concerning the skin.

### A R T I C L E I X.

1 **F**urthermore, when the **Moon** is thus afflicted while moving through the tropical and equinoctial signs, defects occur in the skin. In **Aries** ♈, these arise mostly from <term>vitiligo</term> <note>original: "vitiligine"; a condition causing white patches on the skin</note>; in **Cancer** ♋, from <term>impetigo</term> <note>original: "impetigine"; a contagious skin infection</note>; and near the **Galaxy** <note>the Milky Way</note>, there is excessive whiteness and <term>scrofula</term> <note>original: "scrofulæ"; a swelling of the lymph nodes often related to tuberculosis</note>. In **Libra** ♎, it comes from leprosy, scabies, or the "venereal plague" <note>original: "lue venerea"; a historical term often referring to syphilis</note>; in **Capricorn** ♑, from freckles and other conditions of that kind.

## Concerning diseases in particular.

### A R T I C L E X.

1 **From** those same configurations already mentioned, diseases arise when the **malefics** <note>Saturn and Mars</note> are positioned in an opposite manner—namely, when they are "vespertine" <note>setting after the Sun</note> with the **Sun** ☉, or "matutine" <note>rising before the Sun</note> with the **Moon** ☽.

---

### *Concerning the Planets as authors and qualifiers of diseases.*

### A R T I C L E X I.

1 **In** general, **Saturn** ♄ causes a coldness of the stomach and bowels, making them full of excess humors, phlegmatic, and prone to "fluxes" <note>the discharge of fluid, such as catarrh</note>; he makes people thin, sickly, and prone to dysentery. He causes difficulty in coughing up phlegm, as well as colic, leprosy, and—in women—afflictions of the womb.
2 **Mars** ♂ causes people to spit up blood or be seized by <term>black bile</term> <note>original: "atra bile"; one of the four humors, associated with melancholy and various illnesses</note>. He causes shortness of breath, lung infections, and scabs. He brings about constant burning sensations, fissures, and <term>fistulas</term> <note>abnormal passages in the body</note> in the more hidden parts, as well as hemorrhaging, inflamed burns, and spreading ulcers. In women, he additionally causes miscarriages, premature or incomplete births, or "erosions" <note>likely referring to cervical or uterine lesions</note>.
3 When both planets act together, they mix their powers and their meanings.
4 Likewise, **Venus** ♀ is like the spring, **Mars** ♂ like the summer, **Saturn** ♄ like the winter, and **Mercury** ☿ like the autumn; they bring about diseases similar to the ailments common to those seasons.
5 Truly, the specific natures of the stars in their various configurations indicate the specific type of disease.
6 **Mercury** ☿ contributes to the intensity of these evils. For when he is joined to **Saturn** ♄, he intensifies the cold, and by his constant motion, he excites the flow of phlegm and a disturbance of humors, especially around the chest, throat, and stomach. He also assists **Mars** ♂ by drying things out, as seen in ulcers resulting from the "stripping of the skin" <note>excoriation</note> and dryness, or in encrusted abscesses, <term>St. Anthony’s Fire</term> <note>original: "igni sacro"; likely referring to erysipelas or ergotism, which causes a burning sensation in the skin</note>, "wild lichens" <note>spreading skin eruptions</note> arising from black bile, the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: "comitiali morbo"; the historical name for epilepsy</note>, leprosy, and related conditions.

### From the signs of heaven concerning these same matters.

## A R T I C L E XII.

1 **According** to the nature of the signs found in the "angles" <note>the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the ascendant, descendant, midheaven, and lower midheaven</note> of the aforementioned constellations, specific outcomes of diseases occur. For example, in **Cancer** ♋ first of all, and in **Pisces** ♓ and **Scorpio** ♏, and in signs that are similar to land and water creatures, there arise "eating" <note>spreading or corrosive</note> ulcers, <term>impetigo</term> <note>original: "impetigines"; a contagious skin infection</note>, <term>scrofula</term> <note>original: "scrofulæ"; a swelling of the lymph nodes, often tubercular</note>, fistulas, leprosies, the itch, and <term>venereal disease</term> <note>original: "lues venerea"</note>. In **Sagittarius** ♐ and **Gemini** ♊, the "falling sickness" <note>original: "comitialis morbus"; epilepsy</note> occurs, as well as those ailments that damage the breath. In these latter signs, this is because of **Jupiter** ♃ and **Mercury** ☿; in the former signs, it is because aquatic and terrestrial creatures feed by clinging to things, and thus cause similar diseases. Therefore, whoever designed these figures <note>the symbols of the Zodiac</note> did not do so merely for the sake of memory, but wrote as one skilled in the natural symbols provided by God.

---

### Concerning the curable, the incurable, and those that can be hidden.

## A R T I C L E XIII.

1 **In** all the aforementioned constellations, if no **benefic** planet <note>the "lucky" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> is aligned with the **malefics** <note>the "unlucky" planets, Saturn and Mars</note> or the angular "Luminaries" <note>the Sun and Moon</note>, the diseases and defects will be incurable and severe.
2 Likewise, if benefics are aligned but are overcome by the malefics, they provide little or no help toward a cure—such as when the benefics are in the "dignities" <note>astrological positions of power</note> of the malefics, or are "under the earth," or in "cadent" houses <note>weaker positions in the chart</note>, or are "vespertine" <note>setting after the Sun</note>, etc.
3 If the benefics are more powerful, especially when they are "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun</note>, they will cure diseases and will hide defects or make them appear honorable. **Jupiter** ♃ does this through human assistance, such as through wealth and high status by his own power; but when **Mercury** ☿ is added, he also heals through medicine. **Venus** ♀, however, makes defects appear elegant and praiseworthy through predictions and oracles—as was the case with **Tiresias** <note>the famous blind prophet of Greek mythology who was compensated for his blindness with the gift of prophecy</note>. She cures diseases through divine assistance by her own power. But when paired with **Saturn** ♄, this does not happen without punishment and a public disgrace well known to others, such as when people are being exorcised, etc. With **Mercury** ☿, however, it is not without aid and profit flowing to the sick person from their very defects and diseases. This was the case in the time of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century scholar whose "Tetrabiblos" is the source for much of this theory</note>. Now, however, those who are healed receive gifts and alms. Others gain profit from a <term>Pythonic spirit</term> <note>original: "ex Pythone"; referring to a spirit of divination or "pythonic" possession</note>, as we shall discuss later.
4 Note that according to Ptolemy, diseases are cured by the stars under a divine pretext, either because they are signs, or because they are "co-causes" of the healing intelligence. However, vices <note>or defects</note> are not cured by the stars by any...

## On the qualities of the soul in general.

### CHAPTER VII. ARTICLE I.

1 **The** qualities of the soul follow the <term>temperament</term> <note>original: "temperiem"; the balance of bodily fluids or "humors" that was thought to dictate personality.</note> of the body as a disposing cause. Therefore, the heavens have power over morals by way of disposition; as St. Thomas used to say in Book 3 of *Against the Gentiles* concerning **Mercury** ☿ being in a good state. Thus we also experience these inclinations and operations in children before they have the use of reason.

2 **From** the constitution of **Mercury** ☿, the intellect, reason, and contemplation are known. From the **Moon** ☽ and its configured stars, one knows morals, actions, and the operations of the senses. For Mercury governs the spirits, while the Moon governs the brain—the source of the senses, nerves, and movements—and all the humors of the body, by which both the spirit and the body are nourished, insofar as they are humors.

3 **The** other planets participate as well. For **Mars** ♂ possesses audacity, **Saturn** ♄ persistence, **Jupiter** ♃ simplicity, etc., as discussed previously; but the primary <term>significators</term> <note>the planets that indicate or "signal" a specific quality in a birth chart</note> are the **Moon** ☽ and **Mercury** ☿.

4 **For** this reason, men are mostly wicked, says St. Thomas, because they prefer sensual affection over reason. This is also signified in the stars. For the Moon usually prevails over Mercury. She is often more robust due to Mercury’s continual <term>combustions</term> <note>original: "combustiones"; when a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is thought to be weakened or "burnt up"</note> and retrogressions; she prevails even more when she is in commanding signs and signs of "long ascension," while Mercury is in obedient signs and signs of "short ascension." <note>These terms refer to the amount of time it takes for certain signs of the Zodiac to rise over the horizon.</note>

5 **Mercury** ☿ is greatly harmed in the watery signs, especially in **Pisces** ♓, and by the unlucky rays of **Saturn** ♄. When "combust," he denies the student the sciences, but not eloquence or history. To me, however, being combust denied nothing except freedom from the King; <note>The author, likely Tommaso Campanella, refers here to his long imprisonment by the Spanish authorities.</note> nor did it deny scientific study to Tobias when Mercury was an evening star and joined to Mars. The Moon, however, is fearful; when she is afflicted, even reason is dulled, since it depends indirectly on the senses. The same occurs when the <term>horoscope</term> <note>here meaning the Ascendant or the physical vitality of the birth chart</note> is damaged.

6 **In** the centers of the "angles" <note>the most powerful points of a horoscope: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, both horizontal and vertical, the planets contribute most to the character: where **Saturn** ♄ makes men cautious, **Jupiter** ♃ learned, **Mars** ♂ effective, the **Sun** ☉ serious, **Venus** ♀ eloquent, **Mercury** ☿ prompt, and the **Moon** ☽ a companion.

If [the ruler] is placed in an <term>obscure place</term> <note>original: "obscuro loco"; referring to an "unfortunate" house in the birth chart, such as the 6th, 8th, or 12th, where a planet's power is weakened or turned toward hardship.</note>, it produces, by contrast, people who are sordid, overly frugal, abject, stubborn in their opinions, envious, timid, solitary, and prone to speaking ill of others; they are always dressed in mourning clothes, and are impudent, superstitious, and laborious, yet negligent toward their children and friends, plotting against their own households, gloomy, and entirely careless regarding their own health.

They are seers, religious, and desirous of mysteries and oracles; they are sacrificers, divine, venerable, modest, philosophers, cautious, easily angered, suspicious, and jealous.

# ASTROLOGY

**With Venus in a good state** <note>This continues the description of Mars combined with Venus from the previous page.</note>, they are lovable, easy to deal with, and devoted to their companions. They are people who live together sweetly, are joyful, playful, simple, open, and modest. They are dancers, lovers, fond of children, and mimics. They are seekers of pleasure, fond of personal grooming, and prone to playfulness—yet they are shrewd without being harmful, knowing how to hide their own vices. They are provident and avoid falling under the censure or rebuke of others. They are lovers of young men as much as of women, lavish in their spending, quick-tempered, and prone to jealousy.

**Unfavorably, however**, they have prying eyes, are sluggish, and are prone to **sexual intercourse** <term>sexual intercourse</term> <note>original: "coïtum"</note>. They are careless of everything, mockers, adulterers, insulting, and liars. They are crafty, corruptors of both their own households and those of others. They are quick to satisfy their desires and easily satiated <note>original: "facile satiabiles"; this may suggest they move quickly from one desire to the next</note>, violators of women and virgins, and frequently expose themselves to dangers. They are sly, immoderate, plotters, and perjurers. They are prone to failure and madness, sometimes eager to over-adorn themselves, and are bold, perverse, and insolently petulant.

**When joined with Mercury favorably** <note>This describes the influence of Mars and Mercury in combination.</note>, they are vehement in speech, military-minded, energetic, agile, and respected. They are shifty <note>original: "versipelles"; literally "skin-changers" or chameleons</note>, skilled, sophists, and hard-working. They are cunning "old hands," ready with both tongue and hand, though inconstant. They attack from ambush and are imbued with the "evil arts" <note>technical skills or tricks used for deception</note>, yet they are ingenious. Though they are deceivers, pretenders, prying, and lovers of evil things, they nonetheless act prosperously. They converse easily and pleasantly with their equals and are helpful to friends while being troublesome to enemies.

**Unfavorably, however**, they are deceivers, usurpers of other people's property, and cruel. They expose themselves to dangers and are so bold that they often regret their own actions. They are ready to trade blows and are driven by immoderate impulses. They are bold, thieves, impious, perjurers, and burglars. They are arsonists, stage-players, hostile, and **grave-robbers** <term>grave-robbers</term> <note>original: "sepulcrorum effossores"</note>. They are ferocious, forgers, unfaithful, enchanters, magicians, sorcerers, and murderers.

### 4. Venus Alone

**When Venus is alone and favorably situated**, people are charming, good, and pleasure-seekers. They are accessible to everyone, wise, pure, and fond of dancing. They are ambitious, joyful, and enemies of hard labor. They are lovers of the arts, decent in behavior, and wonderfully reverent of God. **With Mercury favorably**, they are ready for manual crafts, possess a philosophical mind, and are suited to the sciences. They are craftsmen, poets, and elegant...

## On the same subject, based on the configurations of the places and the lords of the places.

### ARTICLE V.

5. ## On the curable, the incurable, and the concealable.

### ARTICLE III.

1 The aforementioned planetary arrangement, if lacking the influence of the benefics, makes the said diseases incurable.

2 But if ♃ Jupiter and ♀ Venus are configured, and the <term>malefics</term> <note>the "harmful" planets Saturn and Mars</note> are in the western parts of the chart while the benefics are in the angles and favorable places, the conditions will be curable. However, these defects will be "illustrious"—meaning they will be famous and a public example to others. Jupiter heals through the works of physicians; Venus heals significantly through oracles and religion. For it is God who heals through religion, though sometimes through "secondary causes" <note>natural means used by God</note>, such as when He healed Tobias with the gall of a fish.

3 If, on the contrary, the malefics are in the eastern angle while the benefics are in the west, the defects will be similarly famous, but incurable according to the stars—though not to God.

# APPENDIX

1 The doctrine of Aristotle in his *Problems*, as well as Galen (who admittedly has better judgment), Avicenna, and others—who think that divine inspiration is the power of <term>black bile</term> <note>original: "atra bilis"; the humor associated with melancholy and, according to ancient tradition, genius or madness</note> alone—is most foolish. For neither the ability to divine the future, nor to compose poems, nor to speak in a foreign language (an experience which even Aristotle does not deny) can be attributed to a dull humor, nor even to the physical bodies of the stars. Instead, these must be attributed to an intelligent cause. Since this cause misuses the humors to torment men, it cannot be a good cause. Therefore, it is the devil. Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the foundational authority on astronomy and astrology in the Middle Ages and Renaissance</note> acknowledges this, although he does not know how to distinguish bad gods from good ones. For the pagans worshipped the bad ones as well. We call them Angels, knowing that there is one true God who is both theirs and ours.

2 Note that a planet "under the rays" <note>original: "sub radiis"; an astrological condition where a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is supposedly weakened or "burnt up"</note> provides nothing in matters of life, death, and children; rather, the Sun acts in its place. In matters of actions, it provides almost nothing. In those things that belong to the planets themselves, they signify weak effects, such as in the qualities of the mind and body, and in diseases—especially Mars, for they signify "combustion" or burning.

# On vices in sexual matters specifically
## ARTICLE IV

1 The stars have the greatest power in sexual matters, since this area of life is almost entirely sensual, and the soul—not entirely unwillingly—submits to the qualities and allurements of the body.

2 Madness, epilepsy, and other diseases are subject to the stars more than the vices of love are. For that reason, you will easily pronounce judgment on the former; but it is not so easy with the latter, which can be restrained by laws and by one's own free will.
