### *Special rules concerning the same subject.*

## ARTICLE V.

1 When the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> are not joined to each other, and are configured to Venus (♀) and Mars (♂) which are also not joined—or the reverse—and they are afflicted in the <term>angles</term> <note>The most powerful houses of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note> by <term>malefics</term> <note>Planets traditionally considered harmful, namely Saturn and Mars</note>, especially in the signs of Venus (♀) and Mars (♂), they usually cause "amorous madness."
I saw a girl who refused no one—not a relative, nor a clergyman, nor the lowliest man—whose Luminaries in Cancer (♋) and Capricorn (♑) were afflicted by Saturn (♄) placed in Libra (♎). Furthermore, Venus (♀) from the 12th degree of Pisces (♓) regarded Mars (♂) in the 24th degree of Gemini (♊). And unless Jupiter (♃) had been in the 4th degree of Gemini (♊), sending <term>trine rays</term> <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered harmonious and helpful</note> to Saturn (♄), she could not have been restrained by her parents from going mad for any passerby. Consequently, she would show the whites of her eyes and point out dogs copulating.

2 If both Luminaries are in masculine signs, the males exceed masculine nature in intercourse; the females, however, cross over to a manly disposition.

3 If, moreover, both Mars (♂) and Venus (♀) are together, or if one is found in a masculine sign, such as Aries (♈) and Leo (♌), then the males will be ready for all intercourse, adulterers, and prone to every foul pleasure. The females, however, will be lustful, desiring intercourse against nature, with wandering eyes, and taking masculine roles upon themselves. And if only Venus (♀) is in a masculine sign, the vice will be secret. If Mars (♂) is also there, they will have mistresses and concubines instead of wives; they will openly boast of their baseness and say more than they actually do.

4 Intercourse is "natural" if the Sun (☉) is in a masculine sign and the Moon (☽) is in a feminine one. If it is the opposite, the males will sometimes be very masculine in intercourse, and sometimes very feminine. This also occurs if Mars (♂) is in a masculine sign and Venus (♀) in a feminine one, and the reverse, as stated above.

5 The Moon (☽) and Sun (☉) in feminine signs make males <term>effeminate</term> <note>original: "euiratos", literally emasculated or unmanly</note>, and they willingly submit to womanly roles; but they make females excessively desirous of natural intercourse.

6 If, moreover, Venus (♀) is also feminine, the females will be adulterous and lustful, never refusing any man at any time, nor avoiding any illicit intercourse. The men, however, will be soft, rushing headlong into unions unknown to nature, and submitting to womanly roles. These things will be done in secret and under cover.

For <term>the Moon</term> <note>The symbol for the Moon is omitted in the text but implied by the context of the previous page and the following rules</note> in <term>Cancer</term> (♋), in the <term>midheaven</term> <note>The highest point in an astrological chart, representing public life and status</note>, free from <term>Saturn</term> (♄) and <term>Mars</term> <note>original: "*" — likely a shorthand for Mars or a generic malefic star</note>, gives a wife without a doubt; and on the contrary, being "under the rays" <note>Too close to the Sun to be seen</note> in <term>Leo</term> with Saturn, it denies marriage. In other positions, I speak with caution.

4 In a sign of a single figure <note>Signs represented by one entity, such as Leo or Aries</note> and applying to one star, the Moon gives one wife; in <term>bicorporeal</term> <note>Signs with dual figures, like Gemini or Pisces</note> or multi-bodied signs placed outside the Zodiac, or applying to many stars, she repeats marriages, according to the multitude of stars and the forms in the Moon's location.

5 Consider the law, national customs, and circumstances. For the <term>Turk</term> <note>A common early modern reference to the Ottoman Empire</note> by law has several wives. The <term>Moors</term> also have very many, while Christians have one. Therefore, you shall judge by inspecting the general constitution, which prevails over the individual: for <term>Saturn</term> does not cause freezing in the summer <note>A metaphor meaning that broad environmental or cultural factors—like the season—overrule the specific influence of a single planet</note>.

## On the Quality of the Wife.

### ARTICLE II.

1 If the stars to which the Moon <term>applies</term> <note>Approaches within a certain number of degrees</note> by body or by "ray" <note>By physical conjunction or by an aspect/angle</note> are good, they give good spouses; if bad, they give bad ones. Understand this primarily at the time of the <term>direction</term> <note>A predictive technique where the movement of planets is mapped to years of a person's life</note> when the marriage occurs. For I experienced in the case of <term>Mastrillo</term> <note>Likely a contemporary reference or a specific case study known to the author</note> a good application of the Moon suddenly at a time when he could not take a wife due to his age; later, however, he did not take such a wife, but rather the kind that the "direction" indicated—though not entirely. Therefore, blend the judgment of the <term>root</term> <note>The original birth chart, also called the radix</note> and the direction.

2 If she applies to <term>Saturn</term> (♄), the wives will be hardworking and gloomy. If to <term>Jupiter</term> (♃), they will rule the family well and be venerable. If to <term>Mars</term> (♂), they will be bold and rebellious. If to <term>Venus</term> (♀), beautiful, graceful, and cheerful. If to <term>Mercury</term> (☿), industrious, useful, and lovers of their husband and children. But with Mars, they are spirited, unstable, and variable. Here, note the law of regions and customs as part of the general constitution: as among the <term>Belgians</term>, wives sell, buy, and trade; in <term>Naples</term> they are playful; in <term>Florence</term> they work, and so on.

### On the Character of the Husband.

### ARTICLE IV.

1 <term>Saturn</term> (♄) configured with the <term>Sun</term> <note>The Sun is the primary indicator for the husband in a woman's birth chart</note> gives husbands who are composed, helpful, and industrious; <term>Jupiter</term> (♃) gives those who are venerable and magnanimous; <term>Mars</term> (♂) gives those who are unruly, energetic, and estranged from their children and wife; <term>Venus</term> (♀) gives those who are pleasant and handsome; <term>Mercury</term> (☿) gives those who are industrious, providers, and agile. <term>Venus</term> (♀) with <term>Saturn</term> (♄) signifies husbands who are lazy and cold in sexual union; with <term>Mars</term> (♂), those who are hot, prone to sexual union, and adulterers; with <term>Mercury</term> (☿), those who are lovers of children.

### On the Shared Life of Spouses.

### ARTICLE V.

1 When the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> of the spouses behold each other with a friendly <term>aspect</term> <note>Specific geometric angles between planets thought to transmit influence</note>, and much more so if they are found in <term>mutual reception</term> <note>A condition where two planets are in each other's home signs, suggesting cooperation</note>, a stable marriage and constant cohabitation is designated. This is especially true if the Moon of the husband and the Sun of the wife are so situated.

2 When, however, they behold each other in a hostile manner, or are in <term>disjunct</term> <note>Signs that do not 'see' each other by standard aspect, creating a lack of connection</note> signs, marriages are dissolved, either totally, or only in the bed, or through a discord of minds.

3 If any <term>aphetae</term> <note>original: "aphetæ" — the 'life-givers' or primary points of a chart used to determine the length and quality of life</note>, or the same planet in both charts, is well configured, the result will be the same, but not as constant. Similarly, if poorly configured, there will be an inconstant discord. The times of discord will be shown by the opposing <term>directions</term> and <term>progressions</term> <note>Technical methods for predicting the timing of events in a person's life</note> of the life-givers, especially the Luminaries.

4 The shared life will be pleasant, charming, and useful if the Luminaries agree and <term>benefic</term> <note>Helpful planets, typically Jupiter and Venus</note> planets are elevated or configured with them; if <term>malefic</term> <note>Harmful planets, typically Saturn and Mars</note> planets predominate, the life will be contentious, shameless, and envious.

5 If the Luminaries disagree but the benefics are well configured, they can restore a shared life that was nearly severed, bringing peace and returning a charming and reciprocal love. If the malefics predominate, they tear it apart with insults and curses; with the addition of <term>Mercury</term> (☿), it includes shouting, reproaches, and accusations; with the addition of <term>Venus</term> (♀), it involves adulteries and incantations <note>original: "incantantionibus" — perhaps implying love-potions or spells to manipulate the partner</note>. For the union is greatly defiled by malefic planets.

## On Illicit Domestic Unions.

### ARTICLE VI.

1 <term>Venus</term> (♀), <term>Mars</term> (♂), and <term>Saturn</term> (♄), if they should meet with the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and the Moon</note>, indicate concubinage with blood relatives, household members, or in-laws, according to the specific condition of Venus toward the aforementioned planets.

2 Venus influenced by Mars through a meeting or an <term>aspect</term> <note>A specific geometric relationship between planets</note> indicates a union with a young kinswoman, because they share alternating heights in mutual <term>triplicities</term> <note>Groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note>.

3 Venus influenced by Saturn indicates a union with an older person, since they possess houses in mutual triplicities; if <term>Mercury</term> (☿) joins them, it will not happen without public scandal. Venus and Mars together indicate amorous passions.

4 In "promiscuous" <note>Also known as "double-bodied" or "bi-corporeal" signs</note> and familiar signs, such as <term>Gemini</term> (♊︎) and <term>Sagittarius</term> (♐︎), they decree the joining of brothers and kinsfolk. Likewise, if the Moon is added to these constellations in a man's <term>nativity</term> <note>A birth chart; original: "genesis"</note>, it signifies concubinage with two sisters or female relatives. In a woman’s nativity, however, if the Sun is added, it signifies a union with two brothers or kinsmen.

5 When Venus is found with Saturn in these signs, it makes these unions light and stable; if Mercury is added, they are profitable; with Mars, they are unstable, harmful, and full of mutual envy and jealousy.

6 If Mars is configured with them by <term>conjunction</term> <note>When two planets appear in the same spot in the sky</note>, he grants a union with those of equal age; if he is more <term>occidental</term> <note>Setting after the Sun</note>, with those who are older; if more <term>oriental</term> <note>Rising before the Sun</note>, with those who are younger. Perhaps this decree is also understood to apply to Venus, according to <term>Cardano</term> <note>Girolamo Cardano (1501–1576), a famous Italian polymath and astrologer</note>.

7 If Venus and Saturn are in "promiscuous" signs, namely Gemini (♊︎) or <term>Libra</term> (♎︎), where both have <term>dignity</term> <note>Planetary strength based on zodiac position</note>, they grant sexual union with in-laws. Furthermore, if this configuration occurs in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon; original: "horoscopo"</note> or the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>The highest point of the chart; original: "medio coeli"</note>, and the Moon joins in, it causes men to lie with their mothers, their mothers' sisters, or their stepmothers. It causes women to lie with their sons, stepsons, or their daughters' husbands. You shall say the same if Venus and Saturn exchange dignity.

8 Likewise, if the Sun joins, especially when the planets are occidental, men will lie with their daughters, stepdaughters, or their sons' wives and their daughters' sisters; women will lie with their fathers, paternal uncles, or stepfathers.

9 When the aforementioned configurations do not occur in signs of a single gender, but in feminine places and persons, they altogether effect toward—

## On the Nature and Habits of Intercourse.

### ARTICLE VII.

1 Mars, when separated from Saturn and Venus and aided by Jupiter, makes people modest and pure in sexual matters, following natural usage. With Saturn alone, it makes them sluggish and cold. With Jupiter and Venus, it makes them agile and lustful, yet temperate and avoiding infamy. With Venus alone, in the absence of Saturn and Jupiter, they are slow to business, lazy, and seeking pleasure from every side.

2 Likewise, if Mars is an "evening star" <note>Setting after the Sun</note> and Venus is a "morning star" <note>Rising before the Sun</note>, one will be captivated by the union of both males and females, though not excessively toward either sex. If both are evening stars, they will be inclined toward the intercourse of women—to the point that they even submit themselves like a woman if their signs are feminine. If both are morning stars, he will love only boys. And if they are also in "masculine" places, they will have no regard for the age of the male.

3 But if Venus is more <term>occidental</term> <note>Western or setting</note>, they will unite with low-born men, slaves, or foreigners. If Mars is so placed, they will unite with those more eminent than themselves and with noble ladies. That is to say, a male will cohabit with more noble women if he has Venus more <term>oriental</term> <note>Eastern or rising</note>, and with more ignoble women if she is more occidental.

1 (It follows that) the children will be lovable, gracious, and charming (to those parents, I say) and they shall inherit. 5 Remember what was said before: that the harmony of the child's Part of Fortune with the parent's Sun and Moon delivers the inheritance of the parents into their hands. Therefore, this is much more certain if it harmonizes with the parents' <term>Luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and the Moon</note>. In a hostile aspect, it denies the inheritance or brings harm.

->*On the relationship of children toward one another.*<-

### ARTICLE IV.

1 If the lords of the "givers" and the locations of the children agree with each other, they produce brothers who are in harmony and who help one another. If they are disconnected or in opposition, they are prone to enmity and plot against one another, such as the sons of <note>original: "Gerifi"; likely referring to a specific historical or legendary family known for internal strife</note> Gerifi.
2 They "agree" either by nature, such as Jupiter (♃) and Saturn (♄); or by quality, such as Mars (♂) and Venus (♀); or by shared dignity, such as Saturn (♄) and Mars (♂); or by an exchange of dignities, or by geometric aspect, or etc.
3 Set the "giver" of the child as the Ascendant, draw up the figure, and judge the child just as you would the father's chart from the child's configured <term>theme</term> <note>original: "themate"; the astrological chart</note>. Calculate the Lot from this new Ascendant, and place the other planets just as they were in the father's chart.
4 Those who have many children are fortunate, because the "givers" are <term>benefics</term> <note>helpful planets, usually Jupiter or Venus</note> and are located in the tenth or eleventh houses, or are opposite to good positions.
5 From the direction of the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "M.C."; the highest point in the chart, representing one's status and actions</note>, the timing of future children's births is determined. Some generate children every year because of the <term>bounds</term> <note>original: "terminos"; subdivisions of zodiac signs</note> and rays in the <term>radix</term> <note>the original birth chart</note>, and in the progression and the <term>solar return</term> <note>original: "ingressu"; the annual chart for the year</note>, provided that there are <term>prolific signs</term> <note>signs that favor many children, like Cancer or Pisces</note> in the radix and the significators are not obstructed.

# *Of friends and enemies.*

## CHAPTER XI. ARTICLE I.

<margin>1 17.</margin>
If the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and the Moon</note>, the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: "horoscopus"; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, and the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>a mathematical point in the chart representing prosperity</note> are in the same signs in the birth charts of two people, or are not more than 17 degrees apart, or have exchanged their positions with one another, they create lifelong, sincere friendships, exposed to no offenses. If they are in an opposition that does not change <note>an aspect of 180 degrees</note>, or in signs that are <term>inconjunction</term> <note>original: "inconiunctis"; signs that do not "see" or aspect one another</note>, they create the greatest and most enduring enmities.

<margin>2</margin>
But if they are only connected by a "ray" <note>an astrological aspect or mathematical angle</note>, whether friendly or unfriendly, they create mediocre friendships in which grudges and silence are occasionally interposed when <term>malefic</term> <note>planets traditionally considered harmful, like Mars or Saturn</note> planets pass through these configurations. Likewise, they create moderate enmities which may happen to be reconciled if <term>benefic</term> <note>planets traditionally considered helpful, like Jupiter or Venus</note> planets intervene during a <term>revolution</term> <note>an annual update of the birth chart</note> or at another time. Nevertheless, consider the character, country, kinship, and fortunes of both; and thus judge the strength of the disagreement or agreement.

<margin>3</margin>
The agreement or disagreement of the Ascendants creates friendship or enmity based on pleasure and insult—that is, regarding the "good and joyful." For the Luminaries, it is in respect to honor and the choice of honest goods. But for the Part of Fortune, it is in respect to the necessity of use and business—that is, "useful goods." Note that friendship arises from the Sun rather for the sake of honor; from the Moon because of sensual habits, travels, and associations.

# *On the one who is the cause of friendship and hatred.*

## ARTICLE II.

<margin>1</margin>
The cause of friendship or hatred is that person in whose birth chart the <term>aphetic place</term> <note>the "life-giving" or most vital point in the chart</note>, or the succeeding place, is stronger than in the other person's. The "succeeding place" is that point toward which the <term>direction</term> <note>a method of timing life events</note> of the life-giver arrives.

# *Of the profit and loss of either person.*

## ARTICLE III.

<margin>1</margin>
He who has the aspect of a benefic star in the aforementioned place gains more abundantly from friendship, and is more greatly damaged by enmity,

## *On the time in which temporary friendship and enmity are contracted.*

### ARTICLE IV.

<margin>1</margin> In temporary friendships and enmities, consider when the stars of one person—especially the <term>aphetic</term> <note>original: "aphetica"; the "life-giver" or most significant point in a chart used to determine the length of life and major events</note> points—arrive at the locations where the other person has their own stars (and vice versa) by <term>direction</term>, <term>progression</term>, or <term>transit</term> <note>these are three different methods used by astrologers to "move" the birth chart forward in time to predict when events will happen</note>. For it is then that friendship or hatred is contracted, and they last as long as that celestial meeting does, until they are separated by 17 degrees, or until some other intervening star disrupts their decree. This separation in the case of <term>Saturn</term> <note>original: ♄</note> lasts about three years from the aphetic place, but not from the planet itself; for the others, the duration depends on the quality of their movement, as seen in the first book.

## *On the foundations of friendships and enmities.*

### ARTICLE V.

<margin>1</margin> Saturn and Jupiter, when entering one another's places, produce friendships through conspiracies, or agriculture, or hereditary successions. Saturn <note>original: ♄</note> and Mars <note>original: ♂</note> create them through quarrels and traps—even voluntary ones—and for the purpose of doing evil. Saturn and Venus <note>original: ♀</note> create them through marriage and kinship that quickly crumbles, and Saturn and Mercury <note>original: ☿</note> through bribery, gifts, trade, and the sharing of secrets.

<margin>2</margin> Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> and Mars create bonds for the sake of ranks and governance. Jupiter and Venus create them for the sake of public religious duties and oracles. Jupiter and Mercury create them for the sake of debates, teachings, philosophy, and similar things.

<margin>3</margin> Mars and Venus create bonds for the sake of loves, adulteries, and lazy leisure; these are, however, unstable and not very honorably established. Mars and Mercury create enmities, outcries, and lawsuits, defamatory pamphlets, and because of legal letters or drugs <note>original: "pharmacorum"; can mean medicines, poisons, or magical potions</note>—as I experienced during the <term>eclipse of the Venetian schism</term> <note>original: "eclipsi schismatis Veneti"; likely referring to the period of the Interdict (1606–1607), a major diplomatic and religious conflict between the Papacy and the Republic of Venice</note>.

<margin>4</margin> Venus and Mercury create close associations due to the study of the same art, or the sharing of music, literature, or divinations—or for the sake of women.

# *On the magnitude and stability of friendship and hatred.*

## ARTICLE VI.

<margin>1</margin> The magnitude and stability of friendship and enmity is identified by the exchange of planets near the <term>aphetic</term> <note>original: "aphetica"; these are the "life-giving" or most vital points in a birth chart</note> places—that is, the Sun, the Moon, the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>original: "fortunæ"; a calculated point in the chart representing prosperity and well-being</note>, the <term>Horoscope</term> <note>original: "horoscop"; here referring to the Ascendant or the starting point of the first house</note>, the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "M. C."; the highest point of the chart representing one's career and public standing</note>, or in the <term>angles</term> <note>the four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>. For in those places, these bonds are great and evident; elsewhere, they are small and obscure according to their distance from these points.

# *On recognizing the benefit gained from them.*

## ARTICLE VII.

<margin>1</margin> The benefit or harm arising from these relationships is known by inspecting the <term>benefics</term> <note>original: "beneficarum"; the "helpful" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> or <term>malefics</term> <note>original: "maleficarum"; the "harmful" planets, Saturn and Mars</note> in relation to these planets while they exchange places.

# APPENDIX.

## ARTICLE VIII.

<margin>1</margin> Enmity also arises from the exchange of planets, but in locations that are <term>opposite</term> or <term>square</term> <note>aspects of 180 degrees or 90 degrees, which are traditionally considered stressful or conflicting</note> from their <term>radical</term> <note>original: "radicalibus"; the positions of the planets at the exact moment of birth</note> positions. For example, if I have Jupiter in the 4th degree of Cancer and you have Mars in the 3rd degree of Cancer: when my Jupiter moves to the 3rd degree of Cancer and your Mars moves to the 4th degree of Cancer, enmity will intervene for the sake of honors or status. Furthermore, if the planets were enemies from the start and located in hostile signs—such as Mars and Mercury—they will produce enmity even when they exchange their own places, and not only when in opposition, because they are naturally antagonistic to one another.

This is especially true of those who have them in Libra, which is the serving sign to my own sign, Virgo.

<margin>5</margin> Every prince has one of his vassals who commands him due to the aforementioned elevation, strengthened by the <term>fixed stars</term>. An example is Tiberius and Sejanus <note>Sejanus was the ambitious prefect of the Roman Praetorian Guard under Emperor Tiberius</note>. If such a person is prudent and good, it will be good for the prince, as it was for Pharaoh from Joseph; if bad, it will be ill, as it was for Charlemagne from Ganelon <note>the knight who betrayed Charlemagne's rearguard at the Battle of Roncevaux Pass</note>. And these favorites often fall from grace because they are granted fortune by the fixed stars, which can also affect them with immoderate greed. If the wandering planets <note>the seven traditional planets</note> contradict them, their end will be bad, as it was for Alvaro de Luna under John II, King of Castile, and Haman under Ahasuerus, King of the Persians and Medes.

<margin>6</margin> It is good to serve princes whose nativity is compatible with your own; and conversely, it is bad to serve those whose is not. You shall count animals among either servants or riches.

## On the Manifold Ways of Attaining Fortune.

### ARTICLE II.

1 Great fortune is held in eight ways. First, when Fortune coincides with **Jupiter (♃)** happily situated: for then wealth flows in from every side. Second, if **Venus (♀)** is in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "M.C." (Medium Coeli); the highest point of the chart, representing status and career</note>, because she bestows goodwill, elegance, and gifts from this place. Third, if **Jupiter (♃)** is in the second house, because it rises toward the horoscope and brings good things, from which life is sustained. It also regards the Midheaven. Fourth, when the **Moon (☽)** is in the horoscope, because it makes men adaptable and skilled in business. Fifth, a <term>sextile aspect</term> <note>symbol: ⚹; a harmonious 60-degree angle</note> in the west, because it illuminates the horoscope, making men serious, pleasant, and in the end wealthy, such as **Nicolò da Ponte**, the Doge of the Venetians. Sixth, the separation of the Moon and its application to a "fortune" <note>a "fortune" or "benefic" refers to a lucky planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, especially if it carries a ray from Jupiter or Venus. Seventh, the conjunction of **Jupiter (♃)** and **Venus (♀)**, or with the **North Node** <note>original: "capite Draconis"; literally the Head of the Dragon, a point where the Moon crosses the ecliptic</note>, or with some fixed star of a benign nature, or with the Moon; or a benign star with Fortune, or the Sun or Moon in the <term>angles</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful areas of a chart</note>. Eighth, the exchange or harmony of Fortune, or of the Luminaries, or of the horoscope, with the birth chart of fortunate princes, or of the republic, or of the city, even if your own birth is not sufficiently fortunate. For a more general and greater constitution prevails. Thus, those who were not destined to die by their own <term>direction</term> <note>a predictive technique used to determine the timing of life events</note> die when the city is afflicted by a plague.

2 Draw out the contrary rules for poverty, by taking **Saturn (♄)** instead of **Jupiter (♃)**, and discord instead of harmony, and "falling" houses <note>original: "cadentes"; houses that are considered weak or unlucky</note> instead of the angles, and so forth.

## *Concerning wealth and poverty more specifically.*

->ARTICLE III.<-

1 The lords of the place of the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>original: "loci ⊕"; the planets that rule the zodiac sign where the Part of Fortune is located</note> grant very great wealth, first and foremost when they are in their own <term>essential dignities</term> <note>original: "dignitatibus"; positions where a planet is traditionally strong, such as its home sign or sign of exaltation</note>; second, when they are in a good position relative to the Sun; third, relative to the world <note>meaning their placement in the houses of the birth chart</note>; and fourth, when they are configured with <term>benefic stars</term> <note>the "lucky" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>, or when those benefics are elevated above them. Elevation increases wealth, but not character—which exists in the middle ground and is pulled toward extremes. For this reason, the most honest people are rarely the wealthiest.

2 Furthermore, if the wealthy are aided by the testimony of the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and the Moon</note>, they are also made illustrious in their success.

### *On the same subject from the configuration of the stars relative to the Part of Fortune and its lords.*

## ARTICLE V.

1 If stars of the same <term>sect</term> <note>original: "sectae"; the division of planets into Day (Sun, Jupiter, Saturn) and Night (Moon, Venus, Mars) groups</note> are configured with the governors of the Part of Fortune, they preserve and increase entire inheritances. If stars of the opposite sect are configured with them or are elevated above them, they ruin the inheritance.

2 If <term>malefic stars</term> <note>the "unlucky" planets Mars and Saturn</note> configured with the governors are in agreement, they will increase wealth through plunder, fraud, and wicked arts, especially when combined with Mercury (☿). If they are in discord, wealth will be snatched away by thieves, usurers, and tax collectors. If <term>benefic stars</term> <note>the "lucky" planets Jupiter and Venus</note> are configured or elevated and agree, they will increase and acquire riches through legal judgments, faith, honesty, and virtue. If they are in discord, wealth will be lost through the judgments of princes and the disdain of the owner.

3 Mars (♂) wastes wealth through quarrels, games, hunting, and squandering. Venus (♀) through luxury, banquets, prostitutes, delights, injuries, and idleness. Saturn (♄) through misfortunes. Likewise, Saturn with Mars (♂) and Mercury (☿) makes <term>alchemists</term>, who, by counterfeiting money, will eventually pay the penalty.

4 The Part of Fortune under the rays of the Moon increases riches; under the rays of the Sun, it does not rejoice in inheritance, as Ptolemy said in his second book. But to Cardano <note>Girolamo Cardano (1501–1576), the influential Italian polymath whose astrological commentaries are likely being referenced or written here.</note> it is not harmful; rather, when happily situated there, it grants stipends from kings. In <term>opposition</term> and <term>square</term> <note>harsh astrological aspects of 180 and 90 degrees respectively</note>, however, it brings the confiscation of goods and ruin.

5 The Part of Fortune with the Moon in the <term>horoscope</term> <note>original: "horoscopo"; in this period, the term specifically meant the Rising Sign or Ascendant</note> gives a robust life and increases the patrimony through contracts with men. But in a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> <note>harmonious aspects of 120 and 60 degrees</note> aspect with the Moon, it happens through public accounts; in the square and opposition, it brings loss from those same contracts and public accounts.

6 When the lords of the Part of Fortune are also the lords of one's <term>profession</term> <note>original: "opificij"; the work or craft a person performs for a living</note>, they grant wealth from that work according to their strength. And if they are malefics, they grant it through crime and fraud in the craft; but even more so if benefics bear witness, they grant wealth even when in the <term>angles</term> <note>the four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> outside of their own dignities, and even from the misfortunes of others. Many are enriched and glorified by their profession even without the Part of Fortune or the attendance of the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and Moon</note> in a happy placement.

->*On the timing of wealth.*<-

### ARTICLE VI.

1 **T**o track the timing of wealth, look at the position of the stars producing it in relation to the angles and the succeeding houses. For when they are in the centers <note>The "centers" or "cardinal houses" (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th) are the most powerful points in a birth chart.</note>, they grant wealth immediately; in the angles, they grant it in youth; in the succeeding houses, in middle age; and in the falling <term>cadent</term> <note>Houses that "fall away" from the angles, usually considered weaker or indicating later stages in life.</note> houses, in old age. Consider the same based on the quarters of the sky and their position relative to the Sun, as mentioned above. Likewise, judge from the speed of their motion and the short <term>direction</term> <note>A calculation used to predict the date of future events based on the movement of a planet after birth.</note> of the Part of Fortune itself.

2 Also <term>direct</term> the second house <note>The house of the zodiac traditionally associated with personal finances and possessions.</note>, and always consult the state of the lords of fortune during <term>transits</term> <note>The actual movement of planets through the sky as they pass over the positions they held at the moment of a person's birth.</note> and progressions. But in the direction of fortune, if a planet formed a bad <term>aspect</term> <note>original: "aspexit"; the geometric angle between two planets which determines if their influence is harmonious or conflicting.</note> at the beginning, it causes harm, even if the harm is not immediate; however, a planet that did not form a bad aspect does not cause such harm.

->*On ranks and honors in general.*<-

### CHAPTER XIV. ARTICLE I.

1 **S**ome are raised to high office because they harmonize with the monarch’s <term>nativity</term> <note>original: "genitura"; a person's birth chart or horoscope.</note>, as Herod Agrippa did with Caligula <note>Herod Agrippa I was a close friend of the Emperor Caligula, who granted him his kingdom.</note>. Others rise because they follow the general constitution of the kingdom, where sons and brothers succeed to the throne; this is known from the birth chart of the first king of that line, and we are not discussing those cases here. Rather, we speak of those who are raised by their own strength and fortune, such as Sforza <note>Francesco Sforza, a mercenary commander who became Duke of Milan.</note>, Castruccio <note>Castruccio Castracani, a famous soldier of fortune and Duke of Lucca.</note>, Julius Caesar, and Pompilius <note>Numa Pompilius, the legendary second king of Rome, chosen for his virtue.</note>. The birth charts of kings who rule by inheritance are not subject to the stars except regarding their life and character, but not regarding their kingship itself, which results from the general constitution of the state.

2 If a firstborn son has a birth chart that agrees with the general constitution of the kingdom, he will prevail in his rule: just as the planet Mars (♂) prevails in summer, because his own particular heat agrees with the general heat of the season. If, however, his chart is discordant, he will either lose the kingdom or govern it poorly; or another will be substituted for him, as happened with Celestine <note>Pope Celestine V, who famously resigned the papacy in 1294.</note> and Childeric <note>Childeric III, the last King of the Franks from the Merovingian dynasty, who was deposed for his perceived weakness.</note>. It is therefore better to appoint those who are more vigorous and who have a more effective birth chart as successors, rather than simply the firstborn.

# BOOK FOUR.

## On dignities acquired by the testimony of the stars.

### ARTICLE II.

1 **I**f both Luminaries <note>The "Luminaries" refer to the two brightest objects in the sky: the Sun and the Moon.</note> are in masculine signs and in an angle <note>The "angles" are the four most powerful points in an astrological chart: the 1st (Ascendant), 4th (Bottom of Heaven), 7th (Descendant), and 10th (Midheaven) houses.</note>, or if one is in an angle and especially well-placed by its condition <note>A planet is "conditionary" when it is positioned in harmony with its nature—for example, a diurnal planet like the Sun being above the horizon during the day.</note>, and is accompanied by five "wanderers" <note>original: "erronibus"; a traditional term for the five visible planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn) as distinguished from the fixed stars.</note>—those rising in the morning before the Sun, or setting in the evening after the Moon—those born under this will be kings, even if they were born as ditch-diggers, such as Sforza <note>Francesco Sforza (1401–1466), who rose from being a mercenary soldier to the Duke of Milan.</note>, Tamerlane <note>The Central Asian conqueror Timur (1336–1405).</note>, and Muhammad <note>original: "Macometus".</note>. This rule encompasses petty kings and the princes of cities, let alone those of provinces.

2 But if the attendants <term>satellites</term> <note>Planets that "guard" or accompany the Sun or Moon, acting as a royal entourage in the birth chart.</note> are simultaneously in an angle, or send their rays <note>The geometric "aspects" or connections between planets.</note> to the Midheaven <term>M. C.</term> <note>From the Latin "Medium Coeli," the highest point in the sky at birth, governing career and public reputation.</note>—especially "dexter" rays <note>Rays cast to the "right" or against the order of the zodiac signs, traditionally considered more powerful.</note>—as they ascend, they decree the empire of the world. This is what Thrasyllus predicted for Tiberius when they were at Rhodes, provided that the universal constitution <note>Mundane astrology, or the general "fate" of the era, which can override an individual's birth chart.</note> does not oppose it. For there cannot be more than one Emperor among the Christians; yet many possess such an attendant configuration. However, since it often harms their well-being, they die easily, and others reign in a different manner, such as Sejanus, who was the first man under King Tiberius. Sometimes many are elevated together, like the thirty tyrants under Gallienus, or the decemvirs and triumvirs at Rome. Likewise, as there are many planets, so there are many kinds of princedoms: for some rule through wisdom, such as Saint Thomas [Aquinas] now among the theologians, or Ptolemy among the mathematicians, because Mercury was the lord of their attendants. Others rule over commoners, like the captains of the Gypsies <note>original: "Cingarorum"; refers to the Romani people.</note> under Saturn. Others over priests or magistrates, such as bishops and deans of magistrates under Jupiter. Others over the more delicate and over women under Venus, such as abbesses, the chief eunuchs among the women of the Turks, and the Marabouts <note>Sufi Muslim religious leaders in North Africa.</note> among the Moors. Others over soldiers under Mars, or over thieves, or hardworking craftsmen. In every kingdom there are heads of people—marquises, dukes, and counts—whose status is hereditary in Christendom with succession, but in the Islamic world <note>original: "macometismo".</note> is without succession; the attendant configuration satisfies these ranks in the ways mentioned. But if someone has a most powerful constellation along with a comet and the favor of the Great Conjunctions <note>Rare alignments of Jupiter and Saturn that were believed to signal the birth of new religions or the fall of empires.</note>, he is raised above all princes, like Osman <note>original: "Ottomanus"; the founder of the Ottoman Empire.</note>, Tamerlane, Muhammad, and Attila [the Hun]. Yet they are not over the entire world; such an empire is said to be of a part, not of the whole.

3 In the aforementioned constellation, if the Sun alone is in a masculine sign and the Moon in a feminine sign, and one is in an angle and the other is outside it, they will be leaders

...only such princes shall be born who are masters of life and death, such as Caesar <note>Julius Caesar.</note>, Borgia <note>Cesare Borgia, the ambitious Renaissance prince.</note>, and Ezzelino <note>Ezzelino III da Romano, a 13th-century Italian ruler known for his cruelty.</note>.

4 But if a Luminary <note>The Sun or the Moon.</note> is in a masculine angle <note>The "angles" are the four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses. "Masculine" refers to signs like Aries, Leo, etc.</note>, but the attendants <term>satellites</term> <note>Planets that flank or "guard" the Sun or Moon.</note> are not in an angle, nor are they connected to the angles by aspect, the person born will be great due to the splendor of their birth, or through a high prefecture, or by the leading of an army; however, they will not hold a supreme leadership <note>original: "ducatu"</note> as in the previous rule—as was the case with Hannibal <note>The famous Carthaginian general who led armies but did not rule as a king.</note>.

5 If the Luminaries are not in the angles, but the attendants are in the angles or connected to them, the person will not attain the more illustrious dignities, but will remain within their own civil rank, being moderately eminent. For example, one born as a king stays within his kingdom; a senator stays in the senatorial order; a shoemaker in shoemaking; a blacksmith in blacksmithing—in which, however, they will somewhat excel among their peers.

6 If neither the Luminaries nor the attendants are in the angles, nor connected to them, the person born will be obscure and promoted to no dignities. This is true regarding honors that come from fortune <note>Inherited status or luck.</note>, rather than from virtues. For we see many who excel because of their virtues even without the testimony of a "planetary bodyguard" <term>satellitij</term>.

7 If neither Luminary is in an angle, nor in masculine signs, and neither is accompanied by any benefic planet <note>Specifically Jupiter or Venus, considered "good" influences.</note>, the person is born extremely lowly <note>original: "abiectus"</note> and unhappy in spirit. For insofar as they "fall" from the angles, they are prone to illness; insofar as they are in feminine signs, they are base; and insofar as they lack attendants, they are destitute of the favor and following of friends.

8 Other mixed conditions of men arise from these, which you should consider from the arrangement of the Luminaries, the "crowding" of planets <note>original: "stipationis"</note>, and the dominion of the attendants.

9 In the Luminaries, consider the houses, the succeeding and cadent houses <note>The houses that follow the angles (succedent) or fall away from them (cadent).</note>, their beginnings, middles, and ends; masculine, feminine, diurnal, and nocturnal signs; the equinoctial and tropical signs; the triplicities <term>trigonos</term>, dignities, and their position relative to the world. In the quality of the attendants, consider whether they are benefics or malefics, their harmony or discord, their position, dignities, and the testimony of the fixed stars.

10 The "soft" or effeminate <term>pathici</term> <note>original: "pathici". In this historical context, the author uses this term to describe men perceived as lacking masculine vigor or those with passive temperaments.</note> hardly ascend to kingship, nor can they protect it due to their softness, as with Sardanapalus <note>A legendary Assyrian king often cited as a symbol of decadence.</note> and Nero. However, Agathocles <note>The Greek tyrant of Syracuse.</note>, though categorized as such, became king because he had the Luminaries in feminine signs but had Venus in a martial state <note>Venus positioned in a sign ruled by Mars, giving her a more aggressive quality.</note>. European "soft" men are not as weak as the Asians described by Ptolemy <note>The 2nd-century father of Western astrology.</note>.

11 A crowd of attendants <term>satellitium</term> harms the character when the "lords of behavior" are shown to be malefic planets; it also harms health for the same reason, and because the Moon does not "rejoice" in a masculine sign. Likewise, I have found through experience that it is worse if all attendants are in the same sign; for when the progression <note>A technique for predicting future events in a life.</note> reaches the opposite point...

->*On dignities: their cause, strength, and quality.*<-

### ARTICLE III.

1 The **Lord of the Attendants** <note>original: "Dominus satellitij." The planet that rules over the group of planets flanking the Sun or Moon.</note> judges the nature of one's dignity. The Lord of the Attendants is, first, he who has a **chariot** <note>original: "carpentum." An ancient term for a planet that is exceptionally strong by being in its own sign or exaltation.</note> within that group, and aspects the Luminary, and is located in an **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses.</note>. Second, he who has a chariot and aspects. Third, then, the lord of the house; understand this as being "under the rays" <note>Within 15 degrees of the Sun.</note>. Fourth, the lord of exaltation. Fifth, the lord of the <term>triplicity</term> <note>The three signs of the same element (Fire, Earth, etc.).</note>. Sixth, the lord of the <term>term</term> <note>Specific degrees of a sign ruled by a particular planet.</note>. Cardano <note>Girolamo Cardano, the famous 16th-century physician and astrologer.</note> places the lord of the triplicity before the lord of exaltation, but not correctly, except in the case of a magistrate of a republic.

2 If the Lord of the Attendants is near <term>benefic</term> <note>The "helpful" planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> stars and is of the same condition, the native's dignity will be greater and more stable. If, however, it is configured with malefics, or with planets that do not agree with it, the dignity will be humbler and more uncertain. Therefore, the status is firmest: first, if a benefic is the Lord of the Attendants and is in agreement; second, if a malefic is in agreement; third, if it is a discordant benefic; fourth, if it is a discordant malefic. For the latter disturbs everything and increases evils.

3 See also whether the planet is in an angle, and in its own dignity, and "oriental" from the Sun, and in the Midheaven more than in the horoscope, and after that in the seventh house, then in the fourth; and see whether the <term>fixed stars</term> <note>Stars like Regulus or Aldebaran, as opposed to the "wandering" planets.</note> testify to it, etc.

4 The quality of the dignity is taken from the nature of the "overseer" among the attendants. Saturn, therefore, gives dignities through the force of resources and hidden riches; Jupiter and Venus through grace, gifts, rewards, magnificence, the priesthood, or a prefecture; Mars through expeditions, victories, and the terror of one's subjects; Mercury through intelligence, erudition, care, and the orderly management of one's affairs; the Moon, when she presides, [makes] an illustrious...

->On Occupations.<-

### CHAPTER XV. ARTICLE I.

1 The first planet emerging from the Sun’s rays <note>A planet making its "heliacal rising" when it first becomes visible in the morning sky after being hidden by the Sun's glare.</note> which is also the lord of the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>The 10th house, representing career, social standing, and public life; abbreviated as M.C.</note> at the same time—especially if it applies to the Moon—is the significator of the occupation. The sign of the "governor" indicates the specific property of the occupation. The governor is the lord of the significator’s location, or a planet in a mathematical relationship with it. This same governor indicates the quality of the occupation.
2 If the same planet is not both emerging from the rays and the lord of the Midheaven while applying to the Moon, take the one that emerges from the rays and is in the Midheaven; or if that is not found, take the one that merely emerges from the rays.
3 For if one planet emerges from the rays, another is in the Midheaven, and another applies to the Moon, choose them all: but the first is most powerful, then the second, and then the third. And when there are several of the first type, take the more powerful one; and similarly from the two aforementioned categories, take the one who has more "votes" <note>original: "fuffragia"; refers to the sum of astrological strengths or "dignities" a planet possesses.</note> in its favor.
4 But if no planet is in the Midheaven, nor rising in the morning before the Sun, we shall take the lord of the Midheaven who is stronger as the significator of the practice, office, or study. For these individuals are usually occupied with a craft. Thus, office, study, and practice take the place of a craft. For even kings are sometimes craftsmen, just as Nero devoted himself to music and Philip of Spain <note>Philip II of Spain, known for his patronage of the arts and personal interest in painting and architecture.</note> to painting, when they have an "oriental" planet <note>A planet rising before the Sun.</note> among the attendants in the culminating point of the sky.
5 Nothing prevents people from becoming craftsmen even without these celestial considerations. For Ptolemy speaks affirmatively, not negatively; and he teaches natural inclinations, not arbitrary upbringing. St. Thomas <note>Thomas Aquinas, the medieval theologian who reconciled astrology with Christian doctrine by arguing that stars influence the body and "lower" passions, though not the free will.</note> attributes the order of artistic things and the efficacy of the craftsmen to the influence <note>original: "afflatu"; literally a "breathing upon" or inspiration.</note> of the stars.

<header>BOOK FOUR.</header>

## On the property of the underlying matter in an occupation according to the signs.

### ARTICLE II.

1 The governors of the occupation, and likewise its qualifiers, are Mars ♂, Venus ♀, and Mercury ☿, when they rule the locations of the significators; however, the material property of the occupation is discerned from the signs in which these governors are found.

2 Contemplative arts <note>Theoretical or philosophical pursuits rather than manual labor.</note> pertain to the tropical and equinoctial signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; the "cardinal" signs that mark the changes of the seasons.</note>; moral arts to the human signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius.</note>; those that imitate nature to the aquatic signs; and those that polish or refine materials relate to the four-footed signs. Take the tropical and equinoctial indications from the position of the Sun, and the others from the constellations.

3 Indeed, human signs indicate operations that are performed through art and science, and which pertain to human use. Four-footed signs <note>Signs representing animals, such as Taurus (the Bull) or Leo (the Lion).</note> relate to metalwork, commerce, construction, and the smithing arts. Tropical and equinoctial signs relate to matters of exchange and transport, as well as geometry, physics, metaphysics, agriculture, and medicine. Earthly and aquatic signs relate to water-based and damp things, such as maritime work and herbalism. Likewise, they indicate fishing, the trade of salted goods, and funeral matters.

---

## On the quality of the occupation from the governors.

### ARTICLE III.

1 The essence of the occupation is derived from the significator emerging from the [Sun's] rays; or it is investigated from the signs. The quality [of the work] is determined by the governors of the signs and the specific signs where those governors are located.

2 Mars, Venus, and Mercury are more mobile than the other planets, and since the arts are performed through the movement of both mind and body, they are the qualifiers. Mars ♂ governs the laborious arts of the <term>power faculty</term> <note>Associated with the "irascible" or spirited part of the soul.</note>; Venus ♀ governs the pleasurable arts of the <term>appetitive faculty</term> <note>Associated with desire and the "concupiscible" part of the soul.</note>; and Mercury ☿ governs the industrious arts of the <term>cognitive faculty</term>, as described in the *Ethics* <note>Refers to Aristotle's *Nicomachean Ethics*, which classifies the different parts of the human soul and their functions.</note>. Mixed planets govern mixed occupations. Haly <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer.</note> however also makes the planets themselves significators, but not by a correct reasoning. Nevertheless, the same planet can be both a significator and a qualifier. The other planets are configured to assist in qualifying the nature of the work.

## On the characterization of the individual planets mentioned.

### ARTICLE IV.

1 **Mercury** ☿ produces scribes, grammarians, accountants <note>original: "à rationibus"; a title for those in charge of financial records</note>, teachers, merchants, money-changers, diviners, astrologers, sacrificial priests, and generally those occupied in literature, interpretation, and in the "giving and receiving" <note>An idiom for bookkeeping or trade.</note> of business. The same with **Jupiter** ♃: lawmakers, rhetoricians, sophists <note>Teachers of philosophy and rhetoric.</note>, priests, great men, and those who consort with the powerful. The same with the **Sun** ☼: physicians, diviners, those in charge of the accounts and councils of kings, and writers on the governance of princes. The same with the **Moon** ☽: diviners, orators, couriers for princes, mail-carriers, printers, actors, and those devoted to public service.

With **Mars** ♂: masters of gladiators, military strategists, and armorers.

If **Mars** ♂: cooks, procurers, those who command women and submissive men <note>original: "pathicis"; refers to passive partners in same-sex relations, here noted in a contemporary cultural context.</note>, as is the custom among the Turks and Moors.

If the **Sun** ☼: tutors of princes, and those wise in political and divine matters.

If the **Moon** ☽: diviners, the leisured class, fullers <note>Those who clean and thicken cloth.</note>, washerwomen, keepers of public baths, etc. Consider these things according to the planet’s place, dignity, and position relative to the Sun and the world, as we discussed when treating the governors of character.

With the **Moon** ☽: couriers, travelers, hunters, and night-walkers. Distinguish these according to the position and the zodiac signs.

### ARTICLE VII.

## *On travel and journeys.*

### CHAPTER XVI. ARTICLE I.

1 The significators <note>planets representing a specific topic</note> of journeys are the **Sun** ☉, since it signifies the whole person; the **Moon** ☽, because of its mobility; **Mars** ♂, since it incites movement through its heat; and **Fortune** <note>the "Part of Fortune," a calculated mathematical point in a chart</note>, since for its sake we undertake everything, and it is derived from the Luminaries.

2 The locations in which the significators are placed that grant journeys are the western angle <note>the descendant or 7th house</note>, because it signifies death, and absence—the substitute for death; likewise all cadent houses <note>houses 3, 6, 9, and 12, which "fall away" from the angles</note>, but especially the ninth for long journeys, and the third for small ones. But our Tobias <note>likely a specific individual or case study known to the author</note> has his significators in the fifth and the fourth, and the Duke of Nocera <note>original: "Dux Nuceriæ"</note> in the sixth and seventh—both of whom traveled through all of Europe.

3 **The Moon** ☽, says Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century foundational authority on astrology</note>, gives travels when located in the seventh house and in all cadent houses.

4 **Mars** ♂ does the same in the seventh, and in the ninth when the **Sun** ☉ is cadent, according to Cardano <note>original: "ex Cardano"; referring to Girolamo Cardano, a famous 16th-century Italian physician and astrologer</note> (but he is mistaken) when it is configured to the Luminaries by opposition, square, or antiscion <note>a mirror-image relationship across the solstice points of the zodiac</note>. The birth chart of our Bina <note>likely another case study</note> contradicts these things.

## *On the directions toward which travel is indicated.*

### ARTICLE II.

1 The **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note>, **Mars** ♂, and **Fortune** <note>the "Part of Fortune," a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and fate</note> located in the oriental quadrants—namely the first and third—grant travel toward the east and south; in the occidental quadrants, they grant travel toward the west and north. Understand this sometimes as distinct directions, and sometimes mixed, according to the nature of the location.
2 Consider the latitude <note>the vertical distance from the ecliptic</note> of the **Moon** ☽ and **Mars** ♂, whether it be northern or southern, ascending or descending. From these, you will recognize simple and mixed directions.

## *On the length and short duration of journeys.*

### ARTICLE III.

1 The more the significators <note>the specific planets or points indicating travel</note> are in cadent houses and in the seventh house, and the more of them that are in movable signs, the longer and more frequent the travels that are indicated. The opposite is also true. Look also at the configurations <note>the geometric relationships or "aspects" between planets</note>.
2 Observe also that those who have the **martial star** <note>the planet Mars</note> in their horoscope <note>the first house or the rising sign</note> are very frequently stirred to travel.
3 Regarding the signs in which the significators of the journey and the governors <note>the planetary rulers</note> of those significators are located, as well as the houses that signify travel—such as the seventh and the cadent houses—add also the subject of the journey, which is the horoscope <note>the rising sign</note>. If these are of a single form <note>original: "unius figurae"; signs represented by one body, like Leo or Taurus, often indicating stability</note>, they rarely grant travel, and only when it is convenient. If they are **bicorporeal** <note>original: "bicorporea"; double-bodied signs like Gemini or Pisces</note> and multiform, they grant travel more often, continuously, and for a long duration.

In **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which represent stability or stubbornness</note>, they indicate danger through precipices and windstorms. In **tropical and equinoctial signs** <note>the cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn, which mark the turning of the seasons</note>, they indicate danger through lack of resources and failing health. In **human signs** <note>signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius</note>, the danger comes from robberies, ambushes, and the violence of rulers. In **earthly signs** <note>specifically animal or "beastly" signs like Taurus or Capricorn</note>, through attacks by wild beasts or earthquakes. And if **Mercury** ☿ joins them, the dangers will include perilous accusations, the bites of reptiles and other venomous creatures, and **meteorological afflictions** <note>original: "meteorologicas passiones"; severe weather events or atmospheric disturbances</note>.

# *On the Quality of Death in General.*
## CHAPTER XVII. ARTICLE I.

1 We said, when we were dealing with the span of life, that a person dies when the chief <term>apheta</term> <note>original: "apheta"; from the Greek for "releaser," this is the specific point or planet in a birth chart that carries the life force</note> reaches—through direction, or through strong progressions and **transits**—the western angle <note>the Descendant, where the sun sets</note>, or its own **square** <note>an aspect of 90 degrees, often considered stressful</note>, or the body of the **malefics** <note>the "unlucky" planets, Saturn and Mars</note>, or their oppositions, squares, and <term>antiscia</term> <note>points in the zodiac that are mirrored across the axis of the solstices</note>; or when it reaches the Sun, Moon, and Mercury if they are imbued with the rays of the malefics. Now, however, it remains to discuss the quality of death.

2 One must consider the stars that follow, or apply to, or precede the <term>interfector</term> <note>original: "locum interficientem"; literally "the killing place," the point in the chart that indicates the end of life</note>. You shall judge the type of death according to their nature, combining their significations according to the nature of both the **zodiac** <note>original: "signiferi"</note> and the **terms** <note>specific subdivisions of the zodiac signs ruled by different planets</note>.

3 Therefore, neither the "killer" planet itself, nor the sign it is in, nor the lord of that sign, nor a planet configured to the killer, actually defines the *quality* of the death.

4 Instead, the first qualifier is the "succeeding" place <note>the house following the one where the killing point is located</note>, or a planet succeeding it in the order of the signs. The second is the lord of the **term** of that degree in which the fatal direction occurs. The third is the sign of the killer. The fourth is the star or planet configured to the succeeding place. These qualifiers are called <term>prothanati</term> <note>original: "prothanati"; from the Greek for "before death," these are the astrological factors that determine the circumstances of one's passing</note>.

## *On violent death in general.*

### ARTICLE III.

1 We have already spoken concerning natural death occurring from <term>prothanators</term> <note>original: "prothanatis"; from Greek *prothanatos*, refers to the celestial points or planets that signify the end of life or the "taker of life" in a birth chart</note> situated in places suitable to themselves, where no power is able to render the end more malignant or more notable than what has been overcome. Now we shall speak of violent death.
2 A violent death is decreed when either of the <term>malefics</term> <note>original: "maleficus"; refers to the planets traditionally considered "unlucky" or harmful, specifically Saturn and Mars</note> holds dominion over the killing place, or gazes upon it with a hostile nature—that is, when it is not the ruler of that specific place.
3 Likewise, when the malefics have afflicted both <term>Luminaries</term> <note>original: "Luminaria"; the Sun and the Moon</note>, or the prothanator, through a conjunction, a hostile aspect, an <term>antiscion</term> <note>original: "antiscio"; a point of astrological reflection across the solstice points (Cancer/Capricorn)</note>, or by rising above them; in such cases, the death will be public, by reason of the involvement of the Luminaries.

## *On violent death specifically from Saturn.*

### ARTICLE IV.

1 Just as the type of death is known from the gaze of the stars toward the prothanators or the Luminaries—or from either of the malefics looking upon them—and from the signs occupied by the malefics both within the Zodiac and outside of it: so too the magnitude of the death is recognized from the Luminaries, especially when they are <term>cadent</term> <note>original: "cadentibus"; planets in the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, which were traditionally seen as weakened or "falling"</note>. In those positions they are more heavily affected, and the malefics more easily rise above them; these stars cause death most surely and most cruelly when they are located in the <term>angles</term> <note>original: "angulis"; the four most powerful points of a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</note>.
2 Therefore, **Saturn**, when striking the Sun against its condition with a <term>square</term> <note>original: "quadrato"; an aspect of 90 degrees, considered stressful or hostile</note> or some other dire gaze in **fixed signs** <note>Leo, Taurus, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note>, indicates those who are to be crushed or suffocated by a multitude of people, if he kills in this way and the Moon follows.
3 But in **bestial signs** <note>original: "feralibus"; signs representing wild animals, such as Leo or the latter part of Sagittarius</note>, he indicates those who will be torn apart by wild beasts.
4 And with the support of **Jupiter**, if the <term>anaereta</term> <note>original: "anæretæ"; the specific planet in a chart that acts as the "destroyer" or "killing planet"</note> is imbued with an evil influence, he indicates those who are publicly exposed to wild beasts.
5 When positioned in the setting [the West], opposite to either the Sun or the Moon, he indicates death in prison.
6 This same **Saturn**, configured with **Mercury** in serpentine or terrestrial signs, kills by the bite of venomous creatures. If **Venus** is added to this configuration, death comes through poisonings and the deceits of women.
7 This same **Saturn**, configured with the Moon in water signs or in **Virgo**, causes suffocation by water, and near the constellation **Argo Navis** <note>original: "Argo nauem"; the "Ship Argo," a large southern constellation since divided into smaller parts</note>, he causes death by shipwrecks.
8 **Saturn** in the <term>tropical signs</term> <note>original: "tropicis"; Cancer and Capricorn, which mark the solstices</note>, when joined to the Sun or configured hostily, or when opposite to **Mars**, decrees those who will be crushed by ruins [of buildings]; especially—

9 Therefore, three things are required for Saturn to cause death in this way. First, that it be hostile to the <term>prothanator</term> <note>original: "prothanato"; the planet or point in a birth chart that signifies the end of life</note>. Second, that it strikes the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun or the Moon</note> or Mercury (if Mercury is the ruler of Mars's position) in a hostile manner. Third—though not in every case, but for the most part—that it be in the setting <note>the Western horizon</note> or the midheaven <note>the highest point of the sky in a chart</note>.

10 Therefore, if in the <term>radix</term> <note>the original birth chart</note> the planet does not rule over the <term>aphetic</term> <note>original: "aphetico"; refers to the 'giver of life' or the point that determines the lifespan</note> place that produces such an effect, this death is not promised. Likewise, Saturn will not kill unless from the beginning it strikes a Luminary or the prothanator; for this reason, we predict death for children right from the start when we see them frequently falling from heights or being wounded. For whenever a <term>malefic</term> <note>original: "maleficij"; a planet like Saturn or Mars traditionally viewed as harmful</note> has any power, it is prepared for a future death. I have seen four people so far who were mutilated in a brawl and then killed some time later.

11 Consider also the configuration of the fixed stars and the type of death common to the region; for the Italians do not hang a nobleman, but behead him. The Turks impale them on a stake.

# On violent death from Mars.

## ARTICLE V.

1 Mars, affecting the Sun contrary to its condition, or hostilely opposed to the Moon in signs of human form <note>astrological signs depicting humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius</note>, kills by sedition, war, or by one’s own hand.

2 If Venus bears witness to this, she adds the involvement of women to the killing.

3 With Mercury involved, [death is] by pirates, robbers, or sorcerers.

4 In mutilated or imperfect signs, or near the Head of Medusa <note>original: "caput Medusæ"; refers to the fixed star Algol, traditionally associated with misfortune and beheading</note>, it decrees those who are to be mutilated or beheaded.

5 In Scorpio and Sagittarius, [it decrees death] by burnings, incisions, or by the <term>revulsions</term> <note>original: "reuulſionibus"; a medical procedure intended to draw 'corrupt' humors away from a diseased area, which could be fatal if it went wrong</note> of doctors.

6 In the midheaven or the bottom of the sky <note>the *Imum Coeli* or fourth house</note>, it signifies those to be crucified, especially near Cepheus and Andromeda <note>constellations in the northern sky</note>. In place of the cross, the stake, the wheel, or the gallows are now used.

7 Opposite the setting of the horoscope <note>the Western horizon</note>, it signifies those to be burned alive.

8 In quadrupedal signs <note>signs depicting four-legged animals like Aries or Leo</note>, [it signifies] those who will die by a fall or by being torn apart.

9 And if a corrupted Jupiter bears witness, the death is of a noble kind—that is, by legal condemnation and the wrath of princes.

10 Mars in the first house also caused burning, because it aspected the seventh house and [was] in the midheaven.

->Concerning violent death from a double malefic influence.<-

### ARTICLE VI.

1 Two malefic planets simultaneously opposed to one another increase the cruelty of death in the aforementioned constellations.

2 The nature of this increase is recognized by the "prince" or ruler of the <term>killing place</term> <note>original: "loci interemptorij"; the specific point in a birth chart that indicates the end of life</note> when many factors coincide, both in general kind and in magnitude, whenever both planets have some relationship to the killing places. For such individuals are even deprived of burial and are consumed by wild beasts or birds, depending on the nature of the signs in which the malefics are found, provided there is no <term>benefic</term> <note>a helpful planet, such as Jupiter or Venus</note> above the earth to intervene in the killing places.

3 Therefore, the "slayer"—who is always a malefic by essence or by office—and another malefic attacking the killing place, create a violent death. The <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and Moon</note> do not determine the nature of this death but rather illuminate and increase its intensity; however, the lord of the killing place declares the specific quality of the death's increase. This ruler is not the primary <term>prothanator</term> <note>original: "prothanatus"; the planet signifying the onset of death</note>, as that is the succeeding ray of the second malefic which increases the death; rather, it is either the second prothanator, who is the lord of the <term>term</term> <note>a specific sub-division of a zodiac sign</note> or the sign itself. Furthermore, the sign declares the type of death: whether it involves wild beasts, water, serpents, and so on.

->Concerning death outside one's homeland.<-

### ARTICLE VII.

1 Those whose planets occupying the killing places "fall from the <term>angles</term>" <note>original: "cadunt ab angulis"; positions in the chart—the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses—traditionally associated with weakness, illness, or travel away from home</note> die abroad; this is especially true if the Moon, as the lady of journeys, is involved or looks upon the place with hostility. That is to say, when the planets following the <term>anaeretic</term> <note>original: "anæreta"; the "destroying" planet that ends life</note> place, or the lord of the second prothanator, are in these <term>cadent</term> <note>falling</note> houses, they signify absence, especially if the Luminaries are involved and do not aspect the <term>horoscope</term> <note>original: "horoscopum"; here referring specifically to the Ascendant or the Eastern horizon of the birth chart</note>.

2 The <term>Arabs</term> <note>referring to the influential medieval Islamic astrological tradition</note> consider whether the lord of the eighth house, which they dedicate to death, is disconnected from the horoscope. This is not without merit, if such power truly resided in the eighth house; however, since death is enacted from the anaeretic place, it is the lord of that specific place that must be considered.

# BOOK FOUR.

3 I saw a man beheaded by a violent axe who had **Saturn** (♄) in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "M. C." or "Medium Coeli"; the highest point in a birth chart, representing public life and career</note> with the **Sun** in **Aquarius**, at the time when a <term>progression</term> <note>a method used to predict the timing of life events</note> infested by malefics reached an opposition to **Mars** (♂), who was in the ninth house in **Capricorn**. I saw another who had **Saturn** in the Midheaven with <term>Azimech</term> <note>the star Spica; generally considered fortunate, but here joined with Saturn</note>, striking the **Sun** in the west in **Cancer** by a square aspect, and the **Moon** in the east in **Capricorn**. This man was tortured with dreadful torments and fire due to the <term>antiscion</term> <note>original: "antiscio"; a "shadow" point or reflection of a planet across the solstice axis</note> of **Mars** in **Virgo**, on account of **counterfeiting money** <note>original: "monetæ adulteratæ"</note>; and even now he remains in danger of hanging. Both of these men died outside their own country. **Pontius**, however, was killed by **Mars** in the tenth house, as evidenced by an afflicted <term>horoscope</term> <note>here meaning the Ascendant or the rising sign at birth</note> and the testimony of the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note>.

4 **First**, look at the time of death. **Second**, see whether at that time the <term>significators</term> <note>planets or points that represent a specific area of life</note> indicate a journey. **Third**, see toward which region it leads, and how long it lasts. **Fourth**, conjecture from the hour of death in what place along that journey the person might be, and you will have the location. **Fifth**, see whether the death is natural or violent. **Sixth**, see whether it is public; for if so, it will occur in a metropolis. If it is done in secret, it will be on the road or in a country villa. **Seventh**, consider the causes of death and the specific type in that place—whether by the gallows, the axe, or other means.

5 Those who have **malefics** <note>harmful planets, Saturn or Mars</note> following the <term>killing place</term> <note>original: "loco interemptorio"</note>, but from a distance, will die a "middle death"—somewhere between natural and violent—such as from extreme fear or from a poorly applied medicine.

6 There is also a noble natural death, such as that of **Chilo the Wise** <note>one of the Seven Sages of Greece, said to have died of joy</note>, which occurs when there is only one "slayer" planet and no malefic is configured against it, but rather a **Luminary** is involved with rays that are neither hostile nor afflicted by malice.

# ON ASTROLOGICAL MATTERS
## BOOK FIVE.
### Concerning the timing of celestial events.

---

->*In addition to universal causes, particular ones must be considered simultaneously regarding the timing and nature of events.*<-

### CHAPTER I. ARTICLE I.

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'E' featuring a human figure (putto) entangled in floral and vine motifs.</image-desc>

<margin>1</margin> The effects of universal causes <note>original: "vniuersalium causarum"; forces that affect everyone, such as the seasons, climate, or major historical shifts</note>, and those that come before, are modified by particular causes <note>original: "particularibus causis"; factors specific to an individual, such as their birth chart or physical health</note>, but they are not removed or hidden. However, the effects of particular causes are hidden by universal ones, even if they are not entirely removed; indeed, they are often taken away.

<margin>2</margin> No star can prevent the **Sun** (a more universal cause) from producing heat when it is in **Cancer** (♋) and **Leo** (♌) <note>the height of summer in the Northern Hemisphere</note>. Neither cold **Saturn** (♄) combined with the **Moon** (☽) will be able to remove or hide that heat at that time, but only to moderate it slightly. Similarly, in **Ethiopia**, **Jupiter** (♃) will not make those people white whom the burning Sun makes dark <note>original: "fuscat"; the author argues that local climate and biology (universal causes) override individual planetary influences</note>. Nor can the most favorable encounter with **Mercury** (☿) during infancy make a small boy a teacher; for the cause of infancy <note>the biological stage of life</note> is more general and takes precedence. It can, however, show some shadowy outline <note>original: "vmbratile"</note> of his future knowledge. Conversely, the **Sun** can hide and remove the cold of **Saturn**, and it can override the "whiteness" of **Jupiter** in **Ethiopia**; likewise, the softness of the **lunar age** <note>the first stage of life, traditionally ruled by the Moon, representing infancy</note> can sometimes take away the clever nature of a boy.

<margin>3</margin> For this reason, it is no wonder if a plague kills many citizens without the agreement of their individual <term>nativities</term> <note>original: "natiuitatum"; a person's birth chart or horoscope</note>, or with very little connection to them—just as in a war, or the sinking of a ship which kills many people sailing in it, whom a <term>direction</term> <note>original: "directio"; a mathematical method used to predict when a specific event in a birth chart will occur</note> did not otherwise condemn to death. For all of these individuals are subject to a **general constitution** <note>original: "constitutioni generali"; a collective fate or a larger environmental event</note>.

<summary>This page introduces Book Five by explaining the hierarchy of astrological influence, arguing that universal forces (like the seasons, climate, or collective disasters) override the specific predictions found in an individual's birth chart.</summary>
