...place the **Sun** ☉ in conjunction with the malefic planets <note>Saturn and Mars</note>, especially with the <term>apheta</term> <note>original: "apheta" — the planet or point in a birth chart considered the "giver of life," used to calculate longevity and health.</note>.

3 While the **Moon** ☽ is applying to <note>moving toward an aspect with</note> **Venus** ♀, **Jupiter** ♃, or **Saturn** ♄, it is not useful to take a purging medicine. This is because the first two planets promote digestion rather than evacuation, while the latter [Saturn] causes the retention of the <term>humors</term> <note>The four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which pre-modern medicine believed governed health.</note>.

4 Commit yourself more safely to **Mars** ♂—the stimulator of the humors—along with **Mercury** ☿, provided you do not fear the discharge of blood.

5 Do not touch the vein of any limb or part of a limb with iron <note>the surgeon's blade</note>, nor apply medicine to any limb, while the **Moon** ☽ is in the zodiac sign ruling that limb—for example, **Aries** ♈, which rules the head.

6 When you wish to treat limbs and internal organs dedicated to specific planets, place the planet that rules that limb in "direct" motion <note>moving forward</note>, in the east, and in its own "dignity" <note>a position of astrological strength</note>, so that it may strengthen that limb; also place it in an <term>angular house</term> <note>The most powerful positions in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses.</note>.

7 When you apply cleansing and restrictive medicines, let the **Moon** ☽ be "thirsty" in dry signs. When applying soothing and purging medicines, let her be in moist signs and increasing in light, for you require moistening. She should not be in "fixed" signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note> when humors are to be moved, nor in "movable" signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> when they are to be stopped.

8 Let the Moon not be in dry signs when we are treating obstructions or hardening; nor in moist signs when we are clearing away an abundance of humors—except when we are purging them so that they flow downward. She should not be in aerial and windy places when we are expelling inflammations. She should not be in "cut" signs <note>signs associated with sharp edges or division</note> when we are treating wounds and incisions. She should not be in fiery signs when we are cooling inflammations and driving out diseases arising from them.

9 Above all, however, take care that a <term>retrograde</term> <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually viewed as a sign of weakness or corruption.</note> malefic planet is not in the place of the <term>apheta</term>, the indicator of the disease, or in the sign ruling that disease. If you cannot avoid this, postpone the treatment and use the benefit of the lunar cycles.

10 When you wish to anesthetize a limb or cut it from the body, place its planetary ruler and its zodiac sign in <term>cadent houses</term> <note>The weakest positions in a chart: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses.</note>, slow in motion, and "empty" <note>without significant connections to other planets</note>.

11 When you visit a sick person, cast an astrological chart for the moment they first took to their bed. Consider the **Moon's** ☽ applications to and separations from the malefic or beneficial planets, the speed of its motion, and its light. Thus, from the relationships to the place where the Moon was at the start of the illness, you will judge whether the change leads toward health or ruin. You will also judge the <term>crises</term> <note>The turning points of a disease.</note> and symptoms—whether they favor or hinder the illness. For "critical days" are not determined by simple counting, but by the Moon's aspects, whether they occur quickly or slowly. See the rest in our medical writings.

12 As for astrological plates <note>original: "laminas aſtrologicas" — metal talismans engraved with celestial symbols for healing or protection.</note>, although **St. Thomas Aquinas** <note>original: "D. Thomas" — the influential 13th-century theologian.</note> may approve of them regarding their material and form, we deliberately omit them here.

BOOK SIX.

### *On Generation.* <note>original: "In generatione" — referring here both to the act of procreation and the resulting birth.</note>

### ARTICLE III.

1 **Y**ou shall begin marriages and banquets when **Venus** <term>♀</term> is "direct" <note>moving forward in the zodiac, not retrograde</note>, oriental <note>rising in the east before the Sun</note>, in an "angular" position <note>located in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of a chart</note>, and in her own "dignity" <note>a sign or degree where she has natural strength</note>. Also, ensure the "Luminaries" <note>the Sun and Moon</note> aspect each other well, especially in royal and fortunate signs. Furthermore, if you are able, ensure the **Moon** ☽ is "applying" <note>moving toward an aspect</note> from **Jupiter** <term>♃</term> to **Venus** <term>♀</term>. Above all else, ensure that the <term>apheta</term> <note>the planet or point designated as the "giver of life"</note> and the <term>horoscopus</term> <note>the Ascendant or 1st house</note> are not afflicted by the "malefics" <note>Saturn and Mars</note>.

2 At the hour of generation <note>conception or birth</note>, place the **Moon** ☽ in a fertile sign, and place a beneficial, masculine planet in the <term>M. C.</term> <note>original: "Medium Coeli" — the Midheaven or 10th house, representing the highest point in the sky</note> if you desire a male child; a feminine planet if you desire a female. If that planet is in the 11th, 4th, or 5th house, it will likewise be good, provided it is not harmed by the "malefics." It will be even better if the **Moon** ☽ reconciles the light of the **Sun** ☉ and other planets to that specific planet at the same time. Do not worry as much about a <term>satellitium</term> <note>original: "satellitio" — a group of planets clustering around another like a royal retinue</note> as you do about good aspects.

3 When you wish to engage in coitus and desire to know the future of the offspring, or to cooperate with fortune, calculate the movements of the planets for the 9th month ahead. If you desire a wise son, choose **Venus** <term>♀</term> with **Mercury** <term>☿</term> in an oriental position and in a good aspect, with **Saturn** <term>♄</term> in a "human sign" <note>Signs with human forms, such as Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius, believed to favor intellectual and social qualities.</note>. Engage in coitus so that such a constellation will be present nine months later when the child is born. Similarly, if you desire a ruler of others, choose a time for intercourse such that after nine months the **Sun** ☉ is accompanied by a retinue of "benefics" <note>Jupiter and Venus</note> and by "royal stars" <note>fixed stars like Regulus or Aldebaran</note> in an "angle" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> and in a masculine sign. You shall work similarly for other goals, observing which planetary alignments are suitable for which fortune or physical build, and when they will occur, as was said in the previous books. For if God should cause a seven-month or eight-month birth, you have done what was yours to do in the ordinary course of nature. For just as when you sow grain, you do what you ought and what you know, and you commit the outcome to God. It is foolish to choose a time for the breeding of animals and the planting of trees, but not for the generation of humans.

4 It is also necessary to consult the "significators of children"—those planets that rule the <term>M. C.</term>, the 11th, the 4th, and the 5th houses—at the moment of intercourse, and to choose them when they are in a good state. In this way, the stars will serve you, and not you the stars.

# *On Kingdoms, Cities, and the State.*

## CHAPTER IV. ARTICLE I.

**1** A **King** is not dated from his coronation, but from the moment of his father’s death, or of his election: and at that moment, cast the figure <note>the astrological chart</note>. Consider the **Sun** <term>☉</term>, the <term>M. C.</term>, and all the <term>aphetas</term> <note>planets or points designated as the "givers of life" or vitality</note>, and from those, gather what shall happen in the kingdom. It is not within the judgment of men to make a king fortunate, for they do not choose when they wish, but when they reach an agreement—which does not happen suddenly—or when a predecessor dies, which is in the will of God.

**2** A man can found a **City** whenever he wishes. Therefore, place "fixed" signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, associated with stability and endurance</note> in the four angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of the chart</note>, and **Leo** in the <term>M. C.</term> or in the horoscope <note>the Ascendant or 1st house</note>, and the lords of the angles in a good aspect to the <term>Luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and Moon</note>: and you shall make the **Sun** <term>☉</term> the apheta, or some "heavy" planet <note>a slow-moving planet like Saturn or Jupiter</note> the lord of the time.

**3** **Saturn** <term>♄</term> is best in a good position, if the Luminaries and all the planets "apply" <note>move toward an aspect</note> to him. For he signifies the longest duration, and that the riches, honors, and weapons of kings and peoples will serve that city. **Jupiter** <term>♃</term> will be similarly powerful and good. Omit the "light" planets <note>the Moon, Mercury, and Venus</note>, since they are judges of only a short time. **Mars** <term>♂</term> in a good position with a retinue <note>original: "satellitio" — a group of surrounding planets</note> and dignity will make a city victorious. The slowness of "anomalies" <note>long-term planetary cycles</note> favors these matters.

**4** In founding a **Republic**, do not make the Luminaries the <term>aphetas</term>, since they subject the state to kings; but rather **Saturn** <term>♄</term> with a fixed sign suitable to him. Let there be "common" signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note> in the angles, and their lords in a good state relative to the world, the **Sun** ☉, and their "dignities" <note>the signs where they have the most power</note>. Also make the "heavy" planets the aphetas, to which the Luminaries apply.

[...lu]minaries: and just as in a kingdom the first "triplicity" <term>triangulus</term> <note>original: "triangulus"; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element, used here to categorize types of government</note> of the **Sun** and **Jupiter** is praised, so in a republic the third triplicity, which belongs to **Saturn** <term>♄</term> and **Mercury** <term>☿</term>, is favored. In all these matters, consider the preceding lunation <note>the New or Full Moon immediately prior to the event</note>, so that it matches the "nativity" <note>founding horoscope</note> of the republic; consider also the physical site. For in maritime regions we choose "watery" signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note>; on land, dry signs and those representing cattle or horses, or whatever best suits the city's way of life.

### *On the election for passing a law.*

#### ARTICLE II.

<margin>1</margin>
**C**hoose the assembly of the people during the New Moon <note>original: "nouilunio"</note>, as the Psalmist says, and as the Hebrews do when they celebrate their new moon festivals <note>original: "neomenias"</note>, because that is when something new is initiated. Place **Mercury** <term>☿</term> safe from the "malefics" <note>the planets Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with misfortune</note> and in a good position, and place the equinoctial signs <note>Aries or Libra</note>, which are suitable for new laws, in the <term>M. C.</term> <note>the Midheaven, the highest point of the chart representing authority</note>, and place **Jupiter** there. But when a law is not being passed for the first time but is being preserved, choose "trine" or "sextile" aspects of the **Moon** and "fixed" signs <note>signs like Taurus or Leo that represent stability</note>. Avoid those signs that represent the "beginnings of things" <note>Cardinal signs</note>, lest you find yourself occupied with changing the laws every day, as the Republic of Florence once was. <note>A reference to the frequent constitutional upheavals in Renaissance Florence.</note>

### *On changing location.*

#### ARTICLE III.

<margin>1</margin>
**W**hen a malefic planet passes through the "altitude" <note>likely the degree of exaltation</note> of the planet that serves as the "significator" <note>the planet representing the entity</note> at the start of a kingdom, republic, or city—especially if that planet is "retrograde" <note>appearing to move backward</note> or "stationary"—and even more so if it is hostile to that sign (as **Saturn** is to **Aries**, **Cancer** <term>♋</term>, and **Leo** <term>♌</term>), then everyone subject to that sign will suffer. This is also true for anyone who has such a birth chart. In such a case, it is good to move to another region, provided your own birth chart does not share that same significator; for if it does, moving will likely be of no help.

### *On the election for battle.*

#### ARTICLE IV.

<margin>1</margin>
**W**hen a battle is to be joined, place yourself in the direction where **Mars** <term>♂</term> is located. For example, if **Mars** is in the East or the North, position yourself and your army to the East or the North. For it is evident that just as the **Sun** turns the "hair" of the trees <note>the foliage/leaves</note>, so **Mars** directs the animal spirits. Observe also the latitude, and always arrange your army from that side, so that the planet's influence is behind you or with you, and not facing against you.

2 Observe that the **Sun** strikes the backs of your army, but the face of the enemy: for it will urge you to pursue and them to flee with its rays; furthermore, it blinds their eyes so they do not see those they must strike, while it does not dazzle yours. Thus the **Sun** and the planets fought at Cannae <note>The Battle of Cannae (216 BCE), where Hannibal defeated the Romans; historians often note that the wind and sun favored the Carthaginians</note> for the Carthaginians, who had their backs to the **Sun** as it climbed above the eastern horizon, against the Romans who were looking directly into it. Perhaps Deborah also sang of this: "The **Sun**, **Moon**, and stars remaining in their order fought against them." <note>original: "Sol & Luna & ſtellæ manentes in ordine ſuo, pugnauerunt eos"; a reference to the Song of Deborah in Judges 5:20 regarding divine celestial intervention in battle</note> You shall observe the same with the **Moon**.

3 When you are forced to fight in this way, you should uncover your polished iron garments <note>highly polished armor</note> and shields, so that at least the reflected rays might harm and terrify the eyes of the enemies.

4 When a comet appears, or a portent in the sky, interpret it for the soldiers as being in your favor; and place yourself where the movement of the comet or portent began, not where it arrived, and imitate its course.

5 Victory varies in turn where **Mars** <term>♂</term> <note>The planet traditionally associated with war, energy, and aggression</note> changes its latitude and motion, or begins to go retrograde <note>the apparent backward motion of a planet in the sky, often interpreted as a time of redirected or weakened energy</note>. Observe this. Caietanus <note>Tommaso de Vio, known as Cardinal Cajetan (1469–1534), a prominent theologian and commentator</note> writes on chapter 12 that Guido Bonatti <note>Guido Bonatti (c. 1210–1296), the most famous professional astrologer of the 13th century</note>, having selected the auspicious hour, went out with the army from Faenza and slaughtered the enemies.

6 Beware of fighting when **Mars** <term>♂</term> is in a hostile aspect <note>a geometric angle between planets, like a square (90°) or opposition (180°), thought to cause tension or conflict</note> to your horoscope <term>horoscopus</term> <note>here referring to the Ascendant or the "rising sign" of the commander's birth chart</note>, or the significator <note>the specific planet representing a person or an objective</note> of the matter for which you must fight. In the 7th house <note>the section of the chart representing open enemies</note>, it is very harmful if received in the horoscope, but it favors you if it is in a good aspect with the Lord of the Horoscope.

7 If you have an "unhappy" <note>meaning poorly positioned or negatively influenced by other planets</note> **Mars** <term>♂</term> in your root <term>radice</term> <note>the "radix" or original birth chart (nativity)</note>, abstain from military service, and from every matter signified by any other planet that you have in an unhappy state.

### ARTICLE V.

1 Begin buildings intended to endure when the four "fixed" signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; signs associated with stability and permanence</note> occupy the four angles <note>the four most powerful points of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</note>, especially the 4th, and when the heavy planets <note>Saturn and Jupiter, which move slowly and represent long-term structures</note> are well-configured among themselves and toward the angle.

However, to finish a building, speed is required.

3 If to these you add a benefic planet <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> in the <term>M.C.</term> <note>Medium Coeli or Midheaven; the highest point of the chart representing the building's public presence and success</note> and the **Moon** flowing from it toward the 4th house, it will be most fortunate.

Thomas <note>Saint Thomas Aquinas</note> in his book *On Fate*; see also the *Metaphysics* <note>Aristotle's work on the nature of reality and causation</note>.

## On the choosing of navigation.

### ARTICLE VI.

1 Observe the properties of the sea in which you sail. For thick water is more disturbed by summer heat, as in the Persian Sea; thin water by winter; and average water by the middle quarters, as is evident in the Indian Sea. Some have a flow and ebb <note>tides</note> from the **Sun**, like the Ocean; some increase along with the **Moon**, like the English Sea. He who is ignorant of these things incurs shipwrecks.

2 When you are about to sail, place the **Ascendant** <term>horoscope</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the start of an event</note> in a moist sign in the fourth house, and in it place **benefic** planets <note>traditionally Jupiter and Venus, thought to bring good fortune</note> by their presence or by a friendly aspect: or place the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> in aspect with the **benefics**, especially those that are **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward in the sky, which here is considered protective</note>, safe from the **malefics** <note>traditionally Saturn and Mars, thought to bring hardship</note>.

3 Observe the lunar cycles as we taught in Book 3, as well as the quarters of the year, the **alignments** <term>syzygies</term> <note>The conjunction or opposition of two celestial bodies, particularly the Sun and Moon</note> of the planets, and the portents of the sky, and indicators of winds and storms. Look there: for we must not linger here since enough has been said there regarding the changes of the elements.

## On the choosing of a journey.

### ARTICLE VII.

1 For a journey, place the significators of your **natal chart** <term>genesis</term> <note>The planetary positions at the moment of one's birth</note> in a good position, and the **Moon** moving swiftly, flowing from them toward the **benefics**. Or vice versa.

2 You will desire the **Ascendant** in the 3rd, 5th, or 9th house, safe from the **malefics**, and from which the **Moon** flows by her body or a friendly ray, increased in light and speed, and in **movable** signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; signs associated with initiation and movement</note>.

3 Also observe imminent storms according to the doctrine in Book 3, lest they overwhelm you on the way.

---

## On elections for agriculture.

### CHAPTER V. ARTICLE I.

1 First inspect which regions, in which quarter of the year, and under which lunar cycles and **fixed stars** sowing, plowing, and harvesting should be done. For under the equator they harvest twice in a year, since they have a double summer: and after the withdrawal of the **Sun** from the equator they plow and sow: and in its approach they reap. For excessive heat accelerates the ripening of crops. In Egypt, however, slightly outside the tropics, they sow after the flooding of the Nile in September, and they harvest—

...which occurs in April. In the coldest regions they sow in March and April. For the sprouts do not survive in winter, but are extinguished by the excessive cold. However, they harvest at the end of July, because they have long days which ripen the harvest along with our own crops, as in Muscovy <note>modern-day Russia</note>, Poland, etc. But in Italy, we sow during the autumnal quarter, when the Sun wanders at the end of <term>Libra ♎</term> and in <term>Scorpio ♏</term>: and we harvest at the end of June.

2 The reason for all this is that ripening occurs through significant heat and dryness: whereas for sowing, a mild and humid time is required: and for rooting, a cold that drives the <term>seminal power</term> <note>the internal vitality or "virtue" of the seed</note> toward the depths, but does not kill it. Therefore, according to the changes of heat, cold, and the moderate states between them, the proper method of sowing, plowing, and harvesting is observed.

3 If you sow in soft, watery soil, choose the waning of the **Moon**, and a time when it is below the earth and in dry signs. Otherwise, excessive moisture will rot the seeds. You should do the exact opposite when you commit seeds to dry and sandy soil.

4 Always place a fertile sign in the 4th <note>the Fourth House of an astrological chart, which governs land, crops, and hidden treasures</note> and ensure an aspect of the **benefic** planets.

5 Observe the quality of the year from its four quarters, noted from the entry of the **Sun** into the <term>cardinal points</term> <note>the equinoxes and solstices</note> and the preceding lunations: and before you sow, perceive what the time of harvest will be like by considering the quarterly moon phases, eclipses, comets, and the time when those decrees of fate are executed: and thus you will sow those seeds, and in those lands, which you know will be aided by the constitutions of the heavens. However, those things which you foresee will be afflicted by blight, mists, frost, dire heat, or rains and adverse winds, you shall not commit to the earth.

6 By this reasoning **Thales** <note>Thales of Miletus, a pre-Socratic philosopher often cited as the first to use logic and observation to predict natural events</note> was enriched; understanding from the moon phase at the rising of the **Dog Star** <note>original: "Canicula" (Sirius)</note> that little oil would be harvested, he bought up all the oil from the previous year and sold it the following year for triple the price. We handed down these rules in the third book. For a man is enriched both by guarding against future losses and by preserving or selling off previous fruits, according as he foresees plenty or scarcity.

7 When you sow, choose a humid time and a fertile lunation configured with **benefic** planets: a cold winter, so that the crops may strike deep roots. For flowering, choose the times of fertile winds—which vary from region to region—based on long observation of the stars. When you harvest, choose a dry and hot constitution of the air.

8 In our region, the rising of the **Pleiades** <note>original: "Vergiliarum"</note> indicates the sowing of summer seeds: but their setting indicates the sowing of wheat and crops: the setting of **Lyra** <note>original: "Fidiculae"</note> or **Aquila** <note>the Eagle constellation</note> opens the spring and the pruning of vines; the opposite time is for burning the stubble.

## BOOK SIX

9 When the **Dog Star** <note>original: *Canicula*; the star Sirius, whose setting was linked to summer heat</note> sets in April, the **Robigalia** <note>an ancient Roman festival involving sacrifices to avert *robigo*, or agricultural blight/mildew</note> are held by the Romans, for at that time mildew usually takes hold of the crops. Shortly after, the **Floralia** <note>a festival in honor of Flora, the goddess of flowers</note> occurs; if a full moon happens then, it kills the crops and flowers. It does the same to grapes at the rising of the **Dog Star**, and to olives when they are blooming. **Democritus** <note>a Greek philosopher who wrote on agriculture</note>, however, fears for the olives and vines at the rising of the **Pleiades** <note>original: *Vergiliarum*; a cluster of stars used to mark the seasons</note>, while others fear it at the evening rising of the **Eagle** <note>the constellation Aquila</note>. During its morning rising, there is fear for the winter and early crops, about which more is said in Book 3.

10 Country folk are ignorant of the stars, except through plants. For the **heliotrope** <note>literally "sun-turner"</note> and the **lupin** turn along with the **Sun**, and they indicate the hours of the day. The turning back of the "hair" <note>the foliage or leaf-surfaces</note> of the linden, olive, and poplar indicate the solstices precisely, but especially the flowering of **pennyroyal** <note>original: *pulegij*; a medicinal herb</note>; when dry, it indicates the winter solstice <note>original: *brumam*</note>, that is, the entry of the **Sun** into **Capricorn ♑**, while the thistle indicates the entry into **Cancer ♋**. The budding of the **mulberry** is a certain sign that the cold has passed; the appearance of **fireflies** marks the rising of the **Pleiades**, as does the blooming of beans, or the departure of the little bee to its pasture. The arrival of the **swallow** brings spring, as does the setting of the **Lyre** <note>original: *Fidiculæ*; the constellation Lyra</note> and the **west winds** <note>original: *fauonios*</note>. The falling of tree leaves marks the setting of the **Pleiades**. But these traditions celebrated by the Romans do not entirely correspond to our current time, except for those signs taken from plants. See Book 3.

11 I know not what <term>sympathy</term> <note>the idea that all parts of the universe are interconnected and "feel" together</note> exists between us and the entire order of nature. For when the grape is trodden, battles usually rage and human blood is often shed. When vineyards are pruned, it has been observed that human heads are cut off and suffocating <term>catarrhs</term> <note>excessive buildup of mucus or respiratory illness</note> spread. When trees bloom, the "seeds" of the body and mind swell and flourish, and they are incited toward certain fruitfulness. When they are harvested, we become sterile; hence the sign of **Virgo ♍** is called sterile. When many winds blow for a long time, we are gathered into the inner chambers of our houses, and then the worst counsels are formed; hence women are accustomed to predict treacherous plots. These things are not without reason: for even if it happens by accident regarding fertile causes that this herb blooms at the same time as that one—as **St. Thomas** <note>Thomas Aquinas</note> says in his commentary on the 6th book of the *Metaphysics*—yet in respect to the heavens, it has a cause. For the stars infuse similar physical states into all bodies, but they are modified according to the type and quality of those receiving them.

12 You shall plant trees when the **Moon** is in fertile signs, increasing in light <note>waxing</note>, and above the earth, in dry and sandy soil; do the opposite in wet soil. In average soil, choose a fertile sign and a **Moon** that is either waxing below the earth or waning above it.

13 Choose terrestrial signs, such as **Taurus ♉**, for the planting of trees; but not **Leo ♌**, because they become sterile. **Aquarius ♒** is suitable for tall trees, such as the fir, beech, and oak; for these do not grow in marshes.

14 Graft trees <note>original: *Inferes arbores*; refers to the technique of joining a plant shoot onto a rootstock</note> when the **Moon** applies to fertile planets, and the lord of the tree is in a good state. For it is said that every plant belongs to its own specific planet.

15 It is most beneficial when a fertile planet applies to a fertile **retrograde** planet <note>a planet that appears to be moving backward in the sky, often interpreted as intensifying its influence</note>, so that a robust "double application" occurs; this is better by **body** <note>original: *corpore*; a physical conjunction or very close proximity</note> than by **ray** <note>original: *radio*; an astrological aspect or beam of light from a distance</note>.

16 These same rules hold true for transplanting.

17 Gather grain and fruit when the weather is dry and the **Moon** is in her decrease <note>waning</note>. Do the same for grapes. Otherwise, they will wither and rot, being affected by too much moisture; unless this is done immediately in the spring, when moisture is stirred up by the heat. They also become prone to worms unless gathered in dry weather. A hanging grape, however, withers suddenly.

### *Selection for the cutting of timber.*

#### ARTICLE II.

1 Wood from which you wish to weave ships, or cover houses, and support floors for a very long time, you should not cut except when the **Sun** is furthest from our regions <note>during the winter solstice</note>, and the **Moon** is waning and below the earth. For then the woods are most solid, and not at all prone to worms or rot. For this reason, they best choose a fading **Moon** before the entry of the **Sun** into **Capricorn ♑**; for then the **Sun** is furthest from us and still receding, and the timbers lack moisture.

2 If, however, you cut wood that is meant to rot, or to be more suitable for firewood, choose the spring when the **Sun** approaches us, and a waxing **Moon** above the earth.

3 If you wish to cut a forest, or trees and branches, so that they may sprout back and bud better, do the same during a waxing **Moon**; for clearly, a man who shaves his beard at that time immediately recovers it longer and faster. In a "thirsty" **Moon** <note>original: *in sitienti*; referring to a dry, waning Moon</note>, the opposite occurs.

### ->On the selection of days.<-

#### ->CHAPTER VI.<-

1 The Egyptians had **auspicious** <note>original: *faustos*; lucky</note> and **inauspicious** <note>original: *infaustos*; unlucky</note> days; they worked on the former and were cautious on the latter. The Romans did the same. This has its basis in observation, because the deeds performed on such days turned out unfortunately for them. For this reason, they avoided the fourth day before the Nones <note>referring to the *Dies Alliensis*</note>, because they fought unsuccessfully at the Battle of **Allia** <note>A disastrous Roman defeat by the Gauls in 390 BCE</note>. There are also others for whom **Saturday** <note>the day of Saturn</note> is harmful, or **Tuesday** <note>the day of Mars</note> for others. On certain days they obtain fortunate successes, and on others unlucky ones; therefore, it must be seen whether reason and experience support this.

2 We read in **Ecclesiasticus** <note>A book of the Bible also known as the Wisdom of Sirach</note> that God blessed some days and cursed others, and thus it seems this doctrine has its origin from God. Furthermore, I can swear that all the great evils I have endured in the world happened to me on **Friday** <note>the day of Venus</note> and **Tuesday** <note>the day of Mars</note>; good things on **Sunday** <note>the Lord's day</note> and **Wednesday** <note>the day of Mercury</note>; some mediocre things on **Monday** <note>the day of the Moon</note> and **Thursday** <note>the day of Jupiter</note>. Yet the evils of those [bad] days turned into good, just as conversely the good of the others [often turned out poorly]. Seven times I was subjected to **torture** <note>original: *tormento applicatus fui*; the author, likely Tommaso Campanella, spent decades in prison for his political and religious views</note>: always on a day of **Mars** <note>♂</note> or **Venus** <note>♀</note>. Every time I was captured, or afflicted, or suffered treachery, it was a day of Mars or Venus. Hence, I am forced to be cautious of these days. Likewise, the illustrious **Mendoza** family in Spain undertakes nothing on a **Tuesday** <note>day of Mars</note> because it always turns out unfortunately for them. For this reason, they have a privilege from the magistrate of the **Holy Inquisition** <note>the ecclesiastical court for the suppression of heresy</note> to be cautious on this day without being branded with superstition. If this is granted to them without superstition, why not to others? Nor can we say that in such days the **apheta** <note>the "life-giver" or planet that determines the length of life and vitality in a chart</note> meets with malefics. For this is impossible and against experience. Nor that the devil modifies the course of fate in such a way that on such days...

# ASTROLOGICAL MATTERS

...does us harm. For the devil cannot pervert the order of things, as the Fathers of the Church testify. It is therefore necessary to assign the rules of the planets to certain days, which the Babylonians were the first to do; and the Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans followed them. For we give the first day to the **Sun**, the second to the **Moon**, the third to **Mars**, the fourth to **Mercury**, the fifth to **Jupiter**, the sixth to **Venus**, and the seventh to **Saturn** in the week, following such ancient observance that it has not been overturned even by the most scrupulous Christians. It has its foundation, therefore, in truth. Hence, God is said to have created the world in seven days, which he dedicated to the planets.

2 But the days are not named according to the sequence of the planets <note>The astronomical order from the furthest to the nearest is usually Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon</note>. For in that case, we would begin with <term>Saturn</term> <note>original symbol: ♄; the furthest and slowest of the traditional seven planets</note> and end with the Moon. Instead, they are named according to the sequence of the twenty-four hours. By counting from the beginning of the day of the Sun, it happens that the first hour of the following day is given to the Moon, and the first of the subsequent day to Mars, and so on for the others. For they use unequal civil hours <note>A system where both the day and night are divided into 12 hours regardless of the season, meaning an "hour" in summer was longer than an "hour" in winter</note>, and every day and every night each has twelve hours.

3 Indeed, I hesitated much on this point; I can neither condemn such an ancient tradition, nor fully approve of it. Hence, Saint Thomas <note>Thomas Aquinas</note> in a short work <note>original: *opusc.*, referring to an *opusculum*</note> responding to this question, says that nothing is established against the faith, nor for the Catholic faith, from this naming and partitioning of days after the planets; and the theologian need not care too much about these things. I would do the same, were it not that the completion of this science urged me on. And although I have said that the names of idols should be wiped out from the days and months in prophetic writings, I do not say the same for the planets, if they can be understood physically in them.

4 Truly, if God established the number seven at the very beginning of things—and in beginnings lie the progress, the ends, and the things themselves—and if He placed the seven planets within the theater of the fixed stars for the mutual governance of things (for even if the Sun is assumed to be at rest, it may still be considered a moving governor), then surely there shall be a "week" of years corresponding to these same planets, and a week of months, and of days, and of hours, and again of centuries, and of millennia. Hence David said that a thousand years are like a single day. And the Apostle Peter repeats the same. And in Daniel, weeks of years are given, as well as of decades, and centuries, and even of tens of thousands. Furthermore, the Rabbis, testifying to Elijah, assert the same: that the Messiah is to come in the fourth millennium, because the Sun (his type and symbol) was created on the fourth day. And truly, Christ came around the end of the fourth millennium. But who can keep the account of the days, and months, and hours, and weeks from the beginning of the world, which is unknown to us due to the variety of chronologies?

However, let us not deny what is known to us regarding the lordships of the planets.

5 I believe, therefore, that in the first <term>millennium</term> <note>a period of one thousand years</note> **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> presided, which is why writers celebrate the "Golden Age" under his rule; in the second, **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>; in the third, **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>; in the fourth, the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>; in the fifth, **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>; in the sixth—in which we now live—is **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>; and in the last will be the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, when all things shall be transformed. Or, if you prefer to model the ages of the world after the ages of a human being, begin from the Moon. For in the fourth age, the world would also be governed by the Sun. One must proceed in this way through centuries, decades, weeks, months, and specific locations; and if you consult the histories, experience does not contradict this. Look to the prophetic writings.

6 That the planets obtain such influence is attested by the laws of nations, as **Haly** and **Cardanus** <note>Haly Abenragel and Girolamo Cardano, two of the most influential astrologers in the medieval and Renaissance traditions</note> have noted. For the Hebrews have **Saturnine** <note>original: saturninos; refers to traits associated with Saturn, such as discipline, gloom, or deep contemplation</note> customs, and they received their law in Egypt under the <term>trine</term> <note>an astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, considered harmonious</note> of Saturn and Mercury. Therefore, they observe the Sabbath on the day of Saturn: because, as **Ficino** <note>Marsilio Ficino, the Renaissance philosopher who sought to reconcile Hermetic astrology with Christianity</note> says on the testimony of the Rabbis, Saturn is unsuited for external actions and is unlucky, but is well-suited for the contemplative life. Therefore, on the day of Saturn, one should be free for divine matters, and God—who established this according to the nature He created—should be appeased, for He rested from His works on the day of Saturn. Likewise, the Hebrews are eloquent, religious, and merchants because of **Mercury**. Indeed, every law clings to the Hebrew law, and proves its own dogmas from its figures and books; for every law requires exposition and reasoning, which is granted to Mercury. Furthermore, every planet <term>applies</term> <note>an astrological term for one planet moving toward an aspect with another</note> to Saturn, and not the other way around. 

The Christian Law, because it began under the trine of the **Sun** and **Jupiter**, cherishes piety, purity, chastity, and all virtues, and it celebrates the day of the Sun, which is a <term>type</term> <note>a symbolic foreshadowing</note> of the Messiah. The Muhammadan law <note>original: Macometana</note>, which began under the trine of **Mars**, **Venus**, and the **Moon**, is full of luxuries, impurity, and variability. It holds the Moon as its insignia and observes the day of Venus <note>Friday</note>. It appears, therefore, that all human affairs have the planets either as causes, co-causes, or types; and thus we shall philosophize concerning the days.

7 But the distribution of the week based on the series of hours does not follow the same sequence as the planets' natural order. Perhaps we run through the millennia of the world in a similar fashion. This, however, must be examined through histories: for from the character of any given time, it is possible to recognize the ruler of that time, just as we recognized the signs and ruling planets from the days of the market in the first book, at least in part.

8 But against this doctrine is the **Apostle** <note>Referring to St. Paul in the New Testament (Galatians 4:10), who cautioned early Christians against returning to the superstitious observance of "days and months and seasons and years"</note> condemning those who observe days and years. Similarly, in the **Decree of Gratian** <note>The fundamental collection of Canon Law for the Catholic Church, compiled in the 12th century</note>, those who observe "Egyptian days" are condemned.

9 I respond that the Apostle <note>St. Paul, specifically referring to Galatians 4:10: "You observe days and months and seasons and years."</note> condemns those who superstitiously observe days and the new moons <note>original: "neomenias"</note> of the Old Law as if their salvation depended upon them. He does not, however, condemn those who observe them for physical reasons, or by the ordinance of God or the Church. Otherwise, we would not correctly observe the day of Easter; nor would a Jewish leper rightly abstain from pork if he did so for physical <note>health-related</note> rather than moral <note>religious</note> reasons. The Popes condemn those who superstitiously worship the "Egyptian days" <note>traditionally unlucky days marked on medieval calendars</note>, but not those who observe them physically. For it is well known that just as beans are not sown in summer—for if they are, they bear no fruit because the constitution of the heavens is then contrary to them—but are rightly sown in December when the heavens are favorable; so too, I should not undertake a task on a day that is unfavorable to me due to the succession of a planet's lordship. For even moral affairs are suited or unsuited to certain times and constellations, at least in a preparatory sense <note>original: "dispositive"</note>, as we have said. The demon knows this well, as St. Thomas <note>Thomas Aquinas</note> testifies. Therefore, I believe the Inquisitors have indulged the **Mendoza** family <note>original: "Mendozinis"</note> in such observations. Furthermore, I say that Egyptian days are worshipped superstitiously when people assume they are equally lucky or unlucky for everyone.

10 But when will you recognize a day as lucky or unlucky for yourself? From your own experiences, good and bad. But what if **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> and **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> are contrary to me, even if in my birth chart <note>original: "genesi"</note> Venus is oriental to the **Sun** <note>rising before the Sun</note> and is the ruler? I respond that both Venus and Mars are in their <term>fall</term> <note>a position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is weakened; original: "casu"</note>: Venus in **Virgo** <note>original symbol: ♍</note> and Mars in **Libra** <note>original symbol: ♎</note>. Therefore they are unhappy, especially since Venus is in the <term>twelfth house</term> <note>the area of the chart associated with hidden enemies and self-undoing</note>. Whoever has a planet so unhappy must consider its day.

11 **Haly Abenragel** <note>a famous 11th-century Arab astrologer</note>, because a ship set sail from port during the hour of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>, predicted a shipwreck for it, and so it happened. But he did not act with enough prudence. That event occurred based on the slightest suspicion, since the lordships of hours and days are indicators of the smallest importance. It would have been better to consider the <term>lunation</term> <note>the current phase and position of the moon</note> and the "nativity" <note>the moment the keel was laid or the ship launched</note> of the ship, along with many other things that are customary.

12 For this reason, I maintain that only the slightest suspicions—not proofs or even probabilities—can be drawn from the lords of hours and days. The Church of God counsels us better: that with God as our leader, we should undertake our affairs through prayer rather than through these innumerable and most frequently futile observations, which are often superstitious because they are false, and the demon can insert himself into such vain practices.

13 Therefore, when God is said to have blessed or cursed certain days, it is understood in respect to us, not to time itself. For it is clear that a fire that burns us is "cursed" to us, as is a thorn that pricks us, even though in themselves all things are "very good." So it is with days. Thus, the day of his birth was cursed by **Job** <note>referring to Job 3:3</note>—cursed for him, not for the day itself—because he then fell into mise-

### BOOK SIX ###

...falls into human miseries. Therefore, the author of Ecclesiasticus <note>The Book of Sirach in the Old Testament</note> speaks relatively, not absolutely.

14 It is better to look toward the favorable constellations according to your birth chart <note>original: "genituram"</note> than toward these hourly governances. However, if all things align, it will be for the best.

15 The Hebrews ask how the moral days of the Christians agree with natural ones, since the whole Law of Moses is adapted to Physiology <note>In this context, "Physiology" refers to the study of the laws of nature and the physical world</note>; and therefore, they believe their law should be preferred above all others, because their God is proven to be the same creator of both nature and law. I respond that the author of nature is the founder of both the Hebrew and the Christian law. In the former, He expressed the planets and the signs of heaven, but in the latter, He declared them more beautifully. The Lord’s Day <note>Sunday</note> is observed because the world and light began on it, and after the week of the ages of time, there will be rest in it through a return to the first principle. In the Sabbath <note>Saturday</note>, however, there is no return. The Sun is the lord of the stars, not Saturn (♄). Likewise, the moveable feasts are in great harmony with nature. We celebrate Easter <note>original: "Pascha"</note> at the first lunation, when Christ rises, and when the trees and dead seeds <note>OCR "femina" is likely "semina" (seeds), referring to the spring germination</note> rise again. We celebrate the Ascension when things—with heat prevailing—emit spirits and breaths upward. We celebrate the Coming of the Holy Spirit when much solar heat descends upon us. We celebrate the Advent of Christ when we hope for the return of the Sun before the winter solstice <note>original: "brumam"</note>. Christ’s birth occurs when the Sun begins to return to us; and the birth of Saint John occurs when the Sun begins to recede, as Augustine says: because John said, "It is necessary for me to decrease, but for him to increase" <note>John 3:30. This refers to the summer and winter solstices.</note>. We celebrate Lent <note>original: "Quadragesimam"</note> when the Sun is in the sign of Pisces. And when the humors <note>The four bodily fluids thought to control health and temperament</note> are overflowing, we fast for our benefit. In the morning of the year Christ rises—Spring is the morning. At midday He ascends to heaven and sends the Spirit—Summer is the midday. In Autumn, Matthew writes his Gospel of the one departing, as if in the evening and the old age of the year. In the winter solstice, which is the decrepit age, Christ is born, and at midnight, when the day begins to grow. Twelve Apostles are assigned to the twelve months. Matthias is inserted in the leap year <note>original: "bissexto," the intercalary day added to the calendar</note> in place of Judas. The Blessed Virgin, like the Moon, grows through fifteen mysteries. Those who have some skill will investigate these things; for indeed, this is the method of St. Augustine in his sermon on St. Job.

# OF ASTROLOGICAL MATTERS

## On elections in general.

### CHAPTER VII.

1 In every action, consider its **ruling planet** <term>significator: the planet that represents a specific person, object, or activity in an astrological chart</term> in the **root of your birth chart** <note>original: "genesis radice"</note>: and see how it stood at the beginning of your life regarding good and evil; and in those matters where you find that planet **unfavorable** <note>original: "infœlicem"</note>, you should abstain. For example, one who has Mars (♂) in a **dishonorable position** <note>original: "despecto loco"</note> should not become a soldier. But if it is favorable, or at least not unfavorable, see how it stands at the start of the action in relation to the Sun, the world, the **angles** <term>angles: the four most powerful points in a chart—the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term>, its **essential dignities** <term>dignities: the strength a planet gains by being in certain zodiac signs</term>, and its configurations; if it is well-placed, proceed; if poorly, do not begin.

2 When the **governor** or **life-giver** <term>apheta: a planet designated as a primary indicator of life, status, or a specific area of interest</term> of honor, or wealth, or health, etc., moves from one sign to another, cast a chart: and see which planet aspects it, or is in its place. From that, judge the matter signified for the person born, or the king, or the city. For instance, if Saturn (♄) is in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M. C." (Medium Coeli)</note> looking upon the governor in the 7th house, the subject, king, or city will be neglected by its own people because of greed. And if the **birth chart** <note>original: "radicalis figura"</note> is weak, he will suffer from betrayals. But nothing is worse than if a **retrograde** <term>retrograde: when a planet appears to move backward in the sky, usually considered a weakening or "malefic" influence</term> **ill-fortune** <note>original: "maleficus" (referring to Saturn or Mars)</note> passes over the place where the significator is **exalted** <term>exaltation: a specific sign where a planet's influence is most powerfully and positively expressed</term>.

3 The worst arrangement is when Saturn (♄) is placed in **opposition** <term>opposition: an aspect where two planets are 180 degrees apart, often indicating conflict</term> to Mars (♂), and one of them is the governor: or if both are retrograde and joined together, looking poorly upon the significator—especially when the significator is in the **west** or **under the Sun's beams** <note>original: "sub radiis Solis," meaning so close to the Sun it cannot be seen</note>: or if they are joined, opposed, or in **square aspect** <term>quadrantur: a 90-degree angle between planets, representing tension</term> to the significator. Consequently, the nature of the damage corresponds to the sign in which the significator is afflicted. For in **Cancer** (♋), one suffers shipwreck; in **Gemini** (♊), one suffers from thieves or in the faculties of the soul; in **Taurus** (♉), there are earthquakes or loss of cattle; in **Aries** (♈), there is damage to crops due to drought, and there will be madness among animals. The same applies to the others, as seen in books 2 and 4.

4 Consider in a similar way in all things and business dealings the lords of **progressions and directions** <note>astrological techniques for predicting timing</note>, not only the life-givers: and see how they stand regarding good or evil: and thus begin or cease. All craftsmen, sailors, farmers, doctors, and smiths do this very thing. Why then should the astrologer not do so in both public and private causes?

5 Furthermore, he who commits his work to God rules the stars; he who follows his senses and emotions serves the stars; but he who uses rational judgment, as we teach in this work, makes use of the stars.

<meta>Continuing from the previous page, which detailed Right Ascensions, this page shifts to Tycho Brahe’s calculations for Declination. While Right Ascension measures "celestial longitude," Declination measures "celestial latitude"—the distance a point is north or south of the celestial equator.</meta>

# Tycho’s Table of Declinations, Northern <unclear>in figures</unclear>
# [for Northern signs]; Southern [for Southern signs].

<note>original: "Tabula declinationum Tychonica." This table shows the "Declination" of the sun or a planet as it moves through the zodiac. Declination is the angular distance north or south of the celestial equator. Tycho Brahe (1546–1601) was a Danish astronomer whose precise measurements were the most accurate in the world before the invention of the telescope.</note>

<note>Historical Note: To read the table for the signs listed at the bottom (Pisces, Virgo, Aquarius, Leo, Capricorn, and Cancer), one would read from the bottom row upward, using the degree markers on the far right. For example, 0 degrees of Cancer (the summer solstice) has a declination of 23 degrees, 31 minutes, and 30 seconds—the value Tycho determined for the "obliquity of the ecliptic," or the tilt of the Earth.</note>
